## 工作原理

```
词元工坊出站请求（模型调用 / web 抓取 / 子进程 curl…）
        │  HTTP(S)_PROXY 指向本地分流代理
        ▼
┌─ 分流代理 127.0.0.1:18118（插件内置）────────────────┐
│  目标域名 → 解析 IPv4                                 │
│  ① 命中 USTC 网段（11 段，内置） ──→ iWAN SOCKS5:1080 │
│  ② 域名后缀命中 ustc.edu.cn 等   ──→ iWAN SOCKS5:1080 │
│  ③ fake-ip（TUN 接管 DNS）按 ② 兜底判断              │
│  ④ 其余目标 ──→ 用户原有代理（如 Clash 7890）或直连   │
│  ※ iWAN 出口连不上时自动回退直连，不掉线              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

插件在宿主进程内做三件事：

1. 启动本地分流代理，按「网段命中 / 域名后缀命中」决定出口；
2. 通过宿主自带的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-http-proxy` 把 `HTTP(S)_PROXY` 指向分流代理
   （卸载时整体恢复原状）；
3. 可选：托管 `iwan-client-oidc --connect --socks` 进程。

转发给 iWAN 的是**域名**（由 iWAN 在校内解析），因此不依赖本机 DNS；
遇到 Clash TUN 的 fake-ip 时自动改用域名后缀判断。

## 内置网段

```text
114.214.160.0/19  114.214.192.0/18  202.38.64.0/19   210.45.64.0/20
210.45.112.0/20   211.86.144.0/20   222.195.64.0/19   210.72.22.0/24
202.141.160.0/19  218.22.21.0/27    218.104.71.160/28
```

域名后缀默认：`ustc.edu.cn`、`ustclug.org`、`ustc.life`（均可在设置卡片中修改）。

## 安装

词元工坊的插件页支持 **GitHub 仓库地址 / npm 包名 / 本地目录路径** 三种来源，
任选一种粘贴进「插件 → 安装」即可。安装完成后**完全退出并重启应用**，
再打开 设置 → USTC IWAN。

### 方式一：GitHub 仓库地址（推荐）

在「插件 → 安装」中输入仓库地址：

```text
https://github.com/cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan
```

以下写法等价，任选其一：

| 写法 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `https://github.com/cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan` | 仓库 URL（推荐） |
| `github:cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan` | GitHub 简写 |
| `git+https://github.com/cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan.git` | 显式 git 地址 |
| `https://github.com/cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan#v0.1.0` | 固定到某个 tag / 分支 / 提交 |
| `github:cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan#<40 位提交号>` | 固定到具体提交（可被插件页更新检查追踪） |

> 通过 Git 安装时，插件以**副本**形式装进 profile 的 `node_modules`。要升级，
> 在插件页对它执行**检查更新 / 更新**，或改为固定提交后重新安装。
> 首次安装需要宿主能访问 GitHub。

### 方式二：npm 包名

```text
dsh-ustc-iwan
```

> ⚠️ 该包**目前尚未发布到 npm**，此方式暂不可用，请先用方式一或方式三。
> 若你自行 fork 并发布，把这里换成你的包名即可。

### 方式三：本地目录路径

```bash
git clone https://github.com/cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan.git
```

在「插件 → 安装」中填入**绝对路径**（也支持 `file:` / `link:` 前缀）：

```text
C:\Users\<你>\dsh-ustc-iwan
file:C:\Users\<你>\dsh-ustc-iwan
```

或直接下 `Release` 里的 `dsh-ustc-iwan-0.1.0.zip` 解压，再按同样方式填入解压目录。

> **本地路径必须以绝对路径给出**（相对路径会被插件管理器拒绝）。
> 以 `link:` 链接方式安装时不会执行依赖安装，因此本项目**刻意保持零第三方依赖**，
> 链接安装同样可用；这种方式改代码后重启应用即生效。

### 方式四：直接写进 profile（CLI / 进阶）

```bash
# 把 <DSH_HOME> 换成你的数据目录：
#   Windows 桌面端：%APPDATA%\tokenworks-desktop-harness
#   CLI 默认：~/.dsh
cd <DSH_HOME>/profiles/<profile>
pnpm add github:cloudbywu/dsh-ustc-iwan     # 或 link:<本仓库绝对路径>
```

并把 `dsh-ustc-iwan` 加入该 profile `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`。

### 安装后

1. **完全退出并重启词元工坊**（客户端 bundle 在启动时组合，仅刷新页面可能不够）；
2. 打开 **设置 → USTC IWAN**，确认「分流代理」指示灯为绿色；
3. 按 [首次使用](#首次使用) 下载 iWAN 客户端并完成一次认证。

## 首次使用

1. 打开 **设置 → USTC iWAN**；
2. 点 **下载 iwan-client-oidc**（自动存到 `<DSH_HOME>/cache/ustc-iwan/`，
   不做系统级安装；也可自行下载后填入「客户端路径」）；
3. 完成一次统一身份认证（终端执行，只需一次）：

   ```bat
   iwan-client-oidc-windows-x86_64.exe --fetch
   ```

   按提示在浏览器完成认证，把 `com.panabit.mobile://...` 回调 URL 粘贴回终端。
   线路配置保存在 `~/.config/iwan/servers.json`。

4. 回到卡片点 **启动 iWAN**（或在配置里开启「托管 iWAN 客户端」）；
5. 用 **测试分流** 输入 `llm.ustc.edu.cn`，显示「走 iWAN」即成功。

## 设置卡片

安装后 **设置 → USTC iWAN** 出现一张卡片，分四组：

| 分组 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 运行状态 | 分流代理 / 出站策略 / iWAN SOCKS5 / 托管进程 四个指示灯；启动 iWAN、停止托管、刷新状态、**分流测试** |
| iWAN 客户端 | **一键下载 iwan-client-oidc**（进度条、sha256 记录、失败自动清理） |
| 配置 | 全部配置项表单化，保存即时生效（改端口自动重启代理；开托管自动连接） |
| 最近日志 | 最近 40 条运行日志 |

宿主侧对应路由：`/ustc-iwan/api/{status,settings,download,connect,disconnect,test}`。

## 配置项

配置持久化在 `<DSH_HOME>/storages/ustc-iwan-settings.json`（原子写）。
环境变量优先级最高：

| 环境变量 | 对应配置 |
| --- | --- |
| `USTC_IWAN_CLIENT_PATH` | `iwanClientPath` |
| `USTC_IWAN_SERVER` | `iwanServer` |
| `USTC_IWAN_UPSTREAM_PROXY` | `upstreamProxy` |
| `USTC_IWAN_SOCKS_PORT` | `iwanSocksPort` |
| `USTC_IWAN_DNS` | `dnsServer` |
| `USTC_IWAN_DISABLED=1` | 完全停用本插件 |

| 字段 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | 关闭后插件完全不介入（策略恢复原状） |
| `listenPort` | `18118` | 本地分流代理端口 |
| `iwanSocksHost` / `iwanSocksPort` | `127.0.0.1` / `1080` | iWAN SOCKS5 地址 |
| `manageClient` | `false` | 是否由插件代启 iWAN |
| `iwanClientPath` | 空 | 托管模式下 exe 路径；留空用已下载副本 |
| `iwanServer` | 空 | 线路名或序号（传给 `--server`） |
| `upstreamProxy` | 自动 | 非 USTC 流量的上游 HTTP 代理；留空自动沿用启动环境里的 `HTTP(S)_PROXY`，再无则直连 |
| `cidrs` | 上表 11 段 | USTC 网段（逗号分隔） |
| `domainSuffixes` | `ustc.edu.cn,ustclug.org,ustc.life` | 域名后缀兜底 |
| `dnsServer` | 系统 | 分流解析用 DNS；TUN fake-ip 环境建议 `223.5.5.5` |
| `verbose` | `false` | 逐请求日志 |

## 与代理软件共存

- **Clash TUN 开着也能用**：分流在应用进程内完成；Clash 接管 DNS 出现 fake-ip 时，
  插件改用域名后缀兜底，且转发给 iWAN 的是域名（由 iWAN 在校内解析）。
  建议在 Clash 配置里把 iWAN 服务器地址与上述 USTC 网段设为 `DIRECT` 更稳。
- **iWAN 隧道不被抢走**：ustc-iwan 客户端本身把隧道 UDP 绑定到物理网卡
  （排除 VPN/TUN 虚拟网卡）。
- **WireGuard / Panabit iWAN**：它们接管系统路由不影响应用层分流，插件不与之争抢
  任何系统资源。
- **iWAN 掉线**：USTC 请求自动回退直连（校内场景仍可用），并在日志中提示。

## 排错

| 现象 | 处理 |
| --- | --- |
| 设置里没有「USTC IWAN」卡片 | 完全退出应用后重启（客户端 bundle 需重建）；仍无则按 F12 看控制台报错 |
| `端口 1080 上没有…且未配置 iwanClientPath` | 先手动启动 iWAN，或填写「客户端路径」 |
| iWAN 客户端一启动就退出 | 先在终端单独跑 `--connect --socks` 看输出；多为线路选择或认证过期，重跑 `--fetch` |
| USTC 请求走了直连且校外不可达 | 确认 iWAN SOCKS 端口存活；看日志是否提示 fake-ip，必要时设 DNS 为 `223.5.5.5` |
| 下载失败 | 走 GitHub Releases，网络不畅时手动下载并填入「客户端路径」 |

## 已知边界

- 网段决策只覆盖 IPv4；IPv6 字面量或仅有 AAAA 记录时按域名后缀兜底。
- 浏览器渲染层自身发出的请求不经宿主网络栈，不在分流范围内；分流目标是
  **应用出站请求**（模型调用、web 抓取、子进程等）。
- 自动化测试覆盖：CIDR 边界、SOCKS5 握手、分流决策、设置热应用与策略恢复。

## 开发

```
lib/index.js          Host 入口（运行时 + 路由挂载）
lib/runtime.js        运行时状态机（设置、分流代理、策略、托管）
lib/routes.js         /ustc-iwan/api/* 路由
lib/split-proxy.js    本地分流代理（CONNECT + 明文 HTTP）
lib/socks.js          极简 SOCKS5 CONNECT 客户端
lib/cidr.js           USTC 网段匹配 + fake-ip 识别
lib/resolver.js       带缓存 DNS 解析
lib/iwan-client.js    iWAN 客户端探测/托管
lib/binary.js         iWAN 客户端下载
lib/policy.js         出站策略安装/恢复
lib/settings-store.js 设置持久化
lib/client.js         浏览器半边（设置卡片）
```

修改 `lib/client.js` 后需**重启应用**，浏览器才会拉到新的客户端 bundle。

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE)。ustc-iwan 客户端由 [yyy1mu/ustc-iwan](https://github.com/yyy1mu/ustc-iwan)
提供，本项目仅在运行时调用它，不重新分发其二进制。

Native settings/routes download and spawn iwan; lib/binary.js uses a latest-release download URL. The fixed source does not pin that binary identity, and credential/connect handlers registered through connection.fetch do not establish an owner-only policy in the captured chain. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Runaway Watchdog · Spend Circuit Breaker

A Harness-level safety plugin for DeepSeek Harness that **detects runaway agent
behavior and deterministically stops it** — before it burns your token budget.

Unlike advisory "you seem to be looping" reminders, the watchdog **enforces**:
a synchronous tool guard blocks the offending call, and a spend/error circuit
breaker pauses tool execution until the situation is resolved.

## What it detects

| Rule | Signal | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `repeat` | N consecutive identical tool calls (name + canonical arguments) | advisory → hard block |
| `error-rate` | error fraction over the recent tool-result window | open circuit |
| `token-velocity` | newly-generated **output** tokens / minute over a sliding window (excludes context re-send input/cache, avoiding long-conversation false positives) | open circuit |
| `spend-velocity` | categorized CNY / minute (per-model input/output/cache-read/cache-write rates) | open circuit |
| `depth` | subagent delegation depth ≥ `maxDepth` | block spawn |
| `fanout` | live children per parent ≥ `maxFanout` | block spawn |

Detection is a **pure incremental fold** of committed session events
(`tool/call`, `tool/result`, `assistant/message`, `user/message`), driven by the
global `session/event` feed and maintained per live session. The fold core is a
pure function (unit-tested in isolation); no new session event type is ever
appended and no deprecated synchronous session-log reader is used. Delegation
depth is read from the durable `SessionHeader.delegationDepth`.

## Categorized per-model pricing (CNY)

Spend is not a blended "one price × total tokens" guess; it is computed **per model
and per usage bucket**:

- **Model identity** comes from each `assistant/message` event's
  `message.source.{provider, model}` — the exact route that produced the message —
  so the watchdog knows which provider/model every call used, no matter how many
  you have configured.
- **Disjoint usage buckets**: model-reported `usage` carries `inputTokens`
  (cache-miss input), `outputTokens` (output, already includes reasoning),
  `cacheReadTokens` (cache hit), `cacheWriteTokens` (cache write). Each is priced
  once at its own rate; nothing is double-counted.
- **Price matching** priority: `model id → provider/model → wildcard (deepseek-*) → *`.
  Source tiers: `user` (your panel overrides) > `builtin` (DeepSeek reference rates)
  > `fallback` (`*`).
- **Real-time effect**: the fold stores only **raw buckets + model name**; cost is
  derived on read against the **current** price table. Saving a price in the panel
  writes `prices.json` and updates memory, so the very next status/fold uses the new
  rate — **no restart**.
- **Currency**: CNY (¥ per million tokens) by default; set `currency: USD` to display
  via the `usdToCny` rate.

> Built-ins (CNY per million tokens, `input / cache-read / cache-write / output`):
> **deepseek-flash 2 / 0.04 / 0 / 8** and **deepseek-v4-pro 9 / 0.30 / 0 / 27** are
> the published **peak-hour** rates (off-peak is half; DeepSeek does not bill cache
> writes separately). Peak is the deliberate default for a spend guard —
> over-reporting trips early, under-reporting would let spend run past the circuit.
> `deepseek-chat` / `deepseek-reasoner` stay as legacy references and `*` is a
> generic fallback. Prices change: verify the official page and override in the
> panel (a per-model row always beats a built-in). Spend and "estimated saved" are
> **estimates** (usage × rate); enforcement decisions rely only on exact counts,
> never on estimates.

The dashboard adds a **Model pricing** panel (detected-model chips with source
badges, an editable per-model rate table, add/delete, and a Save button that applies
live), a top **Est. saved (¥)** card beside Est. tokens prevented, per-session
**Model** / **Total cost** columns, and ¥ amounts in the audit ledger.

## How enforcement works

- **Synchronous tool guard** (`ctx.tools.guard`) reads the folded state and denies
  the N+1th identical failing call, blocks spawns over budget, and blocks every
  tool while a circuit is open. The guard never blocks the watchdog's own tools,
  so you can always inspect status and reset.
- **Global listener** ranks breaches, trips circuits (with a cooldown), and writes
  a durable audit entry per episode (deduplicated **per rule and severity**, so two
  co-firing rules cannot re-audit each other).
- **Advisory context** is attached at the warn threshold and again at the block
  threshold — never on every call, so a loop does not inflate its own context.
- **A denial is not a tool error.** The guard records the call ids it denied; the
  fold keeps those results out of the error-rate window entirely (no observed tool
  outcome). Without this a single identical-call loop would inflate the error rate
  and escalate itself into a full circuit, making the dashboard's 100% error rate a
  measurement of the watchdog rather than of the tools.
- A **repeat block clears only on a different call or a human interjection** —
  resetting does not un-block an ongoing identical loop (that would defeat the
  purpose). `watchdog_reset` closes a tripped spend/error circuit.

### Monitor mode semantics

`mode: 'monitor'` detects and records, and never blocks:

| What the fold finds | `enforce` | `monitor` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| repeat / error spike over the block threshold | guard denies; audit `blocked` | audit `advised` (severity stays `block`) |
| a velocity / error-rate circuit condition | circuit opens (cooldown), audit `circuit-opened` | **no circuit is armed**; audit `would-trip` |
| advisory crossing | injected at warn + block | same |

A circuit is never *armed* in monitor mode: a dashboard showing "circuit OPEN" in a
mode that cannot block would be a lie, so the observation is recorded as
`would-trip` and `would-trip` is not counted as an intervention.

## Architecture

```
lib/detection.js   pure fold + breach ranking + guard decision + categorized cost (no deps)
lib/pricing.js     pure pricing: table matching + source resolution + four-bucket cost (no deps)
lib/config.js      defaults + fail-loud normalization (no deps)
lib/ledger.js      durable audit ledger over a table interface (no deps)
lib/file-domain.js atomic JSON-file table backing the ledger (Node builtins)
lib/tree.js        pure depth / fan-out decisions (no deps)
lib/tool-schema.js minimal JSON-Schema compiler to register tools (no deps)
index.js           incremental detector + guard + listener + 5 tools + routes + service
client.js          dashboard (sidebar entry + main page), theme tokens only
```

**Zero external package imports** — only Node builtins and the plugin's own pure
lib modules. This deliberately avoids the bare-package resolution limits of a
profile-local plain-JS bundle (`zod` / `schemastery` / `dsh-tools` are not
reliably resolvable there). Host services used: `tools`, `connection`,
`profileContext`, and optionally `agents`. Global data reaches the dashboard via
authenticated `connection.fetch` routes (`/api/runaway-watchdog/*`).

## Tools

- `watchdog_status` — live counters, circuit state, and aggregate stats.
- `watchdog_audit` — read the audit ledger (filter by session / rule).
- `watchdog_reset` — close a tripped circuit for the calling session.
- `watchdog_selftest` — run the in-process scientific self-test (see below).
- `watchdog_test_fail` — *(only when `enableTestTools: true`)* a deterministic
  failing tool used to drive a real loop and prove the block fires.

## Configuration

Every field is optional; see `lib/config.js` `DEFAULTS`. Key options:

- `mode`: `enforce` (default) or `monitor` (detect + audit + advise, no blocking).
- `repeatWarnThreshold` (3), `repeatBlockThreshold` (5), `blockSuccessRepeats` (false).
- `errorWindow` (12), `errorMinSamples` (6), `errorRateThreshold` (0.8).
- `velocityWindowMs` (60000), `tokenVelocityLimit` (200000), `spendVelocityLimit` (30,
  in `currency`/min), `circuitCooldownMs` (60000).
- `currency` (`CNY`), `usdToCny` (7.2), `pricing` (per-model rate overrides merged over
  built-ins; also editable live in the dashboard, persisted to `prices.json`).
- `maxDepth` (8), `maxFanout` (16).
- `include` / `exclude` tool-name wildcards; `enableTestTools` (false); `auditRetention` (2000).

Invalid config throws at load (never a silent fallback).

## Scientific verification

Five independent layers, all reproducible (see `TEST_REPORT.md` and `AUDIT.md`):

1. **Unit + integration tests** (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`, **148 cases, all
   passing**): table-driven coverage of every rule, threshold boundary, window
   edge, chain reset, retention eviction, durable rebuild, config validation, the
   input/cache-tokens-do-not-inflate-velocity regression, **self-denials do not
   count as tool errors**, **monitor-mode auditing + would-trip**, **prices-route
   rejection without data loss**, **bounded advisory injection**, **session-log
   repair that preserves the event envelope**, and **client render / locale smoke
   tests**; plus integration tests that drive the *real* `apply()` against a
   faithful mock context.
2. **In-process self-test** (`watchdog_selftest` tool or `GET /api/runaway-watchdog/selftest`):
   exercises the *real* detector, guard registration, detection core, categorized
   pricing (model identity + four-bucket cost + live override), and a durable audit
   write/read round-trip against the live services; returns a pass/fail report
   (live: 11/11).
3. **Real-host end-to-end regression** (`node tests/e2e/real-host.e2e.mjs`,
   **28 assertions, all passing**): boots the *production* DSH spine — real cordis,
   the real `mountAgentLoopTestDependencies` services, the production `AgentLoop`,
   the real `ToolRuntime` guard layer, real committed session events — with a
   scripted model (no network). Proves blocking, folding, auditing, circuits,
   metering, depth budget, route behaviour and the self-test *in the real runtime*,
   not against a mock event bus.
4. **End-to-end behavioral test**: with `enableTestTools: true`, call
   `watchdog_test_fail` repeatedly with identical arguments. The first
   `repeatBlockThreshold` calls fail normally; the next call is **blocked by the
   guard** with a "Runaway Watchdog blocked repeated call" reason, and a `blocked`
   audit entry appears in the dashboard.
5. **Live host end-to-end + user on-site review**: every feature confirmed inside
   the real desktop host (see `TEST_REPORT.md` §8 expected↔actual table).

## Troubleshooting

**Symptom**: every turn fails with
`Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: messages[n]: missing field 'role'`
and `INVALID_REQUEST`, retrying never helps.

**Cause (1.1.0 and earlier)**: the repeat advisory was handed to the host as
`{source, content}`; the host appends that verbatim as a `user/message` event and
replays it straight into the provider request, where the absent `role` key makes
the whole body invalid. 1.1.1 fixes the producer (`id` + `role: 'user'`) — restart
the host to load it. Sessions that were already poisoned are repaired with:

```pwsh
node tools/repair-role-less-context.mjs           # report only
node tools/repair-role-less-context.mjs --apply   # rewrite (backup, only affected frames)
```

## Known boundaries

- **The fold is in-memory.** `states`/`live` are rebuilt from `session/event` as
  events commit; a host restart mid-loop starts a fresh chain. Persisted session
  history feeds the fold only through the events that replay through that feed —
  the watchdog deliberately does not append events or read the session log directly.
- **Per-session tracking is bounded** (256 sessions) and idle sessions are evicted
  oldest-first; the live roster is never evicted. `GET /status` reports
  `tracked: {sessions, live, cap}`.
- **Fan-out counts in-process children only** (`agents.list()`), so subagents
  driven by ACP / remote / CLI subprocess drivers are invisible to the `fanout`
  budget. `depth` is unaffected — it reads the durable `SessionHeader.delegationDepth`.
- **Panel copy follows the host locale service** (`ctx.locale` snapshot), like
  shipping panels. `locale/*.json` are package-catalog metadata (title/description),
  not UI strings.

## Deployment

- After install, **restart the host once** to load the code (HMR ignores
  `node_modules`); **refresh the GUI window once** (Ctrl+R / F5) to load the client
  panel.
- All host registrations are wrapped in `ctx.effect`, `apply()` is synchronous, and
  the guard returns `string` (deny) / `undefined` (allow) — the key to registrations
  landing in the global layer (see `TEST_REPORT.md` §4, §7).

## Safety notes

- The watchdog only ever *denies* tool calls; it never executes anything itself.
- Audit data is plugin-owned, stored in its own atomic JSON document
  (`<profile>/runaway-watchdog/audit.json`), and disposable (a corrupt file is
  rebuilt fresh, never bricking the plugin).
- `watchdog_test_fail` is a harmless diagnostic; set `enableTestTools: false` to
  hide it from the model in production.

# DeepSeek Harness Usage Center

[中文安装与使用说明](INSTALL.zh.md) · [Download 1.1.0](https://github.com/Codenestra/deepseek-harness-plugins/releases/tag/dsh-usage-center-v1.1.0)

An independent DeepSeek Harness plugin for exact, provider-reported LLM usage. It uses public Cordis, LLM waterfall, Session Query, Connection Fetch, and Client Slots extension points and does not modify Harness source.

It reports uncached input, output, cache-read, cache-write, total, and provider-reported reasoning tokens; distinct cache-token and request-hit rates; calls, retries, reliable terminal states; exact live timing; field coverage; cold-session backfill; fork-prefix deduplication; and CSV/JSON export. Every chart exposes exact hover/focus details, local-time daily buckets, and separate filters for working directories, Harness sidebar groups (including Ungrouped), and archived sessions.

Since 1.1.0 the panel also carries:

- **Cost in CNY** priced from a configurable table (same built-ins as the runaway watchdog), with per-bucket detail in the charts, the table, and the exports.
- **Budget and forecast**: daily/monthly bars plus a month-end projection from the last seven days.
- **Chart interaction**: hover tooltips with share and day-over-day delta, keyboard stepping, legend toggling, drag-to-zoom with double-click reset, cumulative mode, an overlay of the previous equal-length window, and click-to-drill into a day or a model.
- **Motion**: line draw, area fade, bar growth, point scale, number count-up, and tooltip fade — all disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **A server-paged detail table** (sort, search, column visibility, click a session id to filter by it, copy `call_key`) instead of a 500-row cut, plus PNG, Markdown, and shareable-link exports, range/refresh shortcuts, and a hidden data table behind every chart for screen readers.
- **Conditional polling**: the query route answers `304` on an unchanged payload, and polling pauses while the panel is hidden.

Calls with no usable provider-reported token data are skipped and never estimated. Valid partial usage is retained with absent fields left unknown; malformed or contradictory samples are skipped without affecting other calls.

Missing optional fields remain unknown. No character- or context-based estimation is performed. A final durable usage sample overrides the same attempt's stream sample, while every settled retry remains a separate call.

See [README.zh.md](./README.zh.md) for the complete metric contract, installation, storage, pricing/budget configuration, and API documentation.

npm run check
npm pack
```

Codenestra 维护的 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件仓库**，提供插件源码、安装包与中文使用说明。

## 插件与下载

| 插件 | 版本 | 功能 | 下载 | 使用说明 |

| [回合级性能剖析器](plugins/dsh-turn-profiler) | 0.1.0 | 时延瀑布图、实时指标、token 与缓存诊断、JSON 导出 | [ZIP](https://github.com/Codenestra/deepseek-harness-plugins/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-turn-profiler-0.1.0.zip) | [说明](plugins/dsh-turn-profiler/INSTALL.zh.md) |

## 安装

1. 下载对应插件的 ZIP 并解压，得到 `.tgz` 安装包和 `.md` 中文安装使用说明。
2. 使用 DSH 插件管理器安装 `.tgz`，按说明启用插件。
3. 从 DSH 侧栏进入插件面板。配置方法与日常操作见上表中的使用说明。

[Releases](https://github.com/Codenestra/deepseek-harness-plugins/releases) 中也提供独立 `.tgz` 文件与 SHA-256 校验文件。

  dsh-runaway-watchdog/
  dsh-usage-center/
```

每个目录是独立的 DSH bundle，包含 `package.json`、`cordis.patch.yml`、host/client JavaScript 源码、语言文件、图标与说明。

Plugins for DeepSeek Harness: **Project Hub**, **Storage Doctor**, **Turn Profiler**, **Runaway Watchdog**, and **Usage Center**. Download installable `.tgz` bundles or ZIPs with Chinese installation guides from [Releases](https://github.com/Codenestra/deepseek-harness-plugins/releases). # CC Sessions Hub

Claude Code 会话工作台，跑在 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）桌面端**里：在同一个界面中浏览本机 CC 会话、继续对话、审批工具调用、调用 skills、预览文件、查看子代理过程。

> 非官方社区插件，与 DeepSeek、Anthropic 均无隶属关系。

## 功能

- **会话列表**：在线/历史、搜索、归档、摘要、fork、后台任务、终端接管。
- **面板内对话**：打开历史会话直接续聊；发送/停止；SSE 增量（长回答逐字）；加载更早。
- **审批**：允许 / 始终允许（显示写入目标）/ 拒绝；并发审批分卡处理；AskUserQuestion 选择卡（选项、多选、自由输入）。
- **会话设置**：权限模式（默认/计划/自动/接受编辑/不询问）、effort（跟随设置 → max）、思考显示开关；默认 **auto + xhigh + 思考显示关**。
- **命令与 skills**：输入 `/` 或点「命令」出列表，skills 可直接调用；终端专属命令自动过滤。
- **文件预览**：Markdown（含表格）、HTML（sandbox 禁脚本）、PDF、Word/ODT（本机 LibreOffice 转 PDF）、图片、文本。
- **子代理过程**：会话行、对话标题栏都有「子代理（N）」入口，点开直接看，不必先进对话；Task/Agent 卡上也可展开单条。运行中每 1.2s 刷新。
- **完整工具输出**：截断的结果可一键读取转录里的完整内容。

## 环境要求

| 依赖 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **DSH 桌面端** | 在 `0.2.2-rc.2` 上测试（开发期亦覆盖 rc.1）；插件使用其客户端私有服务（layout / sidebar / slots 等），**DSH 升级可能失效** |
| **Claude Code CLI** | 已在本机 `2.1.323` 上测试；需要已登录，`claude` 在 PATH 或 `CLAUDE_CODE_BIN` |
| **Node.js** | ≥ 22（插件与 SDK 运行在 DSH 主进程） |
| **macOS** | 文件「打开 / Finder」与 LibreOffice 路径按 macOS 实现；Windows/Linux 需自行适配 |
| **LibreOffice**（可选） | Word/ODT 预览需要；未装时提示"用系统应用打开" |

## 安装

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Covertaker/dsh-cc-sessions-hub.git
cd dsh-cc-sessions-hub
npm install

# 装进 desktop profile（会创建 link 依赖；多数版本同时把包加入 bundle 列表）
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:$PWD
```

确认 `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里有 `dsh-cc-sessions-hub`；没有则手动加入。**完全退出并重启 DSH**。

安装后，DSH 侧栏出现「CC Sessions Hub」入口。

## 使用

1. 打开侧栏「CC Sessions Hub」。
2. 点会话标题或「对话」进入对话；历史会话直接输入即 resume。
3. 右上「设置」改权限模式 / effort / 思考显示；默认 auto + xhigh + 思考关。
4. 终端里正在跑的会话显示**只读**，点「fork 到面板」才能继续（cc 无文件锁，避免双写分叉）。
5. 「预览文件」可输入绝对路径直接打开；工具卡里的路径也可点「预览」。
6. 会话行或对话标题栏点「子代理（N）」看整个会话的子代理；Task/Agent 卡上可直接展开单条。

## 配置

| 变量 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `CC_HUB_CHAT=0` | 关闭对话功能，只保留列表/摘要/终端接管（回滚开关） |
| `CC_HUB_WINDOW=60` | 调小单次渲染窗口（默认 250），用于测试分页 |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_BIN` | 指定 `claude` 可执行文件路径 |

## 安全模型

- 插件在**本机 loopback** 上注册 HTTP 路由；每次启动生成随机 token，`/chat/token` 只对同源可读，除 token 与图片原始流外所有请求校验 `x-cc-hub-token`。
- **文件预览可读任意绝对路径**；「打开」会调用系统默认应用（`open`），「Finder」会 `open -R`。仅在本机可信环境使用。
- 插件**不含遥测**，不会把会话内容发往任何地方（除了 Claude Code 自身的模型/API 请求）。
- 面板会话与终端会话使用同一份 `~/.claude` 配置、hooks 与转录；权限行为与终端一致。

## 已知限制

- DSH 私有客户端服务可能随版本升级变化；升级后请先打开面板验证。
- 仅 macOS 验证；文件打开/Word 预览路径为 macOS。
- 历史默认渲染最近 250 条，更多用「加载更早」。
- 工具输出在传输中截断（结果 2500 字、输入 1200 字）；完整内容按需读取。
- **短回答可能直接出结果**：单分片回答的 partial 窗口只有几毫秒，SSE 也可能看不到逐字；长回答可见。
- 终端专属命令（`/status`、`/context`、`/cost` 等）不可用；skills 可用。
- 无模型选择器（模型跟随 CC settings）；无终端快捷键（Esc/Ctrl+C 等），只有「停止」按钮。
- 子代理过程只展开一层；运行中轮询 1.2s。
- 面板会话空闲 30 分钟后回收；下次发送会 resume。

## 开发与测试

```bash
node scripts/smoke-chat.mjs          # 离线：解析/路由/token/审批/预览/SSE/问题卡
node scripts/smoke-chat.mjs --live   # 联网：再加一轮真实模型调用
```

结构：

```
index.js            列表/摘要/fork 路由与 cc_* 工具
host/engine.js      Agent SDK 运行时：常驻进程、流式、审批、中断、回收
host/history.js     JSONL 转录 → 渲染项（含子代理）
host/files.js       文件预览与系统打开
host/routes.js      /_ccpanel/* 路由（Node handler，支持 POST/SSE）
client.js           DSH 主面板 UI（列表 + 对话 + 预览 + 子代理抽屉）
```

运行时用 `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` 驱动**本机已装的 `claude`**（`pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`），因此 `~/.claude/settings.json` 的模型、hooks、权限规则全部照常生效；SDK 只负责协议。

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# DSH 模型指纹监控

在 DSH 里观察每个模型路由的**协议形状**和**行为特征**，回答：

- 这个声称模型，和它过去的表现一致吗？
- 同一个名称后面有没有换过协议、adapter 或网关？
- 两个不同路由是不是行为相近？
- 某个第三方模型与官方基线的行为相似度是多少？
- 最近的行为是否出现了持续漂移？

> 指纹是证据，不是模型身份证明。黑盒 API 无法被“证明”为某个具体模型；请结合账单、接口文档、人工抽检和人工标签使用。

---

## 快速开始

### 方式 A：从 npm 安装

包发布后：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-model-fingerprint
```

如果 `dsh` 不在 PATH，请使用 DSH 安装目录里的 CLI。

### 方式 B：从本地目录安装

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/Darkhe55/dsh-plugin-models-fingerprint.git
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "C:\path\to\dsh-plugin-models-fingerprint"
```

也可以使用 DSH 的 **Plugins → Add plugin**，或 `plugin_manager install_bundle`，目标指向这个目录。

### 方式 C：开发调试

```powershell
npm install
npm run build
npm test
npm run check
```

然后按方式 B 安装本地目录。

安装或更新后：

1. 完全退出并重开 DSH；
2. 刷新 Web 页面；
3. 插件会出现在输入框上方的 dock。

---

## 30 秒上手

1. 打开输入框上方的 **在会话消息旁显示指纹情况**；
2. 左侧会出现每轮对话的卡片；
3. 点击卡片，或点击 dock 的 **面板**；
4. 在面板里查看逐轮检测、指纹族、模型等价性和官方相似度；
5. 需要官方基线时，到 **官方相似度** 页配置 provider/model。

开关打开或关闭时，会触发一次历史补算并存盘。

---

## 界面说明

### 输入框上方 dock

- **在会话消息旁显示指纹情况**：控制左侧逐轮卡片，不打开面板；
- **面板**：打开完整逐轮检测浮层。

### 左侧逐轮卡片

每轮一张卡片，显示：

```text
第 N 轮
FP-xxxx
一致 / 变化 / 多指纹 / 代际 / 基线
主要声称模型
```

- 中间卡片跟随消息的可见区域；
- 顶部/底部卡片使用固定槽位；
- 窄窗口退化为紧凑标记；
- 点击卡片打开面板。

### 面板页签

| 页签 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| 逐轮检测 | 每轮指纹、协议、行为变化和步骤明细 |
| 指纹族 | 每个协议指纹的样本、名称、标签 |
| 模型等价性 | 不同路由的行为距离和同名模型对比 |
| 官方相似度 | 第三方路由与官方基线的行为相似度 |
| 声称模型 | 一个名称下出现过哪些指纹 |
| 历史会话 | 每个会话的模型、指纹和样本数 |
| 方法与边界 | 能推断什么、不能推断什么 |

---

## 官方相似度

用于回答：

> 这个第三方路由的输出行为，与指定官方模型的行为基线有多接近？

### 配置官方基线

打开 **官方相似度**：

1. 填写官方 `provider`；
2. 填写官方 `model`；
3. 可选标签和最少样本数；
4. 点击 **保存官方基线**。

基线需要足够历史样本才会进入 `ready`。每个官方 API 应建立自己的基线，不要把两个网关当成同一个基线。

### 读取结果

面板显示：

- **行为相似度**；
- 是否已校准；
- 判定：`likely-same-behavior` / `ambiguous` / `likely-different-behavior`；
- 距离；
- 质量代理：`stable` / `watch` / `degrading` / `insufficient`；
- AUC、分离度、正负样本数；
- 主要特征贡献。

解释：

- 高分只表示**行为分布更接近官方基线**；
- 低分表示行为分布不同，不等于模型被替换；
- 未校准时只显示分数，不显示可比较的百分比；
- 内容特征（CJK、Markdown、换行等）权重很低，避免把任务差异误判成模型差异；
- 质量代理不是语义质量评分。

---

## 自动补算与存盘

插件会从 DSH 会话日志补回状态中缺失的轮次观测。

触发时机：

- DSH 启动并完成初次扫描后；
- 打开或关闭左侧指纹开关时；
- 手动调用 API 或工具时。

补算流程：

```text
发现会话文件
→ 重新解析当前文件
→ 去重后补回缺失观测
→ 更新 Turn Index
→ 写入 state.json.zst
```

手动触发：

```text
POST /model-fingerprint/api/backfill
```

需要 token；也可以通过模型工具：

```text
model_fingerprint action=backfill
```

已删除的日志文件无法从磁盘补回；状态中已有的历史观测会保留。

---

## 固定探针（可选，会产生 token）

被动历史会受任务结构影响。需要更强证据时，在 **模型等价性** 页底部运行固定探针。

- 6 个固定 prompt：baseline、英文、中文、代码、emoji、工具调用；
- 可选重复 1–3 次；
- 每次输出 token 很小；
- 运行前需要确认；
- 探针会真实调用供应商模型，产生费用；
- 固定探针结果优先于跨任务被动历史。

---

## 模型工具

工具名：`model_fingerprint`

| action | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `status` | 最近响应、统计、证据提示 |
| `session` | 指定会话的指纹摘要 |
| `fingerprints` | 按样本数列出指纹族 |
| `equivalence` | 跨路由行为距离 |
| `probe` | 运行固定探针，必须 `confirm: true`，消耗 token |
| `label` | 写入/删除人工标签 |
| `scan` | 重新发现会话文件 |
| `backfill` | 补算缺失轮次并落盘 |

示例：

```text
帮我看看最近一次实际调用和声称名称是否一致
→ model_fingerprint { action: "status" }

这个会话里出现过哪些指纹？
→ model_fingerprint { action: "session", sessionId: "session-..." }

把缺失的历史轮次补回来
→ model_fingerprint { action: "backfill" }
```

---

## 判定与边界

常见判定：

| 判定 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `consistent` | 指纹与历史一致 |
| `unverified` | 样本太少 |
| `changed` | 同 API/adapter 下响应 ID 形状变化 |
| `generation` | adapter 或 wire API 变化 |
| `mixed` | 同一路由存在多个指纹 |
| `alias` | 同一指纹出现多个名称 |
| `label-mismatch` | 名称与人工标签不一致 |
| `behavior-drift` | 行为指标偏离历史基线 |
| `behavior-change-point` | 时间序列出现持续变化点 |

置信度是证据强度，最高 90%，不是模型身份概率。

---

## 数据与隐私

- 状态文件：`%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\model-fingerprint\state.json.zst`，或 `$DSH_HOME/model-fingerprint/state.json.zst`；
- 只保存协议形状、指标、哈希、会话 ID、时间；
- 不保存提示词或回复正文；
- 固定探针只保存内置 prompt 的结果指标；
- 历史日志只读，不修改 `~/.dsh/sessions`；
- 面板与 API 仅绑定本机 DSH Web 服务；
- 修改状态、运行探针、补算需要 token；
- 重置：停止 DSH 后删除 `model-fingerprint` 目录。

---

## 性能

- 启动后台扫描，按文件大小/修改时间增量处理；
- 追加日志只解析新帧；
- 补算单独串行执行，不并发重扫；
- 客户端窗口上限 2000 轮，卡片 DOM 上限 9；
- 100,000 轮 turn index 分页约 20ms；
- 100,000 条观测构造单会话轮次约 168ms；
- 报告按 scanner 版本、标签和 limit 缓存。

---

## 兼容性

已在：

```text
@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.2-rc.3
Windows Desktop / Web
```

验证：

- Host：`webServer`、`tools`、`sessions`、`llm`；
- Client：`shell.overlay`、`conversation.composer.dock`；
- `ctx.webServer.getOrigin()`；
- 逐轮卡片、官方相似度面板、固定探针、查询 API。

`0.2.2-rc.1` → `0.2.2-rc.3` 的升级指南中与本插件相关的是 macOS overlay 的窗口拖拽区域；Windows/Web 不受影响。

`engines.dsh`：

```text
>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0
```

---

## 发布到 npm

本仓库使用 **tag 触发发布**，普通 `git push` 不会发布，也不会自动升版本。

### 工作流

文件：

```text
.github/workflows/publish.yml
```

触发条件：

- 推送 `v*` 标签；
- 手动运行 `workflow_dispatch`，但仍要求从版本标签运行。

工作流会：

1. 检查 tag 与 `package.json.version` 完全一致；
2. 查询 npm 上该版本是否已存在，存在则跳过；
3. `npm run build && npm test && npm run check`；
4. `npm publish --access public --provenance`。

### 一次性配置

1. 在 npm 创建 Automation Token；
2. 在 GitHub 仓库 **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions** 添加：
   ```text
   NPM_TOKEN
   ```
3. 确认仓库是 public，`--provenance` 才能正常使用。

### 首次发布

第一次发布需要先在 npm 创建 Automation Token，不能直接依赖本地 2FA 交互：

1. 登录 https://www.npmjs.com/；
2. **Access Tokens → Generate New Token**；
3. 选择 **Granular Access Token**，权限必须是：
   - **Read and write (publish and stage)**
   - 不要选 **Read and write (stage only)**
4. 包权限至少包含当前包名；首次创建包需要允许新包；
5. 在仓库根目录执行并粘贴 token：
   ```powershell
   gh secret set NPM_TOKEN
   ```
6. 创建第一个版本标签并推送：
   ```powershell
   git tag v0.1.0
   git push origin v0.1.0
   ```
7. GitHub Actions 会构建、测试并发布。

如果首次发布报：

```text
E_STAGE_REQUIRED
this token can only publish to a staging area
```

说明 `NPM_TOKEN` 是 **stage only** token。重新生成一个 **publish and stage** token，替换 secret 后重跑 workflow 即可。

如果希望先在本地验证 npm 包：

```powershell
npm login --auth-type=web
npm publish --access public
```

本地 `npm publish` 可能要求浏览器 OTP；CI 使用正确权限的 Automation/Granular Token 不需要交互式 OTP。

### 发布新版本

只在准备发版时执行：

```powershell
npm version patch
git push --follow-tags
```

或者手动指定标签：

```powershell
npm version 0.2.0
git push --follow-tags
```

`npm version` 会：

- 更新 `package.json` 版本；
- 创建 `v0.2.0` 提交和 tag；
- 推送 tag 后触发发布。

如果只是普通代码提交：

```powershell
git add .
git commit -m "..."
git push
```

不会触发 npm 发布。

### 验证

```powershell
npm view dsh-plugin-model-fingerprint version
```

### 用户安装

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-model-fingerprint
```

发布前需确认包名未被占用。若使用 scoped 包名，命令相应改为 `@scope/name`。

### 本地手动检查

```powershell
npm pack --dry-run
npm publish --dry-run
```

`npm publish --dry-run` 会执行 `prepublishOnly` 的构建与测试，但不会真正上传。

---

## 开发

```powershell
npm test
npm run check
npm run build
```

测试覆盖：

- 指纹与声称名称解耦；
- wire API 变化产生新指纹；
- zstd 追加帧增量扫描；
- live 事件去重；
- 状态文件读写与标签/探针持久化；
- 路由变化、别名、标签提示；
- 行为变化点；
- 行为距离和同名模型分组；
- 固定探针；
- 插件路由、工具、标签、探针、补算端到端；
- 客户端几何与用户气泡排除。

---

## 文件结构

```text
index.js                 Host 入口：路由、工具、live 订阅、探针、补算
client.js                构建后的 Client 入口
client/                  Client 源码模块
scripts/build-client.mjs Client 构建脚本
lib/core.mjs             观测提取、指纹哈希、行为统计
lib/scan.mjs             文件发现、增量扫描、live、补算
lib/summary.mjs          指纹族/路由/会话/逐轮/提示
lib/equivalence.mjs      行为画像与距离
lib/similarity.mjs      官方基线、校准、行为相似度、漂移代理
lib/probe.mjs            固定探针
lib/store.mjs            zstd 状态读写
public/dashboard.html    面板
public/widget.js         兜底开关
test/                    单元与端到端测试
```

---

## 已知限制

- 会话日志格式变化可能导致字段缺失；
- DSH/适配器/网关升级会改变协议指纹，可能标记为 `generation`；
- 同一 API 外壳下不同模型可能共享指纹；
- 被动行为受任务影响，跨供应商结论优先使用固定探针；
- 行为相似度不是模型身份概率；
- 质量代理不是语义质量评分；
- 只监控本机 DSH sessions 目录；
- 远程 Web 模式读取的是运行 DSH 的机器上的日志。

# @stofone/dsh-agent-roster

[English](README.en.md) | **简体中文**

面向多 Agent 团队的**静态成员档案**层（DeepSeek Harness）：把「团队里有谁、各自负责什么、走哪个模型、能碰哪些工具」写成可评审、可校验的文件，并在建团之后**核对运行时真实存下的值**。

它不运行团队，也不替代 `dsh-agent-teams`——它补的是「建团前能 review、建完能核、跑偏能回写」这一层。

**一分钟上手**：[安装](#安装) → [快速开始](#快速开始)；完整的格式、工具参数、面板与诊断在 [docs/guide.md](./docs/guide.md)。

## 维护与发版节奏

本仓库由 AI 维护，节奏是公开的，方便你判断「我的问题什么时候会有版本」：

- **每天两次处理**（北京时间 12:00 / 18:00）：12:00 只处理 issue 与 PR，不动版本号；**18:00 才是发版窗口**。
- **一天最多一个版本**；当天没有实质改动就不发。
- **合并 ≠ 已发布**：改动先合入 `main`，随下一个版本发布；`CHANGELOG.md` 的 `Unreleased` 段会写明「计划随哪个版本发布」，升级前可以对照。
- 版本按 SemVer 定级：修 bug 走 patch，新增能力走 minor；一批里含新能力就整批发 minor。
- 所有改动（包括维护者自己的）都走 pull request，`verify` 通过才合并。

安装新版本后需要重启 `dsh web` 才会加载。

## 主要功能

| 能力 | 一句话 | 入口 |
|---|---|---|
| **队长人设运行时注入** | 队长会话的 system prompt 用同名 section 换成档案人设，**每个模型步重读**：改档案下一步生效，不用重启或重建会话 | 自动 |
| 档案定义 | v2 三层：`roles/<name>/AGENT.md`（+ `parts/` 与 `{{> 引用}}`）→ `rosters/<id>/roster.yaml` → 自包含产物 `dist/` | `roster_compile` |
| 校验 | 字段归宿三分（direct / config / declaration）、门必须有可执行的 `verify`、能力要求只报 present / missing / unknown | `validate`、`roster_verify` |
| 建团 | 从档案生成建员参数；新开会话或落到指定会话，可选工作区与会话名 | `roster_team` |
| 换代 | 先比对档案与运行时 → 可选回写 → 新开会话或**在当前会话里换代**（已带队时先问是否归档）；队长用 `handover.summary`、成员用 `handover.members` 带过去 | `roster_iterate` |
| 核对 | 读 `team.json` 里**实际存下的** provider / model / reasoningEffort / toolPolicy，逐项报一致、降级、无法核对 | `roster_verify` |
| 回写 | 把运行时值写回档案；默认**先问再做**，确认后才动文件 | `roster_capture` |
| 知识层 | 角色与档案可声明 `knowledge:`，提示词只放「标题 + 概要 + 路径」，正文按需打开 | `roster_compile` |
| 面板 | 左侧栏「Agent 档案」：档案 / 档案库 / 团队 / 体检四页签，搜索、标签筛选、收藏、拉取空间、导入 | Web UI |
| 空间与订阅 | `space.yaml` 描述一座档案库；可用 `clone` 拉取、`update` 比对六态（不自动合并冲突） | `roster_space`、CLI |

## 它是什么 / 不是什么

| 是 | 不是 |
|---|---|
| 定义与校验层：格式可版本化、可评审，写错时带文件路径与字段路径报错，不静默降级 | 团队运行时：不建成员、不调度任务、不替代调度器 |
| 对 `dsh-agent-teams` 的桥接：产出可直接使用的建员参数，并逐字段标注运行时是否真的接收 | 不写 `.agent-teams/` 状态：只读，用于核对 |
| 核对手段：只认 `team.json` 里实际存下的值 | 不假装通过：证据源缺席时记「无法核对」 |

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @stofone/dsh-agent-roster
```

装完重启 `dsh web`（插件在启动时加载）：左侧栏出现 **Agent 档案**，工具多出十三个。前置只要 Node.js ≥ 22.19。

## 快速开始

档案库默认是**全局**的（一台机器一份），位于 `$DSH_HOME/agent-roster`（默认 `~/.dsh/agent-roster`），首次保存时自动创建。

一份 v2 档案在磁盘上的完整结构（**必需**的两个文件是 `AGENT.md` 与 `roster.yaml`；其余可选，位置在这里列出，内容不展开）：

```
~/.dsh/agent-roster/
├── space.yaml                  # 可选：把这座库登记成一个空间
├── snippets/                   # 可选：正文共享片段（{{> snippets/x.md}}）
├── knowledge/                  # 可选：项目知识，提示词只放标题+概要+路径
├── shared-roles/               # 共享角色（旧名 roles/ 仍读）
│   └── writer/
│       ├── AGENT.md            # 必需：frontmatter + 人设正文
│       └── parts/              # 可选：正文分段，按 prompt.parts 的顺序拼接
├── rosters/
│   └── docs/
│       ├── roster.yaml         # 必需：成员、队长、编排与门
│       ├── roles/              # 可选：只属于这份档案的角色（同名压过共享）
│       └── capabilities.yaml   # 可选：部署侧必须先提供什么
└── dist/
    └── docs-1.0.0.json         # 编译产物（面板、/install 与订阅读它）
```

最小档案就是 `roles/writer/AGENT.md` + `rosters/docs/roster.yaml`，再跑一次 `compile` 得到 `dist/`。完整字段见 [docs/guide.md](./docs/guide.md)。

### 1. 写一个角色

`roles/writer/AGENT.md`：

```markdown
---
kind: dsh-agent-roster/role@1
name: writer
version: 1.0.0
role: 技术写作
title: 文档维护
description: 只改文档，不动代码
tags: [docs]
route:
  model: deepseek-flash
  reasoningEffort: high
tools:
  policy: read-only
---

你负责文档。改完必须跑 `npm run check:locale`，报错就把原始输出贴出来。
```

### 2. 写一份档案

`rosters/docs/roster.yaml`：

```yaml
kind: dsh-agent-roster/roster@2
id: docs
version: 1.0.0
title: 文档小队
members:
  - as: writer
    role: writer@1.0.0
captain:
  role: writer@1.0.0
  notes: 队长人设由插件注入队长会话的 system prompt，每步重读。
```

### 3. 校验

```bash
npx dsh-agent-roster validate --dir ~/.dsh/agent-roster   # 格式、引用、能力、门
npx dsh-agent-roster list --dir ~/.dsh/agent-roster       # 列档案与成员
npx dsh-agent-roster compile --roster ~/.dsh/agent-roster/rosters/docs
```

### 4. 建团并核对

对队长会话说「用 docs 档案建一支团队」，或在面板「团队 → 创建团队」里选它；建完在同一个会话里跑：

```
roster_verify            # 档案 vs 运行时，逐字段
roster_capture           # 想把运行时值写回档案时（默认先问）
roster_iterate           # 换代：新开会话，或当前会话换代（先问是否归档旧队）
```

## 文档

| 文档 | 讲什么 |
|---|---|
| [docs/guide.md](./docs/guide.md) | **完整手册**：三种落盘形态、v1/v2 格式、正文引用、公共知识、字段归宿、能力要求、空间、面板、十三个工具、命令行、路由、配置、诊断 |
| [docs/roster-v2.md](./docs/roster-v2.md) | v2 格式规范（角色 / 档案 / 产物 / 施工图） |
| [docs/design.md](./docs/design.md) | 设计取舍与模块落点 |
| [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md) | 每个版本改了什么、为什么、影响面 |
| [examples/](./examples)、[examples-orchestration/](./examples-orchestration) | 两座示例库：最小档案；带门与施工图的编排 |

## 边界

- 不跑团队、不调度、不写 `.agent-teams/`；也**不自动重启**任何服务。
- 一个会话最多领导一支团队；同一档案的换代请走 `roster_iterate`，而不是原地重建。
- 面板改档案 = 改文件；`.agent-teams/` 里的运行时值不会被面板改写。

## 开发与验证

```bash
node --test              # 468 个测试
npm run smoke            # 宿主 + 客户端两段冒烟
npm run check:host       # 四条宿主契约（对着装好的 DSH 读）
npm run check:locale     # 面板文案 en/zh 对齐
node bin/cli.mjs validate --dir examples
npm run e2e              # 真起宿主：面板 17 项
```

## 许可

MIT。示例库与角色素材的许可见各自目录；`@michengai/dsh-agency-agents` 导入的素材遵循其 Apache-2.0 NOTICE。

# @asuna/agent-line Coding agents on this machine (Claude Code, or another) as an Asuna channel. Each agent has one direct line to her: a trusted home conversation, like the DSH peer line, that she can close herself. Who speaks is its own person (`agent:`), never the owner. The owner is a member of every line too (`OWNER_JOINS`): he writes there in the Web composer, as himself, with his own grants. Closing a line shuts out its agent, not the owner. The package only registers the kind (`agent`, `HOME`, `PEER_LINE`, `ROUTE_KEYS`, `OWNER_JOINS`, `MARKS_ANSWERS` with `answerer`). Nothing runs in the Host for it: the agent posts and polls through the channel API with `tools/agent_line.py`. A line is a local conversation: she speaks there through `speak` in text, sticker and picture parts, with none of QQ's rules on it. ## Configuration (owner-local) Configure the channel in Asuna's settings like any other (`channels.agent`: `account_id`, token, one `dm` route per agent whose `sender_id` is the route name), with a `display_name` for each route: ```json "agent": { "account_id": "home", "token": "", "routes": { "claude-code": {"sender_id": "claude-code", "person_id": "agent:claude-code", "scene_id": "agent:home:dm:claude-code", "target": {"type": "dm", "id": "claude-code"}, "display_name": "Claude（开发助手）"} } } ``` Add `packages/channels/agent-line` to the profile's channel packages (`setup_native_profile.py --channel-package`). At start the host writes the route's key to `/private/route-keys/agent-.json`. ## Use ``` python tools/agent_line.py send claude-code "我是 Claude，……" python tools/agent_line.py send claude-code "改这一行就好" --answers q-1a2b3c4d python tools/agent_line.py poll claude-code --wait 120 python tools/agent_line.py status claude-code ``` `poll` prints what the owner wrote on that line since the last poll (marked as the owner's), then her answers on it, one part each, and confirms each answer; an answer nobody polls stays queued. It claims with `supports=image,sticker`: a sticker or a picture of hers is fetched from the outbox's attachment endpoint, checked against its `sha256` and written to `/asuna-agent-line//.`, and the part prints as `[sticker] ` or `[picture] `; its receipt carries `response.attachment` (`artifact_id`, `media_type`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `sha256_verified: true`), as a platform adapter's does. One that cannot be fetched or does not match its `sha256` prints as `[picture not received: ]` (or `sticker`) and its receipt says `failed`. Each poll removes that route's files written more than 7 days before; her record of what she sent is the stored picture, not the file. The key opens only its own line: posting as that route, claiming her words there, fetching their pictures and confirming them. Anything on the machine can read the key file, so the line's boundary is the machine; what it opens is one agent's voice in her home, never the owner's voice or chat. When she asks on a line with `ask` (`questions_from_program` shows the question's id), a message answers it only with `send --answers `; an agent's message without it answers nothing. A line the owner writes there from the Web (he cannot mark one) is still taken as the answer when it is the first after her question. The developer's line, where a `message_developer` call goes (it runs as `ask` on that line), is the route with `"developer": true`, else the route named `claude-code`. She never sees a local root of this computer: what an agent posts reaches her with each path written as `${ASUNA_WORKSPACE}/...`, `${ASUNA_DATA}/...`, `${ASUNA_HOME}/...` and the other names of the root table, and she writes paths the same way ([Local roots](../../../RUNTIME_API.md#local-roots) says what each name stands for). An agent on this machine reads her paths by those names; a real path it posts is shown to her contracted.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages: `ichinose-asuna`, `kyoyama-kazusa`, `shirase-shiori`, `xiaoman` and `yan-sui`. A persona package carries no channel configuration; any channel package works with any of them. | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-alpha.3, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# @asuna/dsh-peer Another DeepSeek Harness (DSH) agent as an Asuna channel. The peer lives in one session of another DSH Web server; she talks with it in one direct-message conversation of her own. - **Inbound:** the bridge follows that session (`session/follow` over `/api/remote.mux`). The peer's final reply of each completed turn becomes a direct message from the peer. - A turn answers her when its prompt is one she sent (DSH records it as `{kind: 'user', rpcId}`). A reply that did not answer her gets `ownerNote` as its first line and `raw.asuna_aside: true`: the host keeps it without waking her, and her home heartbeats and the plans due at home list it until she speaks on the line. - A new bridge starts from the session's present; it never replays history. - `occurred_at` uses the peer event's timestamp. A peer event without a timestamp omits it; forwarding time is not substituted. - **Outbound:** her words leave through the channel outbox. The bridge sends them as prompts to the session, with `label` as the first line and `replyNote` (her own words on how to answer her) before her text, and records the platform receipt (`platform_message_id` = the prompt's `requestId`). The line carries text only (`TEXT_ONLY`): no picture is offered there, and a sticker part fails at the claim (`CHANNEL_DOES_NOT_DECLARE_STICKER`). - **Scope:** only `session/follow` and `session/prompt`, only on the configured session. It is its own adapter: the bridge runs in this Host's plugin process (no sandboxed integration). It reaches the channel API through `ctx.asuna.channelEndpoint('dsh')`. It keeps its position in `/bridges/dsh-.json`. ## Configuration (owner-local) Configure the channel in Asuna's settings like any other (`channels.dsh`: `account_id`, token, one `dm` route whose `sender_id` is the peer). The scene id is `dsh::dm:` and the person is `dsh:`. Then configure this plugin's row in the profile's editable patch: ```yaml - id: asuna-dsh-peer name: '@asuna/dsh-peer' config: url: https://192.0.2.10 # the peer DSH Web server sessionId: session-… # the one session bridged routeId: peer-dm # the route in channels.dsh senderId: peer # that route's sender_id label: '[from …]' # who is speaking, first line of her messages there ownerNote: '(not a reply to you)' replyNote: '(how she asks to be answered)' # opens every message of hers; her words insecureTls: true # a LAN service behind its own local CA closedUntil: '2026-01-01T09:00:00+13:00' # optional: line closed until then, reopens by itself ``` Without `url`, `sessionId`, `routeId` and `senderId` the bridge stays idle. While `closedUntil` lies ahead, the peer's replies are passed over (not delivered later) and her words wait in the outbox; the line reopens by itself.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages: `ichinose-asuna`, `kyoyama-kazusa`, `shirase-shiori`, `xiaoman` and `yan-sui`. A persona package carries no channel configuration; any channel package works with any of them. | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2-alpha.3, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# QQ through NapCat — Asuna channel plugin

A channel package for `@asuna/cognition-core` 1.x in DSH **0.2.2-alpha.3**. It registers the channel kind `qq`
with Core (`registerChannel`).

- `python/napcat_qq/` is the kind module the worker imports: QQ person ids `qq:<account>` and scene ids
  `qq:<bot>:<dm|group>:<target>`, how the adapter writes a real @ in inbound text (`@<account>`) and how her @
  reaches it (`@qq:<account>`), the media hosts vision fetches QQ images from by default, and the adapter
  settings derived from the configured channel.
- `integration/` is the NapCat / OneBot v11 adapter (`adapter.py`, `qqadapter/`, vendored `websocket-client` with its
  license). Core's integration service runs it in DSH's sandbox; the owner-granted `integration_*` tools develop
  it in this package's own development project (`napcat-qq`).
- `skills/qq-napcat-adapter/` is the adapter's skill; it joins her skill directories.
- The people a group message @-mentions are looked up like its sender (`get_group_member_info`, the same refresh and
  cache windows, at most three lookups per message) and ride on the event as `raw.asuna_mentioned`.
- After a gap (the adapter starting, or its event socket coming back) the messages missed on the routes
  `adapter_config.catchup.routes` names, or on every route Core serves under `"all"`, and that Core admits, are fetched from history (`get_group_msg_history` /
  `get_friend_msg_history`, from a per-route time cursor in the adapter's data folder however old it is; a
  route without one looks back `lookback_hours`, 1–24) and fed oldest first through the usual inbound path,
  marked `raw.asuna_catchup`. At most 5 pages of 100 forward from the cursor, then the newest page: a longer gap
  loses lines in its middle, not the ones just before the adapter came back. Off by default.
- A merged forward (合并转发) is read before the event is posted: from the messages NapCat includes in the segment,
  else with one `get_forward_msg` call (8 s), a forward inside it one level deep, at most 3 forwards a message, 100
  messages and 20,000 characters a forward. They ride on the event as `raw.asuna_forward` (`ref`, `count`, `nodes`
  with name, account, time and text, `source` `inline` or `fetched`), and the line shows `[合并转发｜N 条｜ref]` with
  the first three messages, one short line each. One that cannot be read keeps its placeholder. The log names the
  segment's fields, the source and the count, never the text.
- A group or private-chat message that quotes another carries the quoted message's ID as `reply_to`; one that only
  quotes, with no words, also carries `raw.asuna_reply_only`. On every outbox claim the adapter declares what it
  carries: `image`, `sticker`, `file:<bytes>` (`adapter_config.napcat.max_file_mb`), `react`, `poke`, `quote`,
  `quote_in`, `react_in`, `recall`, `voice_in`.
- A file goes to a group alone, up to `adapter_config.napcat.max_file_mb` (default 50 MiB); a private target is a
  `failed` receipt. Its bytes come from Core's attachment endpoint in 4 MiB pieces, each sent to NapCat's
  `upload_file_stream` (stream id = the attempt id, the whole file's sha256, NapCat's temp file named after the
  attempt), so one WebSocket message stays under 8 MiB; the adapter checks the sha256 across the pieces and NapCat
  checks it again when the stream completes. Then `upload_group_file` sends it under her name for it. The receipt
  carries NapCat's answer (its `file_id` only as data, never as an id) and the file's artifact id, sha256 and size;
  a refusal carries the platform's words as `response.platform`. Each wait has a bound: a piece up to 60 s to fetch
  from Core and 60 s for NapCat to take it (a failed piece ends the send after a reset of up to 10 s), completing the
  stream 60 s + size / 32 MiB/s, the upload 120 s + size / 1 MiB/s. At 50 MiB a whole send is bounded by about
  30 minutes (13 pieces × 120 s, then 62 s and 170 s).
  An upload that outlasts its wait is `unknown`, and a later answer settles it. Files come on a lane of their own
  (`lane=bulk`, one upload at a time), so an upload holds no message, not even the later parts of its own reply.
- Messages, stickers, pictures, reactions and admin actions come on the chat lane: up to four sends at once, each
  of another conversation (Core never hands out two of one conversation at once), so a slow send holds only its own
  conversation. A receipt Core does not take at once, and every receipt of a late platform answer, is spooled and
  posted from a thread of its own, so a Core slow to take receipts holds no send and never NapCat's reader; a spooled
  receipt is not given up while Core is away (no answer or its whole-Core 503), only after 20 error answers. At a stop
  the sends already on their way, the bulk lane's included, get up to 20 s to finish. A Core that names no lane in its
  claim answers (from before ADR-095) gets one send at a time, as before.
- Inbound lines go to Core in their order within each conversation, from a lane of that conversation's own (up to
  8 conversations at once; a lane gives its place after 20 lines, and the conversation that waited longest since its
  last lane goes first). A line is
  prepared once (its lookups, forward and voices; the prepared line is written back to the spool) and posted as often
  as it takes, tried again after 2, 5, 15, 30 and then every 60 s; a line that is slow to prepare or that Core does
  not take holds only its own conversation. An answer about Core itself (no answer, a dropped connection, 503 for the
  whole Core, `CHANNEL_AUTH_REQUIRED`) makes the line wait. A 503 Core names (applying settings, stopping, its
  database) and `CHANNEL_AUTH_REQUIRED` never count; no answer counts only when other lines went in since the line's
  previous try (then Core is there and that line is the one not getting in). A voice that could not be handed to Core
  is fetched and handed over again on the next try. A line Core fails on its own (500 and other 5xx), or one whose try fails
  in the adapter, is set aside after five counted tries in `journal/inbound_failed.jsonl` and its conversation goes
  on; a 4xx goes to `journal/inbound_rejected.jsonl` at once; a 2xx settles it (accepted, a duplicate, or held,
  dropped or passed over by Core, its status in `journal/inbound_sent.jsonl`).
- A voice message (`record` segment) is settled before its line is posted, because NapCat clears its voice cache and
  a line should reach her with its words: on the submit path each voice is asked of NapCat (`get_record` with the
  segment's `file` and `out_format` `mp3`, 10 s) and its audio (`base64` in the answer) is posted to Core's `voice`
  endpoint for that line and segment index, which transcribes it within the request. When there is no outcome
  (retcode 1200 `file not found` is `gone`; another refusal, a timeout, no connection, no audio in the answer, or the
  Core call failing each have their reason), the reason rides on that voice's media item as `voice_refused`, so her
  line says why. The line is posted after its voices either way, so lines keep their order; a voice line, and those
  queued behind it in the same conversation, wait for NapCat's conversion and the transcription (about 1.5 s for a
  minute of speech), at most 210 s per voice (the fetch's 10 s and the Core call's 200 s, longer than Core's 180 s
  for one voice; a QQ voice message carries one voice). The log (`VOICE_SETTLED`, `VOICE_NOT_SETTLED`) carries the
  event, the segment, the byte count and the outcome, never the file name, the audio or the words.
- A message she sends quotes a line (a leading `reply` segment) only when the outbox item carries `quote`, in a group
  or a private chat; the item's `reply_to`, the line her words answer, is not shown.
- A `recall` action in her reply takes back a message of hers (`delete_msg` on its id); the platform's retcode is
  the receipt.
- Duplicate detection binds the conversation, platform message ID and original send time in whole seconds. A pushed message and its catch-up copy use the same key; an ID reused at a later time is a new message. Reply attribution selects the newest matching line at or before the reply's send time.
- Who may speak is Core's, never this adapter's: it asks Core's `admission` endpoint (a sender in a conversation) and
  reuses an answer for the time Core names. A line nobody has judged is spooled without a route; its conversation's
  lane asks before it looks anything up on the platform, so a refused sender costs the platform no lookup. Core not
  answering holds the lines, an older Core without the endpoint holds them too and raises a lane fault. A member's
  leave or removal (`group_decrease`) is posted to Core's `departures` endpoint.
- Each admitted group's member list (`get_group_list`, then `get_group_member_list` for the groups Core has a route
  for) is fetched when the adapter starts and every 6 hours, reduced to id, names, role and activity times,
  and posted to Core's `members` endpoint only when it changed.
- Picture links from the NT media host are signed (`rkey`) for minutes; the picture stays. Every 4 minutes (a
  minute after a failed round) the adapter asks NapCat for its current download keys — `get_rkey`, else
  `nc_get_rkey`, else `get_rkey_server` — and posts them to Core's `media_keys` endpoint as `qq-group` (appid 1407)
  and `qq-private` (appid 1406) with the seconds each still lasts. Core signs a stored link again with them before
  fetching it. The keys are never logged or written to disk; the log says which names were posted, for how long,
  and which action answered.
- Every item in hand (an inbound line's try, a chat send, a file, a pass of receipts) has a budget: the sum of its
  own steps' deadlines plus a margin (an inbound try 120 s, 3 s per person it mentions and 210 s per voice; a chat
  send 150 s; a file 120 s per 4 MiB piece plus its joining and QQ's taking it plus 60 s; 15 s per receipt), so only
  a bug reaches it. Past it the item is marked stuck — a `STUCK` log line, a lane fault (lane, the stage it is in,
  `stuck`), a row in `journal/stuck.jsonl` — and gives its place up, so other conversations keep their lanes; a
  stuck file gets a new bulk lane (one at most). At most a pool's worth of stuck items give their places up; more stuck
  at once is a shared cause, and those hold their places. The item itself is held, never posted or sent twice: its
  conversation waits for it (a later send there waits for it too, after the Core's hold has ended), a lane whose line
  was stuck ends after that line, and `STUCK_ENDED` with a second row tells when it came back. The check runs with the
  health snapshot. A message's forwards are read with at most 6 fetches, nested ones included; a forward past that
  keeps its placeholder.
- The `STATUS` line (every minute) ends with a `lanes:` block, keys in this order: `in_slots` (inbound places taken /
  places), `queued` (conversations waiting for a place), `oldest_wait` (the oldest line waiting, its conversation and
  where it is: `slot`, `retry` or its stage), `longest_running` (the oldest inbound try in hand, its conversation and
  stage), `chat_slots`, `longest_send` (publication and stage), `bulk` (the file's time, size and stage, or `idle`),
  `receipts` and `oldest_receipt`, `stuck` (how many since start) and `last_stuck` (lane/item/stage). Places full
  with conversations queued means too few places; places free while one conversation waits means that
  conversation is slow on its own. `health.json` `lanes` has the whole table: every conversation with lines waiting
  (how many, the oldest's age, where), every item in hand with its stage, age and budget. Each line's journal row
  carries its stage times: `inbound_sent.jsonl` `stages` (peer, mentions, forward, role, voice, host_in) and
  `since_spooled_s`; `sends.jsonl` `stages` (fetch, send, verify, receipt).
- Each lane fault — a line set aside (`inbound_failed`, `inbound_rejected`, unreadable), a receipt refused or given
  up, an exception in a send, an item stuck past its budget — is counted by signature (lane, stage, error class; never the line) and hour, kept in
  `faults_pending.json` until Core takes it, and posted to Core's `faults` endpoint every 5 minutes (a minute after a
  failed post). An error is counted by its code alone, never its words. A batch Core refuses as it is goes to
  `journal/faults_rejected.jsonl` and is dropped, so it never holds the counts after it.
- Her own role in each group (asked with `get_group_member_info` for the logged-in account, cached ten minutes)
  rides on group events as `raw.asuna_self`. Admin actions the host queues (mute, unmute, kick, recall) become
  `set_group_ban`, `set_group_kick` and `delete_msg`, and nothing else; the platform's retcode is the receipt.
- Every NapCat notice and request is projected into one line of words from a versioned table
  (`qqadapter/notices.py`, `WORDS`): a person in a group line is `@<account>` (Core shows their label), her own
  account is 你, text a person controls stays in 「」. Which kinds she is shown is the switch table `SHOWN`: a poke at
  her, a reaction (to a line of hers it asks for her look; one between others is kept for her next turn), a recall, friend and group requests, a kick of her account
  and a change of her admin role. A shown group or private-chat line goes to Core's `events` endpoint from the person
  who did it, under a message's gates, with `raw.asuna_notice` (`kind`, `gate` `poked` / `reacted`, `line`); a
  request or news about her account goes to the `notices` endpoint for her home, with the person's nickname
  (`get_stranger_info`) and, for a group she has no conversation in, its name (`get_group_info`). Her answer to a
  request comes back as an admin action and becomes `set_friend_add_request` or `set_group_add_request` with the
  request's flag. Every kind is counted, with no content: `health.json` `notices` shows today's and the last 7 days'
  counts by kind and outcome (`posted`, `home`, `own_state`, `not_shown`, `not_projected`, `unknown`, a gate that dropped it),
  kept by UTC day for 14 days in `notices/counts.json` in the adapter's data folder. Typing, connection events, her
  messages sent elsewhere and online-file transfers are counted, never projected.
- A face, and a segment of a type the adapter has no word for (a dice, a rock-paper-scissors, a store face under
  another name), carries `shape` in its media item: which fields the platform sent, never their words. It is the sorted key
  names of the segment's `data` and of `data.raw`, and the value of `result`, `resultId`, `chainCount` and `faceType`
  when it is one to four digits (`qqadapter/inbound.py` `shape_of`), at most 200 characters. Core stores the item with
  its line, so the shape has the line's time and order.
- Her own mute in each admitted group goes to Core's `own_mute` endpoint. A `group_ban` notice (`ban` / `lift_ban`)
  about her account, or about the whole group (`user_id` 0), is posted at once as state (until = notice time +
  duration, the operator's account); every other notice is dropped. A send NapCat refuses with retcode 1200 and QQ
  result 120 is a `failed` receipt with `response.reason` `muted`, and that group is looked at at once. When the
  adapter starts or its event socket comes back, each admitted group not looked at in the last 6 hours is looked at,
  one a second; the times are kept in `mutes/checked.json` in the adapter's data folder. A look is
  `get_group_member_info` for her account (`shut_up_timestamp`) and `get_group_info` (`group_all_shut`), both with
  `no_cache`; it never sends, mutes or unmutes. The log (`OWN_MUTE*`) carries the group, the outcome and the seconds
  a round took.

`resources-provenance.json` records the source hashes of the distributed resources. No private configuration,
account, route, log, inbox/outbox or media is included.

## Setting up QQ

You need a running [NapCat](https://napneko.github.io/) logged in to the QQ account she uses, with its OneBot v11
**WebSocket server** enabled (forward WebSocket) and an access token. One QQ account serves one Asuna instance at a
time: two characters on one account both receive every message and both answer it. Give each running character its
own account ([Running several characters](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md#running-several-characters)).

1. **Install the package** with the persona: `--channel packages/channels/napcat-qq` to `tools/pack_plugins.py` and
   `--channel-package packages/channels/napcat-qq` to `tools/setup_native_profile.py` (or add the release `.tgz`
   with `dsh plugin add`). See [Add or remove an optional package](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md#add-or-remove-an-optional-package).
2. **Configure the channel** (`channels.qq` in the deployment; on a first install, the `channels` block of
   `asuna-channel.local.json`, template [config/asuna-channel.example.json](../../../config/asuna-channel.example.json)):
   - `account_id`: the bot's QQ number;
   - `token`: a random string of at least 24 characters, shared by the adapter and Core's channel API;
   - `routes`: at least the owner's DM, `{"sender_id", "person_id": "qq:<id>", "scene_id": "qq:<bot>:dm:<id>",
     "target": {"type": "dm", "id": "<id>"}}`. A group route has `"scene_id": "qq:<bot>:group:<group>"`, `"target": {"type": "group", "id": "<group>"}` and
     `members` (`{"<qq id>": {"person_id": "qq:<qq id>"}}`). Each person's workspace is a folder in the profile's data
     folder unless the route or member names an absolute `workspace` there. With **外部渠道接入策略** (Channel admission) `automatic` (or `--channel-admission
     automatic` at install), new DMs and groups get routes on their first valid message, so only the owner's DM
     needs configuring;
   - optional `blocked_senders` / `blocked_groups` (Core's: the adapter does not read them).
3. **Link the owner** at the top level: `canonical_persons` maps `qq:<owner id>` to the local chat's person, so her
   owner in QQ and at home is one person; `context_links` (`{"<local scene>": ["<QQ DM scene>"]}`) lets the local chat read the owner's DM.
4. **Configure the adapter** (`integration` in the deployment; on a first install, `integration.local.json`):
   - `enabled: true`, and `scene_id` / `person_id` of the owner's local chat (the adapter is the owner's integration);
   - `endpoints`: the addresses the adapter may reach, each `{"name", "host": "<private or loopback IP>",
     "port": <local alias port ≥ 1024>, "target_port": <the device's port>}` — one for NapCat and one for
     Core's channel API (`127.0.0.1`, `channel_port`, default 8766);
   - `adapter_config.napcat`: `{"transport": "websocket_forward", "url": "ws://127.0.0.1:<alias port>", "token": "<NapCat
     access token>"}`;
   - optional `adapter_config.napcat.max_file_mb`: the largest file the adapter sends to a group, in MiB (an integer
     1–4096, default 50); it declares it to Core as `file:<bytes>`, and Core refuses a larger file before sending. A
     value it cannot use is the default, said once in the log (`CONFIG_NOTE`);
   - `adapter_config.host`: `{"base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:<alias port>", "channel_id": "qq"}`;
   - optional `adapter_config.catchup`: `{"routes": ["<route id>", …] or "all", "lookback_hours": 6}` turns on
     catch-up after a gap for those routes (route ids as Core names them: the keys of `channels.qq.routes`, or
     `auto-group-<id>` / `auto-dm-<id>` for a group or DM that open admission admitted; Core says which it admits;
     `"all"` means every route Core serves and every route the adapter has a cursor for).
   With `enabled: true`, the adapter starts by itself on the first start (`python3 /app/adapter.py --service`) and
   restarts with her from then on, unless its integration settings changed since it last ran other than by applying
   the settings card (it then stays stopped until `integration_start`); after an `integration_stop` it stays stopped
   until started again.
   The NapCat account id and the host token are derived from `channels.qq`; do not repeat them. The adapter holds no
   route, allowlist or block list: Core decides who may speak.
5. **Save and apply** on the settings card, then check the card's status line and send her a DM.

Tokens typed into the settings card go to DSH's credential store; the settings keep only references.
