evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-claude-whiteboard A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugin that adds the **claude-whiteboard** skill from [baoyu-design](https://github.com/JimLiu/baoyu-design): the agent lays out diagrams, flows, maps of ideas, plans and comparisons on a whiteboard in your workspace, and opens it in a local board editor, where you move things, draw, type and comment. ## Install In the DeepSeek Harness desktop app: **Plugins** → **Add plugin** → enter `dsh-claude-whiteboard` in **Package name or address** → **Install**, and turn the plugin on. From the command line, for a CLI profile such as `web`: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-claude-whiteboard ``` Then quit and reopen the app, start a new session, and ask for a board, or type `/claude-whiteboard`. A workspace that has its own `claude-whiteboard` skill (in `.agents/skills/` or `.dsh/skills/`) uses that copy instead of this plugin's. ## What is inside - `skills/claude-whiteboard/`: the skill as baoyu-design publishes it (`SKILL.md`, `artifact-type/reference/`, and the prebuilt `scripts/`: the board page and `artifact.mjs`, which is also its server). - `lib/index.js`: the plugin. It registers the skill with the Harness skill registry and, when the skill loads, tells the agent which Node executable runs `scripts/artifact.mjs`: the Host's own Node, the Node runtime the desktop app ships, or `node` on PATH. Set `node` in the `claude-whiteboard` row's config to choose another. That is all this row does, so you can turn it off and [keep the skill to one agent preset](https://github.com/JimLiu/baoyu-design/blob/main/dsh-plugins/README.md#keep-a-skill-to-one-preset). - `cordis.patch.yml`: the bundle layer that mounts two rows: this plugin's, and its row of `dsh-claude-artifacts`. [`dsh-claude-artifacts`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-artifacts) installs with this plugin and does the rest, whichever way the skill is set up: whenever the agent opens a board it waits for comments, so a comment's **Send to Agent** box is there: send one and the agent wakes up, changes the board, and replies in the comment. It shows what is sent as a card in the chat, and adds **Artifacts** to the left sidebar, one entry for all the baoyu-design plugins: the boards and everything else the agent has opened, each a click away from its conversation and editor. The board server listens on 127.0.0.1 only and reads and writes only the folders of the boards it serves. ## License Not all MIT. The plugin's own code and files (`lib/`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `locale/`, `docs/`, `icon.svg`) and the skill's local tooling are MIT, in `LICENSE`. The bundled `claude-whiteboard` skill is adapted from Anthropic's claude.ai Whiteboard type: its instructions, references, board editor and icon fonts stay Anthropic's and are not under the MIT License. `NOTICE.md` sets out which is which. The editor's open-source licenses are in `skills/claude-whiteboard/scripts/editor/third-party-licenses.txt`. # baoyu-design https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5b4f39b-a701-49de-87b8-64f3c6ef9c61 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84ddf462-5ac6-44c6-a175-05a7ccaa019e https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/db6c5d93-dc28-4170-8356-4dbe5725a57c **Run Claude Design on your own local agent — Cursor, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or any file‑capable coding agent.** [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) [![License: MIT for own code, see NOTICE](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT%20for%20own%20code%20%C2%B7%20see%20NOTICE-blue.svg)](NOTICE.md) ![Best with Opus 5.5](https://img.shields.io/badge/Best%20with-Opus%205.5-d97757) ![Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cursor%20%C2%B7%20Claude%20Code%20%C2%B7%20Codex-supported-1f6feb) This repo brings claude.ai's **Artifact types** to local agents: editable slide decks, design canvases, design systems, data dashboards, motion films and whiteboards, each opened in its own editor that runs on your machine. `motion-director` directs those films, from the point of the film to the finished cut. `dataviz` is the chart guide the agent reads before it draws any chart, in these skills or anywhere else. The six editors also ship as [DeepSeek Harness plugins](#deepseek-harness-plugins), installed from npm by name. The original `baoyu-design` skill (self‑contained HTML mockups and prototypes) has been archived to [`archive/baoyu-design/`](archive/baoyu-design/). No website, no separate subscription, no upload step. The agent already on your machine does the work, and every artifact stays in your repo. --- ## Skills in this repo | Skill | Makes | You edit it in | |---|---|---| | [`claude-slides`](skills/claude-slides/) | Slide decks: `project/deck.json` plus one HTML file per slide | The slides editor: present, retype, drag; export PDF, HTML or PowerPoint | | [`claude-design`](skills/claude-design/) | A canvas of artboards: `project/canvas.json` plus `.dc.html` Design Components | The canvas editor: artboards side by side, play prototypes, retype copy, adjust tweaks; export HTML, PDF, PNG or HTML for Figma | | [`claude-design-system`](skills/claude-design-system/) | Design systems: tokens, a README brand book, component previews, fonts, asset groups | The design system editor: browse and edit colors, type, components and assets | | [`claude-data`](skills/claude-data/) | Data‑backed dashboards: datasets (CSV, TSV, JSON) and a page of charts, numbers and tables over them | The dashboard page: live charts, filters, and a Sources panel that traces every number to its rows | | [`claude-motion`](skills/claude-motion/) | Motion films: animated videos, 10–30 s unless you ask for more and 15 minutes at most, written as code scene by scene into the film's own store under `/db/` | The Motion player: watch it fill in, retype lines, drag scene lengths, adjust style and tweaks; export MP4 or GIF | | [`motion-director`](skills/motion-director/) | A finished film with something to say: it finds the point, writes the narration for the ear, has it voiced, times every scene to the words, and checks the frames as a viewer would. Needs `claude-motion` beside it | The same Motion player, open from the first minute | | [`claude-whiteboard`](skills/claude-whiteboard/) | Whiteboards: diagrams, flows, maps of ideas, plans and comparisons, written as elements (blocks, sections, arrows, tables, sticky notes, drawings, working embeds) into the board's own store under `/db/` | The board editor: move, resize, type, draw with the pen, add sections, sticky notes, shapes and stickers, drop in videos; export PNG | | [`dataviz`](skills/dataviz/) | Better charts in any medium (HTML, SVG, d3, matplotlib, plotly…): picking the form, colors that stay readable in light and dark and for color‑blind readers, marks, legends and tooltips, with a palette validator script | Nothing to open: the agent reads it before writing chart code; swap [`palette.md`](skills/dataviz/references/palette.md) for your brand's colors | --- ## Artifact skills: editable decks, canvases, design systems, dashboards, films and whiteboards These six skills write the Artifact type's own file format into a folder and open it in that type's editor page, served from your machine. The agent writes the files and the editor shows each write at once; your edits in the editor are saved back into the same files, so you and the agent can take turns. In the slides, canvas and design-system editors and on the dashboard page, choose **Comment** (or press **C**) to comment on an element or area; in the Motion player, its **Comment** button comments on a moment of the film; on a whiteboard, the comments button comments on an item, a spot or an area. Comments stay in the project's local `comments.json`; the agent reads and replies through `artifact.mjs`. While it listens with `comments --wait`, the editor offers **Send to Agent** to send your comment for it to act on, and the page's own buttons that ask the agent for something (**Ask the agent to fix** on a slide or canvas that can't be shown, the design system's setup buttons, the dashboard's **Ask the agent**) send it their request the same way. To work together, `share ` (or `open --lan`) opens the deck, canvas, design system, dashboard, film or board to your local network, the same Wi‑Fi or LAN, and prints a link per role: **editor** edits and comments, **commenter** comments without editing, **viewer** only looks. Whoever opens a link types a name and is in; what they change shows on everyone's page, and their comments land in the same `comments.json`. The person at this computer is the owner: the **Share** button lists who joined and who is online, changes someone's role or removes them, and turns each link off, back on or resets it. Guests get a Share button too, with the links they may pass on: their own role's and those below it. There is no account and nothing leaves your network; it is plain http, so anyone there with a link gets in. Every change is kept as a version, with who made it: a guest by the name they typed, the owner, or **Agent** for a change made to the files on this computer. The **History** button (the clock beside Share) lists the versions by day; open one to see which slides, artboards or documents it changed, line by line, preview the whole thing as it was, or restore it (or just one part) as a new version, so nothing is lost. When two people save the same slide at once, the later save no longer wipes out the earlier one unnoticed: the version records whose change it replaced, and both people get a notice with **Compare** and **Bring back**, which puts back only what was replaced and leaves the other person's other changes. In the slides, design and design-system editors, someone else's save updates your page in place instead of reloading it, and if they saved the slide, artboard or file you have unsaved edits on, a bar asks whether to use theirs, keep yours, or keep both (yours becomes a new slide after it, an artboard beside it, or a copy of the file). The two are first merged: on a canvas element by element, in slides and design-system files line by line (a token file token by token). When you changed different elements or lines, both changes stay and nothing asks; the bar comes up only when the merge cannot sort it out, such as both changing the same line. The history lives in the project's `history/` folder. While others have the page open, their avatars sit beside History. In the slides and canvas editors each one's card says which slide or artboard they are on and whether they are editing, and their cursors and selections show where they work; when someone starts editing what you are looking at, you get a short note, and nothing is ever locked. While Claude changes the files, it shows up there too. To back a project up, move it to another computer or hand it to someone, the owner's **Whole folder (.zip)** item, last in the Share panel's Export tab (the owner's: guests can pass a link on but not export), downloads the whole folder as one zip, its history and comments included; `artifact.mjs archive ` does the same from the command line. Unzip it anywhere and `open` it with the same skill to carry on. This computer's server state and the share links are left out, so a copy you send is not shared until its new owner shares it. ### `claude-slides`: slide decks A deck is `project/deck.json` plus one HTML file per slide. In the editor you can present full screen, retype any text, drag elements, add text, images, tables and shapes, and export to PDF, HTML or PowerPoint. A video added by link plays in its provider's player, and the agent can upload a clip for a slide. *Above: a five‑slide health class deck about sleep, built on a sample design system.* ### `claude-design`: a canvas of artboards A canvas holds artboards side by side: `project/canvas.json` plus one `.dc.html` Design Component per artboard. Play an artboard as a working prototype, on the canvas or full screen; retype copy, adjust tweaks and leave notes; export the whole design as a standalone HTML page, a PDF or PNG images (1× or 2×, several artboards in a .zip); **HTML for Figma** saves the artboards as a page without frames, for Figma's Chrome extension to capture. Full window, an artboard lays out at a screen width you pick (phone, tablet or desktop sizes), and its Export saves the whole page at that width as a PNG. *Above: the landing hero of a coffee subscription, with its mobile signup form beside it.* ### `claude-design-system`: design systems A design system is tokens, a README brand book, component previews, fonts and asset groups. In the editor you browse and edit colors, type, spacing, radii, shadows, components and assets. Import one from a component library and its previews are the real components, live and interactive. Decks and canvases can install it: their editors' Theme and color menus then offer its colors and text styles. *Above: Nimbus, a small design system for a weather app.* ### `claude-data`: data‑backed dashboards A dashboard is datasets (CSV, TSV or JSON) and a page of charts, numbers and tables computed from them. The charts are live, and the Sources panel traces every number back to its rows. Give the agent a newer export and it swaps the file in; the page recomputes every number. Numbers, dates and labels follow your language. *Above: a year of daily X account analytics, with sample data.* ### `claude-motion`: motion films A film is a folder of documents the agent writes with the skill's script, scene by scene, while you watch it fill in the player. Everything on screen is code, a pure function of time, so a change is a rewrite of that moment, not a re-render you wait for. Retype a line, drag a scene's length, change the style in **Tweaks** or a line's weight, size, spacing and color there, or comment on a moment and send it to the agent. A narrated film carries a voice track: one take a scene, from a speech provider of yours or recorded by you, with the motion timed to the words and captions that follow them; a recorded track can play as the music bed. Export MP4 or GIF from the player, or `export` from the command line (Chrome needed; `record`, for filming a page of your own product, also needs ffmpeg). For a film with a point to make, ask for `motion-director`, which directs and uses `claude-motion` as its crew. *Above: the film that introduces Motion, made with Motion.* ### `claude-whiteboard`: whiteboards A board is a space for laying out thinking in the form it needs: a diagram, a flow, a map of ideas, a plan, a comparison, a drawn explanation or a small working embed. The agent writes it as elements (blocks, sections, text, arrows, tables, sticky notes, drawings and embeds) into the board's own store with the skill's script, and the editor shows each one as it lands. Move and resize things, type, draw with the pen, add sections, sticky notes, shapes and stickers from the toolbar, and drop a video on the board to play there; what you change goes into the same store. Comment on an item, a spot or an area and send it to the agent, which changes the board and replies. Everyone on a share link sees the others' cursors and changes live, has cursor chat and can follow one another's view. The **Share** panel's **Export** tab saves the board as a PNG. One server serves every board on this computer. *Above: a board that explains how a change ships.* ### Run the editors Each `SKILL.md` keeps the type's original instructions nearly word for word; only the Artifact tool calls are swapped for local ones. That tool lives inside each skill as `scripts/artifact.mjs` (Node 20+, the dashboard's, Motion's and the whiteboard's Node 22+; nothing to install). The agent runs it for you; by hand: ```bash node skills/claude-slides/scripts/artifact.mjs open designs/q3-review # start the editor, print its URL node skills/claude-slides/scripts/artifact.mjs check designs/q3-review # validate the files node skills/claude-slides/scripts/artifact.mjs upload designs/q3-review hero.jpg # store an image, print its /_blob/ URL node skills/claude-slides/scripts/artifact.mjs list # find design systems on disk node skills/claude-slides/scripts/artifact.mjs share designs/q3-review # open it to the local network, print a link per role ``` A dashboard, a film or a board is written through the same script (`write-db`, `read-db`, `upload`, `check`, `open`) into its own store under `/db/`. Each skill runs its own local server, and everything in `scripts/` ships prebuilt: plain JavaScript that runs on Node alone, with nothing to install or build. --- ## DeepSeek Harness plugins The six editor skills also come as [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins, published on npm. Each plugin carries its skill exactly as this repo publishes it, prebuilt editor included, so Claude Design and the other editors run on your DeepSeek agent. | npm package | Adds | Version | |---|---|---| | [`dsh-claude-slides`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-slides) | `/claude-slides`: slide decks | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-slides)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-slides) | | [`dsh-claude-design`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-design) | `/claude-design`: a canvas of artboards | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-design)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-design) | | [`dsh-claude-design-system`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-design-system) | `/claude-design-system`: design systems | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-design-system)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-design-system) | | [`dsh-claude-data`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-data) | `/claude-data`: data‑backed dashboards | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-data)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-data) | | [`dsh-claude-motion`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-motion) | `/claude-motion`: motion films | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-motion)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-motion) | | [`dsh-claude-whiteboard`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-whiteboard) | `/claude-whiteboard`: whiteboards | [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-claude-whiteboard)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-whiteboard) | In the slides, canvas and design-system editors, on the dashboard page, in the Motion player and on a whiteboard, a comment goes straight to the agent: whenever the agent opens an editor, the plugin waits for comments. Mark up the page, tick **Send to Agent**, and the agent wakes up, reads your comment, makes the change and replies in the comment thread. The comment also shows in the chat as a card. The plugins also add **Artifacts** to the app's left sidebar: every deck, canvas, design system, dashboard, film and board the agent has opened, each with a thumbnail, as a grid or a list, with search, sort and filters. Click one and the app goes back to the conversation that made it and opens the editor in the right sidebar. A tile at the top starts a new session with the input filled in for that kind of thing, so the right skill loads. ### Install from npm All you need is the DeepSeek Harness desktop app: no repo to clone, nothing to build. The app downloads the plugin from npm (or from the npmmirror registry when npm is out of reach) and runs it on the Node.js it ships with. 1. In the app, open **Plugins** → **Add plugin**. 2. Enter a package name from the table, such as `dsh-claude-design`, in **Package name or address**, and click **Install**. If the plugin's switch is off, turn it on. Repeat for each plugin you want. 3. Quit and reopen the app, then start a new session and ask for a deck, a canvas, a design system, a dashboard, a film or a whiteboard, or type `/claude-design` (`/claude-slides` and so on). To install into a CLI profile, such as `web`: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-claude-design ``` **From the Discover tab.** The app's experimental Discover tab can list the plugins, install them with a click and show when an update is out. On the Plugins page, click **More** beside **Experimental plugins** and switch on **Custom plugin markets**; then in **Discover**, click **Add index source** and add this index: ```text https://jimliu.github.io/baoyu-design/dsh-plugins/index.json ``` **Updating.** When a new version is out, the **Artifacts** row in the sidebar gets an **Update** label, and the top of the Artifacts page says what changed: **Update all** updates the plugins together, with nothing to uninstall, and each plugin has its own **Update** if you want just one. Versions 2.9.2 and earlier don't offer it: from DeepSeek Harness 0.2.2, click **Update to x** on the plugin's page. On older apps, uninstall the plugin on the Plugins page, install it again, then quit and reopen the app. For a day after a release, adding by name still gets the previous version; Discover gets the new one right away, and so does entering the name with the version, such as `dsh-claude-design@2.4.0` (the versions are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md)). Had `dsh-claude-dashboard`? It is now `dsh-claude-data`, and the Artifacts page offers the move as an update ([details](dsh-plugins/README.md#update)). Each plugin brings along [`dsh-claude-artifacts`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-claude-artifacts), the part they share: the Artifacts page, and comments reaching the agent. To have a skill only in one agent preset, see [Keep a skill to one preset](dsh-plugins/README.md#keep-a-skill-to-one-preset). Running Harness on one computer and using it from another (`dsh web` on a server, opened on your laptop or phone)? Open your work from **Artifacts**: the plugin opens the editor at an address that device reaches, with you as its owner. See [Use it from another device](dsh-plugins/README.md#use-it-from-another-device). A workspace that has its own copy of a skill (in `.agents/skills/` or `.dsh/skills/`) uses that copy instead of the plugin's. Step by step, with installing from a folder, uninstalling and what to do when something doesn't work: [`dsh-plugins/`](dsh-plugins/README.md). --- ## ChatGPT plugins The same skills also come as plugins for the ChatGPT desktop app and Codex: [Baoyu Slides](chatgpt-plugins/baoyu-slides/), [Baoyu Canvas](chatgpt-plugins/baoyu-canvas/), [Baoyu Design System](chatgpt-plugins/baoyu-design-system/), [Baoyu Data](chatgpt-plugins/baoyu-data/), [Baoyu Motion](chatgpt-plugins/baoyu-motion/) (with `motion-director` and `dataviz`), [Baoyu Whiteboard](chatgpt-plugins/baoyu-whiteboard/) and [Baoyu Dataviz](chatgpt-plugins/baoyu-dataviz/). Add this repository as a marketplace, then install the ones you want: ```bash codex plugin marketplace add JimLiu/baoyu-design --sparse .agents/plugins --sparse chatgpt-plugins ``` ```bash codex plugin add baoyu-slides@baoyu-design ``` The editors run on your computer, so opening one needs local network, which the default sandbox blocks: approve it if the app asks, or use a permission mode that allows it. Step by step, with installing from the app's Plugins Directory and updating: [chatgpt-plugins/README.md](chatgpt-plugins/README.md). --- ## Why run it locally - **Free yourself from the website.** You get the vast majority of `claude.ai/design`'s capabilities without ever leaving your editor — same methodology, same craft standards, same output format. - **Best with Opus 5.5.** The skill is a long, demanding design brief; the stronger the model, the better the result. Pair it with **Claude Opus 5.5** for the best output, and it still works well on other capable models. - **Edit side by side with the agent.** Each editor runs on `localhost`; your edits save back into the same files the agent writes, so you can take turns. - **Work together, no cloud.** Share an editor on your local network with a link per role; others edit, comment or watch, and you decide who stays in. Version history shows who changed what and brings any version back. - **Everything is yours.** Output lands in `designs//` as plain files you can version, fork, export, or ship. --- ## Quick start Using the DeepSeek Harness app? You don't need this section: [install the plugins from npm](#install-from-npm). ### Prerequisites - A local agent — **[Cursor](https://cursor.com)**, **[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)**, **[Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/)**, or any of the 70+ agents the installer supports (Cline, Roo Code, GitHub Copilot…). Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex have first‑class tool references inside the skill. - **Claude Opus 5.5** selected as the model, for best results. - **Node.js**, for the `npx` installer below and for the artifact skills' editors (Node 20+, the dashboard, Motion and the whiteboard Node 22+). ### Install **Recommended — the `skills` CLI.** [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) (from Vercel Labs) reads this repo, finds the skills under `skills/`, and drops them into the right folder for whatever agent it detects: ```bash # Install into the current project (auto‑detects your agent) npx skills add JimLiu/baoyu-design # …or install globally, for every project npx skills add JimLiu/baoyu-design -g # Target a specific agent explicitly npx skills add JimLiu/baoyu-design --agent claude-code npx skills add JimLiu/baoyu-design --agent cursor npx skills add JimLiu/baoyu-design --agent codex # Just list what's in the repo first npx skills add JimLiu/baoyu-design --list # Install only some of the skills npx skills add JimLiu/baoyu-design --skill claude-slides --skill claude-data ``` It installs to `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code and `.agents/skills/` for Cursor/Codex-style agents (add `-g` for the `~/`‑level user install). ### Update If you installed with the `skills` CLI, update from the terminal: ```bash # Update one skill (the CLI prompts for the install scope) npx skills update claude-slides # Update the project-level or global install npx skills update claude-slides -p -y npx skills update claude-slides -g -y ``` `upgrade` is also supported as an alias. You can also run `npx skills update` to update all installed skills. After updating, restart Claude Code (or start a new agent session) so the refreshed skill files are loaded. **Alternative — hand the repo URL to your agent.** Don't want to install anything? Paste the URL into chat and let the agent fetch the skill itself: > Read https://github.com/JimLiu/baoyu-design and follow its `skills/claude-slides/SKILL.md` to make a 10‑slide deck from this PRD. The agent clones or fetches the repo, loads `SKILL.md`, and proceeds — perfect for a one‑off. ### Use it Once a skill is installed (or fetched), ask for what you want (*"Make a 12‑slide deck from this PRD"*, *"Turn this CSV into a dashboard"*) or call one by name: `/claude-slides`, `/claude-design`, `/claude-design-system`, `/claude-data`, `/claude-motion`, `/motion-director` or `/claude-whiteboard` in Claude Code, `$claude-slides` and so on in Codex. The agent writes the files under `designs//`, starts the editor, and gives you its `http://127.0.0.1` URL. --- ## Example prompts - *"Make a claude-slides deck for the Q3 review, then export it to PowerPoint."* - *"Put a landing page and its phone version side by side on a claude-design canvas."* - *"Turn the Chakra UI component library into a design system with live component previews."* - *"Turn this analytics CSV into a dashboard that compares the last 28 days with the 28 before."* - *"Use motion-director to turn this launch post into a 60‑second narrated film."* - *"Map out our onboarding flow on a claude-whiteboard board, with the open questions as sticky notes."* For best results, **give it design context** — a screenshot, a UI kit, a design system, or a codebase. Starting from real context is the single biggest lever on quality; the skill will ask for it if you don't provide it. --- ## Credits & license This project repackages **Anthropic**'s claude.ai Artifact types and design skills so they can run on local agents. It is an independent, community effort and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Repackaged and maintained by **Jim Liu 宝玉**. The repository holds material under three sets of terms, set out in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md): - **The maintainer's own work** (the local command line and editor server, the local comments, the DeepSeek Harness plugin code, the docs) is under the [MIT License](LICENSE). - **Material from Anthropic** stays Anthropic's and is not under the MIT License; this project grants no license to it. That covers the skill instructions and reference docs adapted from the Artifact types, the `dataviz` skil

# @local/dsh-lazy-plugins

按需加载市场插件的 Host 插件（v3.14.4）。本地没有的插件，在任务需要时由 agent 从市场索引解析、安装、**当场可用**；用完可以卸载移除。
默认激活方式为 `proxy`：插件真正生效，但它的工具**不进模型可见的 tools[]**，因此不会打碎提示词前缀缓存。

## Claude 式形态（v3.14）

常驻只注入一句（152 字符 / ≈38 tokens），细节在注册的 **skill** 正文里，模型需要时才加载：

- `skills/lazy-plugins/SKILL.md`：frontmatter（name/description/whenToUse）+ 正文（何时用、三个动作、判定规则、示例、注意）；
- 插件 apply 时读文件并 `ctx.get("skills").register({ name, description, whenToUse, content, invocation, provider, source: "runtime" })`；
- 实测：工具描述 **936 → 152 字符（234 → 38 tokens）**，skill 出现在模型技能目录并能按需加载（`advise.skill = ["lazy-plugins:runtime"]`）。

## 工具（模型可见面）

只有一个工具 `lazy_plugin`：

| 动作 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `ensure` | **给一句需求**，自动挑出最匹配的插件并在判定明确时直接安装（默认走 proxy） |
| `suggest` | 任务句 → 候选排序（IDF 加权，可翻页） |
| `search` | 关键词检索（可翻页，去重 + 隐藏装不上的条目） |
| `resolve` | 看一个包的版本、安装目标（npm / git）、兼容性 |
| `load` | 安装指定版本并激活（已装则只做启用） |
| `reload` | 停用→启用，让新版本模块生效（不重启 dsh） |
| `unload` | 停用但保留安装 |
| `release` | 停用并移除 |
| `uninstall` | 直接移除 |
| `list` | 已装清单、懒加载记录、常驻判定与使用分、索引缓存状态 |
| `refresh` | 立刻刷新索引（条件请求）并预热常驻插件 |
| `advise` | 体检：工具面 tokens、缓存命中率、使用分、隐藏工具、建议 |
| `invoke` | 调用被 proxy 隐藏的工具（`{tool, arguments}`） |

## 模型调用准则

1. **有需求先 `ensure`**：一句话描述要做什么，它负责挑；判定不明确时才回候选让人选。
2. 想自己挑就用 `suggest` / `search`，按「描述最匹配」优先，其次热度；可 `offset` 翻页。
3. **优先最新版本**：不传 `version` 就是索引默认（最新）版本。
4. **一次装一个**，用完 `release`，不要囤。
5. `load` 回 `installable:false` 说明该条目任何 registry 都装不上（索引里有这类幽灵条目），换候选，别重试同一个。
6. 没有 `force` 参数：base bundle 一律拒绝停用/移除，常用插件只提示不阻断。

## 激活方式与提示词缓存

工具是 API 独立字段 `tools[]`、按名字排序，缓存断点在最后一个工具，所以**可见工具集一变，前缀就重建**。

| `activate` | 当场能用 | 前缀缓存 | 做法 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy`（默认） | ✅ | ✅ 不变 | 插件激活，工具被 **per-agent `tools.restrict`** 藏起来，经 `invoke` 调用 |
| `now` | ✅ | ❌ 重建一次 | 工具原生进入 `tools[]` |
| `session` | ❌ | ✅ | 只安装，之后 `load` 一次启用（无下载，约 0.1–0.5 s） |

`invoke` 之所以能调用隐藏工具：`tools.execute()` 在 host 作用域执行，而 `restrict` 只作用于 agent 作用域（实测：`visibleForAgent: false` / `visibleGlobally: true` / `executeWithoutAgent: ok`）。
屏蔽落盘在 `hidden.json`，启动时重新打上；插件卸载后失效名字会自动剔除；插件异步注册的工具由 1.2 s / 3.5 s / 7 s 三次补扫兜住。

## 检索与自动选取

- **候选池**：`limit × 3`，先按相关性排序，再 `enrich`、过滤不可装、按安装目标合并近重复（`dsh-voice-7` / `dsh-voice-13` → `dsh-voice`，带 `variants`）。
- **IDF 加权**：`idf = ln(1 + N/(1+df))`，命中按 `idf × 字段权重`（name 3 / title 2 / description 2）累加，`dsh`/`plugin` 这类全库词不再决定排序。
- **自动选取守卫**：`ensure` 只在 `top ≥ autoSelectScore(40)` **且** `top ≥ 第二名 × autoSelectMargin(1.5)` 时才装，否则回 `needs-choice` + 候选；`auto:false` 只报告不装。
- **阈值是实测校准出来的**（31 条真实需求语料）：`40/1.3` 的自动安装精度只有 **0.636**（11 次装错 4 次），`40/1.5` 提升到 **0.80**（recall 0.367→0.167）；没有参数组合能到 0.90，所以默认偏保守，模型多看候选是更便宜的错误。
- **git-pinned 条目**（当前占 52.5%）判为可装、不走 npm 探测；`source` 字段直接回 `npm` / `git`。

## 常驻（resident）怎么算

三路来源（社区做法见 CREDITS.md）：

| 来源 | 判定 | 效果 |
|---|---|---|
| `base` | `availability !== 'profile'` 且**当前启用**的 bundle | 硬拒绝 `unload/release/uninstall` |
| `explicit` | `config.resident` | 只加提示，不阻断 |
| `auto` | `score >= residentScore(3)` | 只加提示，不阻断 |

```
score = 1.0·Σ_loads + 0.3·Σ_manualEnables + (base ? 1000 : 0)   每项 × 0.5^(Δ/14天)
```

只写本机 `~/.dsh/cache/dsh-lazy-plugins/usage.json`，不联网、不上报。

## 索引与缓存

- **拉取**：单次尝试只等首字节 3 s，失败转镜像；源顺序 = profile 索引 → `indexMirrors`。
- **缓存优先**：磁盘副本直接返回，后台条件请求热更新（304 = 0 字节）；断网时旧副本仍可用。
- **描述表**：索引自身描述覆盖率 ≥80% 时**直接投影**（零额外请求）；否则按 `descriptionSources` 拉 sidecar/旧文档。
- **刷新触发**：启动一次、**打开插件面板一次**（client 半调用 `GET /lazy-plugins/refresh?src=panel`，60 s 节流）、每天保底一次、手动 `refresh`。
- **client 半**：`client.js` + `package.json` 的 `dsh.client{platform:web,immediately:true}` + `exports['./client']`，用 `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})` 形态（无需构建）。页面挂载即调 `GET /lazy-plugins/refresh?src=mount`，点进插件面板再调 `?src=panel`，页面侧 60 s 节流 + `sessionStorage`，失败只 `console.debug`。
- **自愈（重要，给后续维护者）**：`link:` 安装的包在**主机进程启动早于 `dsh.client` 声明**时，会被上游 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules` 的 `ClientModuleRegistry.pkgMeta` 缓存成 `null`（该缓存**没有任何失效路径**，`set_bundle false/true` 命中缓存、不够）。本插件在**启动后 `bootDelayMs` 自动一次**、以及显式 `POST /lazy-plugins/repair-client`（或 `GET /lazy-plugins/state?repair=1`）时自愈：删掉陈旧 `null` → 强制 `reconcile` 报变更 → `flush()`（内部 `compose()` + 通知）→ 图里出现本行。`GET /lazy-plugins/state` 本身**纯读、无副作用**。
- **自愈返回值**：`repair.attempted:false` + `why:"already in graph"` 是**幂等 no-op（已在图中，不是失败）**；真正的失败看 `repair.errors` 或 `repair.compose.error/failures`。
- **自愈的退出条件（必须遵守）**：这是**上游缺陷的 workaround**，不是本插件的功能。一旦 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules` 让 `pkgMeta` 的 key 带上 `package.json` 的 mtime/size、或暴露 `invalidate()`、或 `flush()` 前对 dirty 行强制重解析 —— 就**整段删除** `ensureClientRow` 及其三个触发点（启动定时器、`POST /lazy-plugins/repair-client`、`GET /state?repair=1`），此 README 对应段落一并删除。依据与建议修法见 `_tmp/panel-trigger/UPSTREAM-ISSUE.md`；`clientHalf.lastRepair.upstream` 字段也带同一句提示。
- **验证计数**：`state.panelPings`（过闸执行的刷新数）、`clientRequests`（含被节流的客户端调用）、`browserPings`（带 `Sec-Fetch-Mode`+浏览器 UA 的调用，`curl` 伪造不了）+ `lastBrowserPingFingerprint`、`lastBrowserPingSource`（`mount`/`panel`），以及 `clientHalf{inGraph,rows,graphRev,url,clientPath,lastRepair}`。
- 索引现状（2026-11-07 实测）：10,559 条、99.96% 带 zh 描述、52.5% git-pinned、166 个后缀名条目。

## 装前探测与别名

- npm 条目：并行 HEAD `<registry>/<name>/<version>`（命中 26–230 ms）；全 404 直接回 `installable:false`；超时/网络错判为未知，不挡安装。
- 别名：索引把重名条目改名成 `dsh-voice-8`，真实包名在 `title`。`load` 用 `title` 作第二候选，探测通过就装真名并回 `installedAs`。

## 可配置项

`cordis.patch.yml`（全部有默认值）：`defaultActivate`、`autoSelectScore`、`autoSelectMargin`、`autoSelectEnabled`、`resident`、`halfLifeDays`、`residentScore`、`fetchTimeoutMs`、`bodyTimeoutMs`、`refreshIntervalMs`、`dailyRefreshMs`、`panelThrottleMs`、`bootDelayMs`、`indexMirrors`、`descriptionSources`、`descriptionTtlMs`、`descriptionSearch`、`enrichDescriptions`、`enrichTimeoutMs`、`enrichRegistries`、`verifyInstall`、`probeFastMs`、`probeTimeoutMs`、`deferLoading`、`diskCache`、`cacheTtlMs`。

## 性能（本机实测）

| 场景 | 耗时 |
|---|---|
| 已装再 `load`（快路径） | 75–490 ms |
| 冷装小包（含探测+安装+激活） | 1.9–2.6 s |
| 冷装大包 / registry 抖动 | 3–5 s（个别 38 s，属上游 installBundle 抖动） |
| git-pinned 安装（`@lbxc/dsh-voice-input`） | 5.07 s |
| 索引冷拉 | ~1.0–1.7 s（gzip 约 300 KB–1 MB，随版本变化） |
| 索引 304 热更新 | 0.5–1.1 s / 0 字节 |
| 索引磁盘命中（新进程） | 42 ms |
| `search` / `suggest`（本地 10,559 条，含 IDF 扫描） | 10–30 ms |

`load` 结果带 `phases`（lookup/resolve/probe/install）与 `ms`；`advise.cache` 有命中率计数。

## 失败恢复

`reload` 是「先停用再启用」，启用失败会停在停用态 → 现在失败自动重试一次并回传 `diagnostic` + 修复提示（最常见成因：`cordis.patch.yml` 里 `@scope` 未加引号）。

## 数据边界

只做三件事：读市场索引、调 profile 的 `pluginManager`、返回结果。不写日志文件、不上报、不采集会话内容。

# dsh-market · DSH 插件市场索引（自动爬取）

为 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的「插件 → 发现」提供一份**自动生成、格式合规**的索引源。

- 主源（GitHub Pages，实测最稳）：`https://jingjiangze.github.io/dsh-market/index.json`
- 品牌域名（Cloudflare Pages）：`https://dsh.jiangjiangze.icu/index.json`
- 两个地址内容同源：都来自本仓库 `site/`，由 CI 生成后提交

## 加进 DSH

「插件 → 发现 → 添加索引源」，两个都加（互为主备）：

```
https://jingjiangze.github.io/dsh-market/index.json
https://dsh.jiangjiangze.icu/index.json
```

> 为什么主源选 GitHub Pages：2026-11-02 本机直连实测 **3/3 成功，0.61–0.81 s**；同一份索引走 Cloudflare Pages 自定义域名时 **3 次里 1 次卡在 25 s 只收到 538 B**、其余 3.8–17.5 s（CF 边缘境内无节点，直连不稳；走代理 2/2 成功 1.9–2.9 s）。DSH 的 fetch 超时是 15 s，所以把 Pages 当人读站点、把 GitHub Pages 当机器源，两边都不丢。

## 它是什么 / 不是什么

- 是：从 **npm 公共源**爬到的、**声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`** 且 `engines.dsh` 满足当前运行时的包的元数据清单（分类、多语言描述、图标直链、精确版本）。
- 不是：不是代码托管，不镜像任何包，不对任何插件背书。装什么、跑什么，以包本身为准。
- 索引里**只有元数据**：`source.type = npm`，安装走你本机 pnpm + 你自己的 registry 配置。

## 爬取与准入（`crawler/crawl.mjs`，零依赖）

```
node crawler/crawl.mjs --selftest     # 门禁自测（正例 + 反例）
node crawler/crawl.mjs                # 爬取并生成 dist/
```

两段式，先便宜后贵：

1. **发现**：`registry.npmjs.org` 关键词检索（`keywords:dsh-plugin`、`keywords:deepseek-harness`、`keywords:dsh`）。
2. **初筛**（每包 1 次 `/<name>/latest`）：必须声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`；不得含 `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`。
3. **定版**（入选包再取完整 packument）：取**最新稳定版**且满足 `engines.dsh`；未声明 `engines.dsh` 的一律**不收**（不猜"应该能跑"）；发布不足 `MIN_AGE_DAYS`（默认 3 天）的不收（pnpm 的 `minimumReleaseAge` 会扣住它们，写进索引用户也装不上）；许可为空或 `NOASSERTION`/`UNLICENSED` 的不收。

产出：

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `dist/index.json` | format 1 索引（DSH 唯一读的东西） |
| `dist/index.sidecar.json` | format 1 装不下的东西：`dist.integrity`、provenance、体积、生效的门禁 |
| `dist/rejections.json` | 每个被排除的包 + 原因（可复盘，不静默丢） |
| `dist/stats.json` | 候选数 / 初筛数 / 收录数 / 拒绝原因分布 / 索引字节数 / 耗时 |

环境变量：`NPM_REGISTRY`、`SEARCH_REGISTRY`、`DSH_RUNTIME_VERSION`、`MIN_AGE_DAYS`、`MAX_PLUGINS`、`MAX_CANDIDATES`、`CONCURRENCY`、`SEARCH_QUERIES`。

### 已知的爬取坑（踩过）

- **npmmirror 不支持 `keywords:` 语法**：`registry.npmmirror.com/-/v1/search?text=keywords:dsh-plugin` 返回 `total=0`，而 npmjs 返回约 11.9k。所以**发现阶段固定用 npmjs**；manifest 阶段可换镜像加速。
- **不能信 latest**：一个包可能同时有多个兼容版本，`latest` 未必兼容当前运行时，所以定版要读完整 packument。
- **未声明 `engines.dsh` ≠ 兼容**：DSH 的安装侧会用真实包的 `engines` + `peerDependencies` 再判一次，索引里谎报兼容比不收更伤口碑。

## 双语与分类

- 每个插件都有 `{en, zh}` 标题与简介，并被归到一个声明过的类别（9 类：safety / ui / media / integrations / memory / models / automation / devtools / other）。
- 中文来源优先级：**包自带 `locale/zh.json`** → **本仓库 `data/zh-overrides.json`**（可按 `version` 钉版）→ 兜底英文并标 `zh-fallback`（当前 0）。当前 38/38 双语：`zh-native` 13 + `zh-override` 25。
- 标签写明来源（`zh-native` / `zh-override` / `zh-fallback`），数量统计进 `dist/stats.json`。
- 分类规则在 `crawler/crawl.mjs` 的 `CATEGORY_RULES`，**必须带词边界**——裸子串会把 `inspired` 命中 `ide`、把主题插件误判成开发工具。
- 不编造翻译：没有机器翻译，全部来自作者 locale 或仓库内人工整理。
- **不在本机跑任何服务**：爬取、校验、发布都在 GitHub Actions；本地 `node crawler/crawl.mjs --dry-run` 只是一次性脚本。

## CI（三段流水线）

| 工作流 | 触发 | 做什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `crawl.yml` | 每 3 小时 + 手动 | 三分片采集 → 合并目录 → 生成多语言/浏览分片/资源 → **离线 + 在线发布门禁** → Git Data API 提交 `main` → 显式触发 `deploy` |
| `ci.yml` | 每次 push / 每个 PR | 门禁自测 → 官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index` 校验 → 页面预算与引用检查 → registry 回查 → `--dry-run` 冒烟（守住 main 与人工 PR） |
| `deploy.yml` | main 的 `site/**`、`dist/**` 变化，或由 crawl 派发 | 双端发布：GitHub Pages + Cloudflare Pages（`wrangler`） |
| `dependabot.yml` | 每周 | GitHub Actions 版本升级 PR（人工审） |

**发布纪律**：`crawl` 和 `translate` 共用 `catalog-publish` 并发组，避免两个写入者同时基于旧 `main` 创建提交；完整发布门禁在写入 `main` 前执行，push 触发的 `ci` 作为发布后回归检查。

**两个必须知道的 GitHub 行为**（都已在代码里绕过）：

1. **用仓库 `GITHUB_TOKEN` 写入 `main` 不会触发其它 workflow**（防递归）→ 所以 `crawl` 提交后显式 `gh workflow run deploy.yml`，不指望 push 事件。
2. 当前 `crawl` 走 Git Data API 直接写 `main`，不再创建 crawl PR；因此发布门禁必须在写入前执行，不能依赖 push 后才运行的 `ci` 来阻止错误版本上线。


`ci` 里的检查（`crawler/validate.mjs`）：

1. `parseMarketIndex()` —— 与 DSH 运行时同一份校验器，不是自己重写；
2. `site/index.json` 必须与 `dist/index.json` **逐字节一致**（防止发布物与验证物脱节）；
3. `site/index.html` < 1024 B，`style.css` 存在；
4. 页面里不允许出现 `127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `file://` / 内联图片字体；
5. 每条 plugin 的 `name@version` 在 registry 上真实存在、仍声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`，且 `engines.dsh` 与索引里写的一致（防止**索引漂移**——DSH 安装侧会用真实包再判一次兼容性）。

本地复现（不需要网络可加 `--offline`）：

```bash
npm i --no-save @deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index@0.2.1-rc.5
node crawler/crawl.mjs --selftest
node crawler/validate.mjs
node crawler/crawl.mjs --dry-run
```


## 已知限制

- **索引没有签名**：format 1 里没有 signature / digest 字段，DSH 不验签。篡改只能靠外部核对 `dist/index.json` 的 sha256（见每次提交与 `stats.json`）。
- **没有 upgrade 流程**：DSH 侧「有新版」只显示 `update-available`，升级 = 卸载 + 重装。
- **索引是单文档全量读**：超过 ~5k 条要考虑拆多源（官方口径：20k 条 ≈ 7.6 MiB，反序列化约 35 ms）。
- **只覆盖 npm**：不发布到 npm 的插件（只在 GitHub 的）暂不收录；后续可加 `source.type=git` + commit 固定。
- **不做安全审计**：门禁只保证「是个能装的 bundle、版本兼容、许可清楚、不跑安装脚本」，不代表代码安全。

# @local/dsh-session-reader

读取**其他** DSH 会话：列出来、跨会话检索、把某个会话的完整对话读出来。只读，无遥测。

## 为什么需要它

官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-session-search` 提供 5 个工具（`session_search` / `session_event_search` /
`session_trace` / `session_event_trace` / `session_event_read`），但它们依赖 `ctx.sessionQuery` 的**抽象 FTS 方法**
（`searchSessions` / `searchEvents`），而：

1. 该 FTS 后端在默认 profile 上不可用（本机实测 `~/.dsh/session-query.sqlite` 不存在，profile 也没有 `session-query` 行）；
2. 它的 SQLite FTS5 用 `unicode61` 分词器，**不切连续中文**，中文全文检索会漏。

本插件用**字面子串**在 JS 侧匹配：中文天然正确、英文大小写不敏感，且服务路径与磁盘回退共用同一条代码路径。

## 一个工具，三个动作

| action | 做什么 | 主要参数 |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | 最近会话：短 id、标题、创建/更新时间、agentPreset、消息数、cwd、live/origin/parent | `limit`（默认 10，最大 30） |
| `search` | 跨会话字面子串检索，返回命中会话 + 前后各 60 字片段 + 事件序号 | `query`（必填）、`session`（只搜这一个）、`limit`（默认 10，最大 30） |
| `read` | 读某个会话的完整对话 | `session`（必填，支持 8 位短 id / 唯一前缀 / `session-<uuid>`）、`limit`（尾部消息数，默认 20，最大 60）、`window`、`role` |

参数共 6 个（`action` / `session` / `query` / `limit` / `window` / `role`），工具描述 370 字符。

### `window` 的两种写法

- `"120-180"` 或 `"150"` —— 按**事件序号**取窗口（`read`）。
- `"offset:N"` —— 从 `nextCursor` 续读（任何动作）。`read` 的语义是「已从最新往回看过 N 条」。

### 输出上限

单次结果序列化后 ≤ **20 000 字节**；超出时从尾部裁剪，给 `truncated: true` + `nextCursor`（`offset:N`）。
`read` 里单条消息 > 2000 字会被截断并标记 `textTruncated: true` + `fullChars`（原始字数）。

## 数据来源（按优先级，代码里同样注释）

1. **Host 服务 `sessionQuery`**（可选，用 `ctx.get('sessionQuery')` 拿，没有也能加载）：
   - `listSessions(signal?)` → `SessionRecord[]`
   - `readSession(sessionId)` → `SessionLogSnapshot{session, inheritedEventCount, events}` —— **完整原始日志**
   - `readTitleSnapshots(ids, signal?)` → 标题
   - `listEvents(sessionId)` → 轻量事件记录（用于消息数与最后活动时间）
2. **磁盘回退**：`~/.dsh/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<sessionId>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`
   该文件是**多帧拼接的 zstd**（实测一例：74 帧 / 727 578 B / 126 事件），`zstd -d` 只会吐出第一条记录。
   本插件按魔数 `28 b5 2f fd` 逐帧贪心解压，再按行解析 `{type, seq, time, data}`。
3. 两者都不可用 → 返回 `{ unavailable: true, reason, tried }`，不抛裸错。

### 刻意不用 `readSurface()`

`readSurface()` 返回的是**模型当前视图**，compaction 会把旧事件替换成 `compaction/summary`，原文在 surface 上会消失。
只有 `readSession()`（完整日志）才拿得到被压缩掉的内容。这一判断借鉴 `dsh-archive-viewer@1.1.5` 的
`docs/INTERNALS.md:44`，见 CREDITS.md。

## 只读保证

- 只调用 `readSession` / `listSessions` / `listEvents` / `readTitleSnapshots` 这类读方法，以及 `node:fs` 的 `readFile` / `open(r)` / `readdir` / `stat`。
- 源码里没有任何 `writeFile` / `unlink` / `rename` / `mkdir` 调用（有机械测试断言，见下）。
- 没有网络调用、没有遥测、没有上报。

## 自测

机械验收（本机真实会话数据 + 服务桩）：

```bash
node _tmp/session-audit-session-plugin-audit/test-reader.mjs   # 磁盘路径 + 服务路径
node _tmp/session-audit-session-plugin-audit/test-edge.mjs     # 20KB 预算 / 截断 / 游标 / id 形态 / 无损 JSON / 无遥测
```

证据与真实返回片段：`_tmp/session-audit-session-plugin-audit/VERIFY.md`。

**PENDING**：真正装进 profile 后的端到端（真机）验证——那一步由 Lead 装载后执行；截至交付，服务路径只在镜像
`sessionQuery` 签名的桩上验证过（方法名、入参、出参形状一致，但未连真实服务）。

# dsh-market · DSH 插件市场索引（自动爬取）

为 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的「插件 → 发现」提供一份**自动生成、格式合规**的索引源。

- 主源（GitHub Pages，实测最稳）：`https://jingjiangze.github.io/dsh-market/index.json`
- 品牌域名（Cloudflare Pages）：`https://dsh.jiangjiangze.icu/index.json`
- 两个地址内容同源：都来自本仓库 `site/`，由 CI 生成后提交

## 加进 DSH

「插件 → 发现 → 添加索引源」，两个都加（互为主备）：

```
https://jingjiangze.github.io/dsh-market/index.json
https://dsh.jiangjiangze.icu/index.json
```

> 为什么主源选 GitHub Pages：2026-11-02 本机直连实测 **3/3 成功，0.61–0.81 s**；同一份索引走 Cloudflare Pages 自定义域名时 **3 次里 1 次卡在 25 s 只收到 538 B**、其余 3.8–17.5 s（CF 边缘境内无节点，直连不稳；走代理 2/2 成功 1.9–2.9 s）。DSH 的 fetch 超时是 15 s，所以把 Pages 当人读站点、把 GitHub Pages 当机器源，两边都不丢。

## 它是什么 / 不是什么

- 是：从 **npm 公共源**爬到的、**声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`** 且 `engines.dsh` 满足当前运行时的包的元数据清单（分类、多语言描述、图标直链、精确版本）。
- 不是：不是代码托管，不镜像任何包，不对任何插件背书。装什么、跑什么，以包本身为准。
- 索引里**只有元数据**：`source.type = npm`，安装走你本机 pnpm + 你自己的 registry 配置。

## 爬取与准入（`crawler/crawl.mjs`，零依赖）

```
node crawler/crawl.mjs --selftest     # 门禁自测（正例 + 反例）
node crawler/crawl.mjs                # 爬取并生成 dist/
```

两段式，先便宜后贵：

1. **发现**：`registry.npmjs.org` 关键词检索（`keywords:dsh-plugin`、`keywords:deepseek-harness`、`keywords:dsh`）。
2. **初筛**（每包 1 次 `/<name>/latest`）：必须声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`；不得含 `preinstall`/`install`/`postinstall`。
3. **定版**（入选包再取完整 packument）：取**最新稳定版**且满足 `engines.dsh`；未声明 `engines.dsh` 的一律**不收**（不猜"应该能跑"）；发布不足 `MIN_AGE_DAYS`（默认 3 天）的不收（pnpm 的 `minimumReleaseAge` 会扣住它们，写进索引用户也装不上）；许可为空或 `NOASSERTION`/`UNLICENSED` 的不收。

产出：

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `dist/index.json` | format 1 索引（DSH 唯一读的东西） |
| `dist/index.sidecar.json` | format 1 装不下的东西：`dist.integrity`、provenance、体积、生效的门禁 |
| `dist/rejections.json` | 每个被排除的包 + 原因（可复盘，不静默丢） |
| `dist/stats.json` | 候选数 / 初筛数 / 收录数 / 拒绝原因分布 / 索引字节数 / 耗时 |

环境变量：`NPM_REGISTRY`、`SEARCH_REGISTRY`、`DSH_RUNTIME_VERSION`、`MIN_AGE_DAYS`、`MAX_PLUGINS`、`MAX_CANDIDATES`、`CONCURRENCY`、`SEARCH_QUERIES`。

### 已知的爬取坑（踩过）

- **npmmirror 不支持 `keywords:` 语法**：`registry.npmmirror.com/-/v1/search?text=keywords:dsh-plugin` 返回 `total=0`，而 npmjs 返回约 11.9k。所以**发现阶段固定用 npmjs**；manifest 阶段可换镜像加速。
- **不能信 latest**：一个包可能同时有多个兼容版本，`latest` 未必兼容当前运行时，所以定版要读完整 packument。
- **未声明 `engines.dsh` ≠ 兼容**：DSH 的安装侧会用真实包的 `engines` + `peerDependencies` 再判一次，索引里谎报兼容比不收更伤口碑。

## 站点（`site/`）

- 首页第一屏是**索引源卡片**（渐变描边 + 外发光，纯 CSS）：「由 DSH 制作」徽章、**全部 / 国内 / 国际**三个索引源切换、源地址 + 一键复制。
- `index.html` 690 B；`style.css` / `app.js` 为**同源**资源（Pages 直接提供，部署即生效）。第三方图标仍走 jsDelivr 的 npm 直链（npm 版本不可变，不存在缓存问题）。
- 页脚：交流 QQ 1689170897。
- **多语言**：右上角切换 中文 / English / 日本語 / 한국어 / Русский；ja/ko/ru 由 CI 里的 Google Translate 生成（`crawler/translate.mjs`，按内容哈希缓存，失败即跳过不发布）。
- 卡片**点击打开详情**：中英对照 + 类别/版本/作者/发布/来源/包名 + 安装命令一键复制；卡片本身不再放「主页」按钮（链接在详情里）。

## 索引源：一个链接就够了

| 索引源 | 内容 | 国内实测 |
|---|---|---|
| **`index.zh.json`** | 全部 1 万余条，中英双语（推荐加这一个） | 4.3 MB，**gzip 后 1.08 MB / 1.8 秒** |
| `index.<lang>.json` | en / ja / ko / ru，同一份目录的其它语言 | 各 4.3–4.8 MB |
| `index.json` | 五语合并文档（站点与工具用，最大） | 11.6 MB，gzip 2.2 MB / 24 秒 |

**关键事实（实测）**：GitHub Pages 对 JSON 走 `Content-Encoding: gzip`，所以 4.3 MB 的文件实际只传 1.08 MB。用不带 `Accept-Encoding` 的 `curl` 测会得到「40–88 秒」的假象。

不建议、也不需要的做法（都验证过不可用）：
- ModelScope 数据集 URL：`/resolve/` 与 API 都 **302 → cdn-lfs-cn-1**，DSH 的加载器拒绝重定向；
- 品牌域 `dsh.jiangjiangze.icu`：国内被限速到约 4 KB/s；
- jsDelivr 镜像：该路径返回 **403**；
- 分片（多链接）：能满足速度，但配置要写 6 条，已撤掉；
- Cloudflare Worker：明确不使用。

## 双语与分类

- 每个插件都有 `{en, zh}` 标题与简介，并被归到一个声明过的类别（9 类：safety / ui / media / integrations / memory / models / automation / devtools / other）。
- 中文来源优先级：**包自带 `locale/zh.json`** → **本仓库 `data/zh-overrides.json`**（可按 `version` 钉版）→ 兜底英文并标 `zh-fallback`（当前 0）。当前 38/38 双语：`zh-native` 13 + `zh-override` 25。
- 标签写明来源（`zh-native` / `zh-override` / `zh-fallback`），数量统计进 `dist/stats.json`。
- 分类规则在 `crawler/crawl.mjs` 的 `CATEGORY_RULES`，**必须带词边界**——裸子串会把 `inspired` 命中 `ide`、把主题插件误判成开发工具。
- 不编造翻译：没有机器翻译，全部来自作者 locale 或仓库内人工整理。
- **不在本机跑任何服务**：爬取、校验、发布都在 GitHub Actions；本地 `node crawler/crawl.mjs --dry-run` 只是一次性脚本。

## CI（三段流水线）

| 工作流 | 触发 | 做什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `crawl.yml` | 每 3 小时 + 手动 | 三分片采集 → 合并目录 → 生成多语言/浏览分片/资源 → **离线 + 在线发布门禁** → Git Data API 提交 `main` → 显式触发 `deploy` |
| `ci.yml` | 每次 push / 每个 PR | 门禁自测 → 官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index` 校验 → 页面预算与引用检查 → registry 回查 → `--dry-run` 冒烟（守住 main 与人工 PR） |
| `deploy.yml` | main 的 `site/**`、`dist/**` 变化，或由 crawl 派发 | 双端发布：GitHub Pages + Cloudflare Pages（`wrangler`） |
| `dependabot.yml` | 每周 | GitHub Actions 版本升级 PR（人工审） |

**发布纪律**：`crawl` 和 `translate` 共用 `catalog-publish` 并发组，避免两个写入者同时基于旧 `main` 创建提交；完整发布门禁在写入 `main` 前执行，push 触发的 `ci` 作为发布后回归检查。

**两个必须知道的 GitHub 行为**（都已在代码里绕过）：

1. **用仓库 `GITHUB_TOKEN` 写入 `main` 不会触发其它 workflow**（防递归）→ 所以 `crawl` 提交后显式 `gh workflow run deploy.yml`，不指望 push 事件。
2. 当前 `crawl` 走 Git Data API 直接写 `main`，不再创建 crawl PR；因此发布门禁必须在写入前执行，不能依赖 push 后才运行的 `ci` 来阻止错误版本上线。


`ci` 里的检查（`crawler/validate.mjs`）：

1. `parseMarketIndex()` —— 与 DSH 运行时同一份校验器，不是自己重写；
2. `site/index.json` 必须与 `dist/index.json` **逐字节一致**（防止发布物与验证物脱节）；
3. `site/index.html` < 1024 B，`style.css` 存在；
4. 页面里不允许出现 `127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `file://` / 内联图片字体；
5. 每条 plugin 的 `name@version` 在 registry 上真实存在、仍声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`，且 `engines.dsh` 与索引里写的一致（防止**索引漂移**——DSH 安装侧会用真实包再判一次兼容性）。

本地复现（不需要网络可加 `--offline`）：

```bash
npm i --no-save @deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-market-index@0.2.1-rc.5
node crawler/crawl.mjs --selftest
node crawler/validate.mjs
node crawler/crawl.mjs --dry-run
```


## 已知限制

- **索引没有签名**：format 1 里没有 signature / digest 字段，DSH 不验签。篡改只能靠外部核对 `dist/index.json` 的 sha256（见每次提交与 `stats.json`）。
- **没有 upgrade 流程**：DSH 侧「有新版」只显示 `update-available`，升级 = 卸载 + 重装。
- **索引是单文档全量读**：超过 ~5k 条要考虑拆多源（官方口径：20k 条 ≈ 7.6 MiB，反序列化约 35 ms）。
- **只覆盖 npm**：不发布到 npm 的插件（只在 GitHub 的）暂不收录；后续可加 `source.type=git` + commit 固定。
- **不做安全审计**：门禁只保证「是个能装的 bundle、版本兼容、许可清楚、不跑安装脚本」，不代表代码安全。

## 许可

本仓库的爬虫与站点代码以 **GPL-3.0-or-later** 授权，全文见根目录 [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)。

索引里的条目版权归各包作者：本仓库只写元数据，不分发任何包的代码或素材，插件图标一律从上**游地址外链加载而不打包**。第三方数据与素材的边界见 [`NOTICE`](NOTICE)。

# AI Terminal Pet bridge for DeepSeek Harness

A Host-only Cordis bundle that reports DeepSeek Harness session state to the
AI Terminal Pet desktop overlay.

## What it does

| Harness event | Overlay state |
| --- | --- |
| `turn/start`, `agent/inbox/claimed`, `agent/status` running | `working` |
| `tool/call` | `tool_use` |
| `approval/asked`, `approval/request` | `waiting_permission` |
| `tool/result` with error, `command/done` error, `agent/error` | `error` |
| `turn/end`, `command/done` success | `idle` |
| Harness process exit | `closed` |

The overlay then plays an alert tone and shows a tray balloon on those
transitions, and its one-click jump button targets the Harness window.

## Protocol source

This bundle contains **no** pipe-name, state-set or snapshot logic of its own.
It loads the official protocol module from
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\protocol.js`, which `scripts/install.ps1` copies from
`reporters/protocol.js` and verifies by SHA256 on every install. All reports
are fire-and-forget; a missing overlay never affects Harness.

Session id = Harness `session.header.id`; `pid` is a synthetic
`stableProcessId`, `parentPid` is the real Harness process id. Sessions are
closed explicitly on exit so the overlay does not accumulate ghosts.

## Install into DeepSeek Harness

The `desktop` profile is managed exclusively by the Electron application (the
`dsh` CLI refuses it), so install through the in-app plugin manager. In a
Harness conversation, ask:

```
Use plugin_manager with action install_bundle and target
"%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\bundles\ai-terminal-pet-bridge"
```

That string is pasted into the in-app manager, so the environment variable form is intended:
%LOCALAPPDATA% resolves per user, and a hard-coded C:\Users\<name>\... would be wrong on
every other machine. If the manager does not expand variables, substitute your own profile path.

That directory is a copy of this package, refreshed by `scripts/install.ps1`.
Installing links the local directory into the profile and applies
`cordis.patch.yml`; restart Harness if the manager reports `restart-required`.
Do not hand-edit the profile's `package.json` or `cordis.patch.yml`: the
desktop profile runs pnpm on startup and would discard manual edits.

To verify, start a Harness task and run:

```
"%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
```

A `deepseek-harness` session should appear and change state as the task runs.
`plugin_manager` with `remove_bundle` removes it.

## Files

- `index.js` — Host plugin (`apply(ctx, config)` + cleanup disposer)
- `cordis.patch.yml` — loader `insert:` row
- `locale/{en,zh}.json` — display metadata
- `icon.svg` — plugin-manager icon

# ai-terminal-pet

Stop glancing across terminal windows to track agent states. It costs one small executable with no account and no cloud.

![ai-terminal-pet](docs/assets/hero.png)

![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-blue) ![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/go-1.23-00ADD8) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.0.7-blue)
![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green) ![Size](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-4.17%20MiB-blue) ![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-3-informational) ![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-206-brightgreen) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-ai-terminal-pet?label=dsh%20plugin)

> 🇬🇧 [English](#english)  ·  🇨🇳 [中文](#中文)

---

## English

### The problem

You run Claude Code, OpenCode, or Antigravity in multiple terminal windows at once. A background task prompts for permission to execute a tool, but you are focused in another window and never notice the prompt.

Fourteen minutes later, you switch back only to discover that your build has been sitting idle the entire time. Glancing across multiple terminal tabs wastes focus and breaks your concentration.

ai-terminal-pet anchors a 56px strip to the screen edge. It aggregates your sessions in real time, pulses when an agent needs permission, and displays which project is waiting and for how long.

The table below contrasts the everyday workflow before and after using the overlay:

| Context | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Multiple terminals | Four terminal windows open; you lose track of which window needs attention. | One 56px strip on the edge of the screen aggregates every active session. |
| Blocked build | You find out a build was blocked on a permission prompt fourteen minutes ago. | The overlay pulses immediately and shows which project is waiting and for how long. |
| Context switching | You click across tabs to check whether builds and tasks are still running. | A single glance reveals current states without touching your keyboard or mouse. |

### What it looks like

![Demo](docs/assets/demo.gif)
*The actual sequence: a session blocks on a permission prompt and the strip breathes, hovering unfolds the session list, and clicking the arrow at the end of the waiting row brings that terminal forward. Frames are rasterized from the shipped renderer; the ring stands in for the click, since a layered window draws no cursor.*

![Compact strip](docs/assets/overlay-compact.png)
*Compact strip: pulsing state orb with status glyph, session count, state word, and waiting project name.*

![Expanded list](docs/assets/overlay-expanded.png)
*Expanded list: active sessions showing per-row project name, state, source hook, and relative time.*

![Many sessions](docs/assets/overlay-expanded-many.png)
*Expanded list with many sessions: six session rows followed by the overflow line showing remaining sessions.*

![Auto-approve countdown](docs/assets/overlay-auto-approve.png)
*Auto-approve countdown: draining bar with "Allow (5s)" prompt allowing manual veto before automatic permission approval.*

![In context](docs/assets/desktop-scene.png)
*In context: the strip sits at the screen edge beside two terminals, so a blocked session is visible without switching windows. The panel is the real renderer output; the two terminals around it are drawn, since a real capture would contain somebody's project names.*

---

### Features

The table below outlines the core capabilities and exact runtime parameters of the application:

| Feature | What it actually does |
|---|---|
| State aggregation | Aggregates sessions across 7 states (`idle`, `thinking`, `working`, `tool_use`, `waiting_permission`, `error`, `closed`), showing the highest-priority state across all active sessions. |
| Compact and expanded panels | Compact panel occupies 56x156 logical pixels anchored to a screen edge; clicking expands to 200 px wide, displaying 1–6 rows before adding an overflow line. |
| Copy a project path | Click a session row (or the copy half of the compact strip) to put that conversation's working directory on the clipboard; a short pill over the row confirms it, and a failed copy says so instead of claiming success. Rows whose reporter sent no working directory keep their old meaning: clicking them collapses the panel. |
| Whole-panel gestures | Clicking anywhere that is not a session row or a control toggles compact and expanded; drag anywhere moves 1:1 with the cursor; the wheel zooms between 65% and 160%. |
| Edge retract | Slides mostly off-screen when docked at an edge leaving a thin sliver; hovering restores it, while waiting_permission or error states override retraction to remain visible. |
| Tray menu | Right-click tray menu toggles visibility, resets position and zoom, opens settings, switches language, toggles autostart, and configures auto-approve. |
| Settings window | Native four-tab window (General, Sound, Sessions, Look) where every change persists immediately to `config.json` without an OK button. |
| Synthesized alert tones | Generates 44.1 kHz 16-bit mono PCM WAV tones in memory across four sound schemes (`chime`, `bell`, `soft`, `pulse`), with separate gates for waiting, error, and finish. |
| Per-session alerts | Fires Windows tray notification balloons and audio alerts when a session starts waiting for you, fails, or finishes — one pure policy decides (see below), so a prompt you are already reading does not also pop a balloon. |
| Attentiveness | An alert depends on what the session is asking for and whether you are looking: approval / question / plan review are told apart from the reason reporters already send, keyboard-and-mouse idle time is read from the OS, and the window that owns the session is resolved with the same ranking jump-to-terminal uses. Unmeasurable facts alert rather than stay quiet. |
| Per-session mute and unread | Right-click a session row to mute or unmute that conversation; a suppressed alert still marks its row unread, cleared by jumping to it, by it running again, or by it disappearing. Muting never silences the auto-approve countdown, which is a safety control, not a notification. |
| Alert receipt | The last alert decision is written to `alerts.json` beside `config.json` - not in `runtime/`, where every `*.json` is a reporter snapshot and the scanner deletes what it cannot parse - and printed by `--json` under `alerts` and summarised by the tenth `--doctor` check, so "why was I not told" has an answer instead of folklore. |
| Auto-approve and denylist | Provides a 5-second veto window on permission prompts where a tap denies and silence approves; blocks commands matching the dangerous-command denylist. |
| Jump to terminal | Walks session process ancestry and matches window titles to bring the waiting terminal window or tab to the foreground. |
| Scriptable CLI | Outputs structured session state via `ai-terminal-pet --json` by reading disk snapshots, avoiding blocking on GUI processes. |
| Single instance | A named mutex makes a second launch activate the running overlay instead of starting another one. |
| Connection capacity | The pipe server accepts 32 concurrent connections with a 5 s read timeout, so IPC never blocks the UI thread. |
| Idle lifecycle | A session is dropped only after a 2-minute absence grace; with no session left, the process removes itself after 10 minutes. |

### How it works

```text
Host CLI (Claude Code / OpenCode / Antigravity)
       │
       ▼ (Fire-and-forget hooks)
reporters/*.js
       │
       ▼ (JSON line over Windows named pipe: \\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>)
AI-Terminal-Pet.exe (Go 1.23, single-instance mutex)
       │
       ├─► internal/pipeserver (32 connections, 5s timeout, OK/ERR response)
       ├─► internal/store (in-memory state, TTL, disk snapshots fallback)
       └─► internal/ui (Win32 layered window, GDI topmost canvas)
```

- **Per-user named pipe**: IPC flows through `\\.\pipe\ai-terminal-pet-v1-<8hex>`, where `<8hex>` is derived from the SHA-256 hash of the user home directory. The exact same pipe-name algorithm is implemented in Go and JavaScript, locked by a cross-language golden test.

- **JSON line protocol**: Sessions transmit one JSON line per message with a 1 MiB payload cap. The server replies with an exact `OK` or `ERR` acknowledgment, and reporters retry until a deadline without treating partial reads as success.

- **On-disk snapshots**: Snapshot files under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\runtime\` provide a fallback channel and serve as the authoritative on-disk record of active sessions.

- **OS observation over heartbeats**: Session existence is decided by operating system observation of the process table and window titles rather than reporter heartbeats. A session remains active as long as its terminal window exists, and removal requires the host to be unobservable for a continuous 2-minute grace period.

- **Disks beat heartbeats**: The disk snapshot is authoritative for session existence: a session that was on disk and is gone is over, while synthetic PIDs from hooks never participate in liveness probing.

- **Connection handling**: The server accommodates 32 concurrent connections with a 5s read timeout, keeping IPC processing off the UI thread.

- **GDI rendering**: A top-down 32bpp DIB section created with CreateDIBSection is painted through a memory DC and handed to the layered window with UpdateLayeredWindow.

### Install

There are three ways in. Pick the one that matches how you got here.

**A. DeepSeek Harness user — no Go toolchain, nothing to build**

```powershell
dsh plugin add dsh-ai-terminal-pet
```

The package carries a prebuilt overlay and this project's own `protocol.js`. On first load it copies them into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\` **only when they are missing**, so it never overwrites an install you maintain yourself. That is the whole setup: the panel appears on the next session. It is also on npm as [`dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-ai-terminal-pet) (1.2.15), and the release tarball, a tag-pinned git source and a bare repository URL all work (`dsh plugin add <path-or-git-url>`); the same bootstrap runs either way. It targets DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x (`engines.dsh` `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0`, Node 24.9+); a 0.1.x host is not covered, and such a host refuses the bundle instead of loading it untested.

**B. Everyone else — download a package, no Go toolchain**

Two packages are published for this release: a self-extracting `pet-setup.exe` and a portable zip. Both install the same 11 artifacts into the same directory; the zip additionally lets you look inside before running anything.

1. Download one of them from the [`pet-v1.0.7` release](https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/tag/pet-v1.0.7):
   - **`pet-setup.exe`** (14,307,840 B, 13.6 MiB): double-click it. It verifies its own payload against `SHA256SUMS.txt` **before** writing anything, then runs the installer inside itself. `pet-setup.exe --verify` re-checks the installed files at any time, `--uninstall` removes them, `--add-to-path` puts the commands on your PATH.
   - **`ai-terminal-pet-1.0.7-win-x64.zip`** (5,053,946 B, 17 files): unzip it anywhere and double-click `install.cmd`. Everything is inspectable first; `install.cmd -VerifyOnly`, `-Uninstall` and `-AddToPath` work as they do in the source tree.
2. Verify that the installation works:
   ```powershell
   & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
   ```

The zip and the setup exe carry the three binaries, `protocol.js`, the Harness bundle, the installer and a `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so the only thing on Windows is one download and one double-click. Neither needs Go, Node, or an installer framework. The release is **not code-signed yet**, so the first run shows SmartScreen's "unknown publisher" prompt:

![SmartScreen on an unsigned build](docs/assets/smartscreen-unsigned.png)
*What an unsigned build produces on a machine that has never seen it: click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. This image is a reconstruction of the documented dialog, not a capture - see [docs/assets/README.md](docs/assets/README.md).*

That prompt is a certificate the project does not have, not a problem with the file you downloaded — the per-file SHA256 values in `SHA256SUMS.txt` are the honest substitute until a certificate exists.

After installing, `--doctor` should look like this (paths shortened here, everything else is the program's own output):

![--doctor on a healthy install](docs/assets/doctor-green.png)
*Ten checks, and the one that matters when you see an empty panel is `instance` — if it says a live instance is listening, the overlay is healthy and the missing piece is the terminal's reporter, not the install.*

**C. Developers — build from source (Go 1.23+)**

```powershell
# 1. Build the overlay, the native statusline shim and the native hook
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe ./cmd/ai-terminal-pet
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-statusline.exe ./cmd/pet-statusline
go build -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags "-s -w" -o .\bin\pet-hook.exe ./cmd/pet-hook

# 2. Install (stops a running overlay, copies, re-hashes every artifact)
.\scripts\install.cmd

# 3. See it work
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json
```

Re-verify the installed artifacts at any time with per-file SHA256 checks:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -VerifyOnly
```

It prints `install: verified - 11 file(s) match the repository, 0 warning(s)` and exits 0 only when every deployed artifact matches (the 11 artifacts are the overlay, the statusline shim, the native hook `pet-hook.exe`, `protocol.js`, and the 7 files of the DeepSeek Harness bundle). The installer itself stops a running overlay first and waits for the process to release its file handles; a plain file copy over a live binary fails at random, which is what the retry loop and the SHA256 comparison after every copy are for.

`install.cmd` is the entry point rather than `install.ps1` because a stock Windows install runs PowerShell at `RemoteSigned`, and `RemoteSigned` refuses a local `.ps1` that still carries the "downloaded from the internet" zone marker — the exact shape of a file you unzip from a release. The wrapper starts one `powershell.exe` with `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`, changes no machine or user policy, forwards every argument and every exit code, and adds no install logic: `install.ps1` remains the only implementation, and `.\scripts\install.ps1 -VerifyOnly` works unchanged on a machine whose policy already allows it.

Put `ai-terminal-pet` on your PATH so you can type the bare command:

```powershell
.\scripts\install.cmd -AddToPath
```

It writes **only** `HKCU\Environment\Path` (never `HKLM`), backs the previous value up to `<install dir>\path-backup.txt` first, and does nothing if the directory is already listed. **Open a new terminal** for the change to take effect. `-Uninstall` also removes that PATH entry, so uninstalling does not leave a dead entry behind (the previous value is backed up again, this time into `%TEMP%`).
Without this step the installer does not touch your PATH at all, so keep using the full path `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\AI-Terminal-Pet\AI-Terminal-Pet.exe" --json`.

The installer lives under `scripts/` rather than at the repository root on purpose: market indexers fetch a root `install.ps1` by name and regex-scan it, and this script legitimately mentions the `HKCU` Run key and a `-Recurse -Force` cleanup. Moving it one level down takes those two false positives off the root without taking any behaviour off the script.

Run `ai-terminal-pet --doctor` at any point after installing to self-check the environment, install files, runtime state, pipe, autostart entry, and node availability. To remove the deployed artifacts, run `.\scripts\install.cmd -Uninstall`; it asks for a typed `yes` confirmation first, refuses unsafe target directories, and accepts `-Force` for unattended removal.

Installing a terminal hook is required for that terminal to report; see the next section to connect your tools.

### Connect your terminal

| Terminal | How to connect | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| OpenCode | Add `file:///C:/path/to/ai-terminal-pet/reporters/opencode.js` to `plugins` in `opencode.json` (OpenCode 2.x: the file is a plugin with an `id` and a `setup`) | Turn, tool and permission states, including the difference between "waiting for you" and "still working" |
| Claude Code | Add `& "%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\pet-hook.exe" --mode=claude` for `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Stop`, and `Notification` in `settings.json`. `node <repo>/reporters/claude-hook.js` still works and is the fallback when you cannot run the `.exe`. | Real-time status updates, tool execution tracking, and permission prompt alerts |
| Antigravity | Set `statusLine.command` to `pet-statusline.exe` and configure `pet-hook.exe --mode=antigravity` for agent and tool events (`antigravity-hook.js` is the fallback) | Fast statusline updates, agent state changes, and permission request forwarding |
| DeepSeek Harness | Install the Cordis bundle from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\bundles\ai-terminal-pet-bridge\` via the plugin manager (`install_bundle`) | turn/start to working, tool/call to tool_use, approval/asked to waiting_permission, tool/result with an error to error, turn/end to idle, process exit to closed |
| Anything else | Run `node reporters/generic.js` with `--source`, `--state`, and `--project` flags | Instant status reporting from any custom script or CLI tool |

Writing your own reporter for a tool that is not listed here needs no source reading: [docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md) specifies the wire protocol (fields, state semantics, pipe-name derivation, acknowledgment contract, and redaction rules) that a conforming reporter must implement.

The Harness side is a host-only Cordis bundle: it holds no pipe-name, state-set or snapshot logic of its own, it loads the protocol from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\protocol.js` and delegates everything to it.

The Harness side has a second, self-contained option since `dsh-ai-terminal-pet` `1.1.0`: a standalone DSH plugin package at [`packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet`](packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet), also shipped as a GitHub Release asset. The package is now **1.2.15** (tag `dsh-plugin-v1.2.15`, asset `dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.15.tgz`); 1.2.14 and everything before it stay published and immutable but are superseded. 1.2.15 changes no code: it is the DSH 0.2.x compatibility release, moving `engines.dsh` to `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0` and `engines.node` to `>=24.9.0` (the Node floor DSH 0.2.x itself requires) after installing the tarball into a real 0.2.0-rc.1 host and a real 0.2.2-rc.3 host. 1.2.9 through 1.2.15 carry overlay 1.0.3 through 1.0.7 (1.2.12 and 1.2.13 both carry 1.0.6; 1.2.14 and 1.2.15 both carry 1.0.7): 1.0.3 turned alerts into a decision with a written receipt (`alerts.json`, which `--json` and `--doctor` read back); 1.0.4 moved that receipt next to `config.json`, because the runtime scanner deletes any snapshot file in `runtime/` it cannot parse; 1.0.5 made a click on a session row copy its project path and answer with an on-panel receipt; 1.0.6 tracked down three phantom alerts (a vanished session no longer counts as a completion, one conversation is one row, and OpenCode 2.x events map to the states they mean); 1.0.7 rebuilt the settings window - four real type sizes instead of two, hints that wrap instead of being cut with an ellipsis, its own DPI, and a Look tab that finally switches. 1.2.7 shipped the 1.0.1 overlay, whose compact strip answers "which terminal is blocked, and for how long" without expanding the panel; 1.2.8 shipped 1.0.2, where the look itself became a setting - three named palettes, an optional per-terminal tint on each row's source name, and "start hidden". 1.2.5 is the first version that works on a machine that never ran the overlay: it declares `vendor/package.json` as CommonJS (without it, `require()` of the shipped protocol returned a namespace with no `sendStatus`, so a `DSH_PET_NO_BOOTSTRAP=1` install silently reported nothing), it reads the project path, lineage and start time from the session header instead of `process.cwd()` (the desktop Harness starts from the install directory, so every session was attributed to one wrong path), and its de-duplication signature now covers state, reason, tool, project, title and parent session instead of state alone. 1.2.4 was a wording fix (one market install read as if it covered every terminal, and it does not - the bundle mirrors **Harness** sessions out of the box, while OpenCode, Claude Code and Antigravity sessions appear only after each of those terminals gets its own reporter); 1.2.3 added the `dsh.marketplace` block a third-party storefront reads before offering a plugin to its desktop client, and 1.2.2 moved the installer from the repository root into `scripts/`, which edits Go comments, which changes the source digest `vendor/manifest.json` records. Release assets cannot be edited, so a wording or manifest fix costs a version - shipping different bytes under an unchanged version is exactly the drift this repository removes. The three install forms are verified end to end, and the 1.2.4 assets were installed again from three fresh directories after the release went out: the release tarball in **1.8 s**, the tag-pinned git source in **3.7 s**, and the repository URL in **6.5 s**, all rc=0, with the unpacked bytes matching `git show ff7f6de:` file for file (a bare `add dsh-ai-terminal-pet` still waits on the npm release described below):

```powershell
# from the release tarball: no git clone, no build step
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet/releases/download/dsh-plugin-v1.2.15/dsh-ai-terminal-pet-1.2.15.tgz

# from git, pinned to the release tag
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "git+https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet.git#dsh-plugin-v1.2.15&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet"

# from the repository URL: resolves through the root manifest shim
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet
```

The repository URL works because the repository root now carries a 68-line `package.json` shim that contains no code: it points `main` at the package, declares `dsh.bundle.patch` as `./packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet/cordis.patch.yml` and limits `files` to that subtree. Without it a host that reads the repository root sees no `dsh.bundle`, installs an empty package and warns `declares no dsh.bundle`. The shim is `private`, so it never occupies the npm name, its `version` tracks the package (`verify.mjs` asserts they are equal, so a bump cannot land in one manifest only), and it carries the same `dsh.catalog` block the package does.

The package ships no lifecycle hooks at all — `prepack` was removed in 1.1.0 — because pnpm runs them for a git dependency and fails an unpinned source with an `allowBuilds` error that never mentions AI Terminal Pet. `vendor/` is committed instead and only verified: `node scripts/vendor.mjs --check` re-hashes the two vendored files and checks `vendor/manifest.json` against them, writing nothing. One form still fails, for a different reason: `git+https://github.com/jjjjjjjjnnjnn/ai-terminal-pet.git&path:/packages/dsh-ai-terminal-pet` without a `#ref` — pnpm concatenates the fragments and asks `ls-remote` for a repository that does not exist, so it reports `repository ... not found`.

1.2.0 also makes the package self-describing: `dsh.catalog` declares a `category` (`tool`), a one-line summary in English and Chinese, and five `capabilities` — `windows-overlay`, `named-pipe`, `session-state`, `tray-icon`, `no-network`. Those capabilities are **self-declared and unenforced**; dsh does not sandbox plugins, so the block describes what the overlay already does rather than granting it permission to do so. `keywords` gained `dsh-plugin`, the tag auto-indexing marketplaces harvest. 1.2.3 adds `dsh.marketplace` next to `dsh.bundle` and `dsh.catalog`: `profiles: ["desktop", "headless", "web"]`, `requiresBuildApproval: false` and `manualSteps: false`. That field is read by third-party registries, not by DSH - the plugin mounts through `dsh.bundle` either way, and this bundle only subscribes to `session/event`, so no profile-specific service is involved: that makes two independent discovery paths — registry review (a reviewed entry merges into `main` and only then appears in the list) and topic/keyword harvesting (no application needed at all). Two marketplaces already harvest automatically: [LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop) rebuilds daily from npm metadata, and every entry in its published shard is pinned by tarball integrity, so a Git-only package cannot appear there until it reaches npm; [zasenjc/dsh-plugins-store](https://github.com/zasenjc/dsh-plugins-store) syncs every 30 minutes and lists any public repository carrying both the `dsh-plugin` and `deepseek-harness` topics.

Its payload carries a prebuilt overlay and this project's own `protocol.js`, copied into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AI-Terminal-Pet\` on first use **only when they are missing** — an existing install is never overwritten, and the overlay keeps running entirely on its own, so a machine that only wants the pet still needs nothing but `scripts/install.cmd`. Its entry in the [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) registry ([PR #13937](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/13937)) passed both upstream checks and was merged on 2026-11-10, so the upstream catalogue lists the entry (that file pins which tarball the entry installs and can only be changed by pull request against that repository, never by an edit here: [PR #14076](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14076) moved it to 1.2.2 and merged at 19:59:37Z, and [PR #14089](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14089) moved it to 1.2.3 and merged at 2026-11-10T21:10:15Z, so the next rebuild renders that asset while [PR #14243](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/14243), opened on 2026-11-11, carries 1.2.4 and adds the same "other terminals need their own reporter" sentence to both descriptions; [imsai-sh/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins PR #912](https://github.com/imsai-sh/awesome-deepseek-harness-plugins/pull/912) makes the same wording fix there, and that repository never auto-merges an edit to an existing entry, so it waits for a maintainer; #14063, which had targeted 1.2.1, was closed once 1.2.2 packed the corrected bytes); the rendered catalogue page returned 404 at 16:16Z and became reachable later the same day once the upstream site build finished (`42844452013`, started 15:27:09Z, concluded 16:39:27Z); the catalogue file that DSH's in-app Market actually loads (`plugins.json`; its `count` was 10119 before that build and 10,304 when re-read after the 1.2.3 release) contains this repository too, but its `install` command is rendered from that `tarball` field a

decision.reason: The repository is already represented by catalog id jjjjjjjjnnjnn-ai-terminal-pet; this additional manifest or newer fixed-source snapshot is not a separate repository-level catalog entry. Existing retained catalog snapshots are not re-certified or replaced by this duplicate decision.
