# dsh-plugin-lint [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint) [![CI](https://github.com/shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22-brightgreen)](package.json) [![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20dependencies-0-brightgreen)](package.json) **Conformance checks and a compatibility matrix for DeepSeek Harness plugins: what the code declares, what it publishes, and what the host does with it.** [Rules](#the-rules) · [Probe](#the-probe) · [Matrix](#the-compatibility-matrix) · [Panel](#the-panel) · [v0.3 analysis (experimental)](#v03-analysis-experimental) · [Federation](#federation) · [中文](#中文) ![The compatibility panel inside the DSH settings page](docs/assets/panel.png) *The panel, running in a throwaway web profile: what this profile has installed, and how each plugin fares across DSH versions.* --- ## Why this exists The ecosystem catalog used for the measurements below lists 4,508 entries (snapshot 2026-10-11). Upgrade breakage is a recurring problem, and the code that plugins publish is not checked against the documented practices. Measured on 2026-10-13 against the Top 100 published community plugins (static analysis of the published tarballs; no plugin code was executed): | Observation | Result | | --- | --- | | plugins that load at least one Harness Client package | **62 / 100 (62%)** | | plugins declaring `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` | **13 / 100 (13%)** | | plugins declaring no compatibility range | **87 / 100 (87%)** | | plugins declaring an `icon` | 31 / 100 (31%) | | plugins triggering at least one error-level rule | 1 / 100 (1%) | A coupling to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*` breaks when the host updates those packages without notice. A missing compatibility declaration means upgrade day is untested. A `files[]` gap passes local testing and only fails in the published tarball. The raw artifacts behind these numbers (`reports/`, `matrix/cells/`) are generated locally and gitignored; they are not part of a clean clone. See [docs/09](docs/09-ecosystem-measurements.md) for the aggregate record and the [data policy](#data-policy). ## What this is Four tools that answer four different questions about a DeepSeek Harness plugin. ```mermaid flowchart TB pkg["plugin package
on disk"] pkg --> lint["dsh-plugin-lint
static rules
is it written the way the reference says?"] pkg --> probe["probe-boot
one plugin, throwaway profile
does it mount, and what does the model get?"] probe --> matrix["matrix runner
plugin × DSH version × composition
which version breaks it?"] probe --> conflicts["conflicts
several plugins at once
do they collide?"] matrix --> panel["settings panel
your installed plugins
what about my setup?"] matrix --> index["aggregate index
ecosystem numbers"] classDef tool fill:#eef6ff,stroke:#4a7dbd,color:#123 class lint,probe,matrix,conflicts,panel tool ``` The linter and the static analysis commands need no build step, no config file and no network access. The probe and the matrix runner install packages from npm, so they need network access; the upgrade planner reads a local matrix and makes no network request. Every lint finding carries a file, a line, an evidence excerpt, and the upstream document the rule encodes. ## What this is not - **Not a security endorsement.** A clean run means no rule fired, nothing more. - **Not a replacement for the tools beside it.** Each answers a different question: | Tool | The question it answers | This project | | --- | --- | --- | | [dsh-plugin-doctor](https://github.com/zoahdev/dsh-plugin-doctor) | does the package structure and build hold up? | does not touch builds | | [dsh-testkit](https://github.com/iiwish/dsh-testkit) | does it install, run and uninstall on a real host? | only checks artifacts on disk | | [dsh-trust-check](https://github.com/liuwenji007/dsh-trust-check) | what can this plugin touch? | makes no security judgement | | [dsh-my-guardian](https://github.com/baosfeng/my-dsh-plugins) | what happens after it breaks? | does not recover anything | | **dsh-plugin-lint** | **is it written the way the reference says, will it survive publishing, and will it survive an upgrade?** | — | ```console $ node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . demo-plugin@1.0.0 13 checks E2 error client bundle factory id matches nothing the loader can ask for lib/client.js:2 factory id "other-name" is neither the package name "demo-plugin" nor a row name in the bundle patch. evidence: __ModuleLoader__.load({ id: "other-name" }) why: the browser module table keys the factory by the id it asks for and the loader throws when a bundle registers another one, leaving the client half unreachable. doc: dsh plugin-development / references/ui-plugin.md W1 warn couples the plugin to a Harness Client package lib/client.js:12 loads 1 Harness Client package from the browser module table: @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives. why: the reference advises copying the primitive instead — these packages change without notice and a throwing component blanks the slot. Official first-party bundles do the same, so treat this as a coupling risk to watch at upgrade time, not a defect. 1 error · 1 warn · 0 info ``` The header count is read from the rule set (`RULES.length`); it is 12 in this checkout. ## The rules Levels are assigned by **how reliably a rule can decide**, not by how bad the pattern sounds. A rule that cannot decide reliably does not get to be an error. Rule IDs are stable identifiers, not severity labels: `W3` reports at info level and `I3` at warn level. The tables below are grouped by level. **error** — mechanically decidable, never observed in the official packages | Rule | What it catches | | --- | --- | | E1 | `session.append("type", …)` with a type outside the Harness event catalog (380 types harvested from the official packages; 379 observed) | | E2 | client bundle factory id ≠ anything the loader can ask for (the registration silently never resolves) | | E3 | `main` / `exports["./client"]` / `dsh.bundle.patch` / `icon` points at a missing file | | E4 | `dsh.client` declared with no resolvable `./client` export | | E5 | `files[]` omits an artifact the manifest depends on — the "works locally, broken after publish" bug | | E6 | a `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer range does not accept the target runtime (`--dsh-version`); the host's real admission gate | | E7 | a published subpath export or bin target points at a missing file; icon format/size and stale `files` entries are warns | **warn** — documented risk patterns, evidence required | Rule | What it catches | | --- | --- | | W1 | loads a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*` package as a module (first-party packages exempt: they ship with the module table) | | W2 | subscribes to `session/event` and rescans the log inside the listener instead of folding through `ctx.sessionProjections` | | I3 | locale metadata exists but is not exported or published | **info** — review hints and metadata completeness | Rule | What it catches | | --- | --- | | I1 | no `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` (or it omits the running DSH version, with `--dsh-version`) | | I2 | no `icon`, or no `meta` title/description in `locale/.json` | | W3 | a timer that looks unowned (brace depth is approximate on bundled output, which is why this is a hint and not a warning) | Rules the first draft had, and why they are gone: "a waterfall listener must call `next()`" (real plugins reject deliberately, and re-enter `ctx.llm.stream()` on purpose), "never listen to `system-prompt/assemble`" (the official packages do, four times), "never subscribe to `session/event`" (the reference forbids *rescanning*, not subscribing). See [docs/06](docs/06-detailed-design.md). W1 encodes this passage from the reference, verbatim: > Do not `require('@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives')` or load any other Harness Client package as a module … copy markup, CSS, and behavior from the primitive into the plugin. > — `dsh plugin-development / references/practices.md` Measured on 2026-10-13: 62 of the Top 100 published plugins load at least one of these packages. The ui-primitives package is referenced by 48 distinct plugins; 71 of the 86 W1 findings mention it (one plugin can produce more than one finding). ### Measured with this tool | Run | Result | | --- | --- | | 80 official `@deepseek-ai/*` packages (zero-false-positive baseline) | **0 error · 0 warn** · 241 info | | Top 100 published community plugins | **1 error · 86 warn** · 240 info | | — of which couple to a Harness Client package | **62%** | | — of which declare no DSH compatibility range | **87%** | The official-package run predates the Top 100 run (both 2026-10-13); the two info totals are no longer equal (241 = 80 I1 + 160 I2 + 1 W3 on the official set; 240 = 87 I1 + 136 I2 + 17 W3 on the Top 100). The error rules fired on 1 of the 100 published plugins (E1: an append type outside the catalog). The daily value is the coupling inventory (W1) and declaration completeness (I1/I2), which nearly every plugin is missing something on. See [docs/07](docs/07-m1-results.md) and [docs/09](docs/09-ecosystem-measurements.md). ## The probe Static analysis reads code. The probe reads **behaviour**: it boots a real DSH in a throwaway home with one plugin installed and records what the host did with it. ```mermaid flowchart LR a["temporary
DSH_HOME"] --> b["materialize the
shipped profile"] b --> c["dsh plugin add <target>"] c --> d["boot with a stub
Anthropic-Messages provider"] d --> e["parse stderr:
mount warnings,
registered tools,
system prompt"] e --> f{"verdict"} f -->|"mounted"| g["active
+ what the model receives"] f -->|"waiting for a service
this composition lacks"| h["awaiting-service
not a failure"] f -->|"the host refused it"| i["rejected-by-host"] ``` Two details make it work, and both were learned the hard way: - **The success sentinel is a missing credential.** The throwaway home has no API key, so a plugin that mounted successfully ends in `MISSING_CREDENTIAL`. That is the signal. - **The exit code is never the signal.** A mount failure is a warning and the process still exits 0. ```bash node scripts/probe-boot.mjs dsh-mnemon --tools --dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 # active (3732 ms) # tools 24 -> 41 +17: mnemon_remember, mnemon_recall, mnemon_forget, ... # system prompt 2640 -> 7153 chars ``` That is example output from the 2026-10-13 run. The probe runs the target in a hardened Docker container (read-only root, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, non-root, network only during install) and refuses to run when Docker is unavailable. `--unsafe-host` is the explicit escape hatch: it runs the desktop DSH and the plugin in the current user's environment without isolation, and its results stay self-reported. The Docker backend needs an explicit `--dsh `; the desktop DSH can only be probed with `--unsafe-host`. Run the probe only on plugins you are willing to execute. See [docs/11](docs/11-m4-capability-probe.md). ## Usage The npm release is **0.4.0** (published 2026-11-13). The linter, the probe, and the analysis binaries ship in the package; commands that read the matrix snapshot or build reports still need a checkout. ```bash npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . # lint the package in the current directory npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint ./plugins/a ./plugins/b npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --json # machine-readable report npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --sarif # SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --dsh-version 0.2.0-rc.2 npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --exit-code # exit 1 when an error-level finding is present ``` Exit codes: `0` ok · `1` errors found with `--exit-code` · `2` the run failed. The 0.4.0 author workflow adds the CI-facing surface: ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --phase author # pre-build TypeScript tree: unbuilt outputs are hints, not errors node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --fail-on warn # gate on errors+warnings; --max-warnings N also works node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --format github # GitHub Actions annotations node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --format junit -o report.xml node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --format json-envelope # { schemaVersion, reports, baseline } node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --baseline .dsh-plugin-lint-baseline.json node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --write-baseline # record the current findings node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --init # write a workflow, baseline, and agent skill node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --dsh-version 0.2.2-rc.1 # E6 checks the host's peer admission node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --changed HEAD # only packages touched since HEAD (or --staged) node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --pack # lint the tarball npm pack would publish node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs dist/plugin-1.2.3.tgz # or lint an existing tarball node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --from-npm @scope/name@1.2.3 # lint a published artifact node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --profile ~/.dsh/profiles/default # host-truth scan of an installed profile node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --rules --explain E6 ``` `--changed` and `--staged` map a git diff back to the nearest `package.json`, so a monorepo lints only the packages a PR touches. `--pack`, `.tgz` and `--from-npm` force the publish phase and lint the real artifact: missing subpath exports, bins or icons are reported against what npm will actually ship, and tarballs containing path traversal or symlinks are rejected before extraction. `--profile` reads the runtime version and installed bundles from a DSH profile, reports which plugins the host will load or reject, and prints the exact `dsh plugin allow-version … --accept-risk` command for each rejection; with `--exit-code` it fails on any `will-reject`. The composite action is the same surface in CI: ```yaml jobs: lint: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: contents: read pull-requests: write # needed only when comment: true steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint@main # or the release tag once v0.4.0 is tagged with: path: . fail-on: error baseline: .dsh-plugin-lint-baseline.json comment: true # one sticky PR comment, created once and updated in place ``` Set `sarif: dsh-plugin-lint.sarif` to write SARIF, then upload it in a separate step (the job also needs `security-events: write`): ```yaml - uses: shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint@main with: path: . sarif: dsh-plugin-lint.sarif - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3 # use the current major from GitHub's docs with: sarif_file: dsh-plugin-lint.sarif ``` The package ships `schema/dsh-manifest.schema.json` (subpath `@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/schema/dsh-manifest.schema.json`). Point `$schema` at it so the editor validates the `dsh` block before CI runs: ```json { "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/main/schema/dsh-manifest.schema.json", "name": "@you/my-plugin", "version": "1.0.0", "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } } } ``` The baseline fingerprint is `sha256(rule + file + normalized evidence)` and deliberately excludes the line number, so reformatting or rebuilding does not revive a suppressed finding. Every report still prints how many findings the baseline suppressed. To run the checkout instead of the npm release, use `node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs `. Commands in this README that start with `node scripts/` also run from a **checkout** — the matrix runner, the probe, the upgrade preview, and the report builders read files the npm package does not ship. ## v0.3 analysis (experimental) The published release is 0.4.0. The four capabilities below ship behind the `./experimental` subpath and the `dsh-plugin-analyze` bin, and remain **experimental**: they are static heuristics over files on disk. None of them executes a plugin, measures runtime cost, or issues a security verdict. A clean run means no pattern matched. | Command | The question it answers | | --- | --- | | `dsh-plugin-analyze conflicts ` | do two or more plugins claim the same slot, tool name, route or config key? | | `dsh-plugin-analyze performance ` | how much does the package ship, and which static patterns look expensive? | | `dsh-plugin-analyze security ` | which patterns would a reviewer want to look at first? | | `dsh-plugin-analyze full ` | lint + performance + security for one package | | `dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan ...` | given a profile and a target DSH version, which plugins need action? | All four `analyze` subcommands accept `--json` (stdout is pure JSON; diagnostics go to stderr) and `--exit-code`. `--help` exits 0; an unknown option exits 2; a missing package directory exits 2. With `--exit-code`: `conflicts` exits 1 when any conflict is found, `security` exits 1 when a warning-level finding is present (info-level inventory entries do not gate), `full` exits 1 when lint reports an error or security reports a warning, and `performance` always exits 0 (a score is not a gate). Without the flag every successful run exits 0. ### Composition conflicts ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs conflicts ./plugin-a ./plugin-b ./plugin-c node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs conflicts ./plugin-a ./plugin-b --json ``` The static scan compares literals at registration sites: UI slot names (`ctx.slots.inject` / `ctx.slots.register`), tool names (`ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))` and declarative arrays), route paths (`connection.fetch.register`, older `ctx.router.*`), config keys, and waterfall listeners. A name claimed by two plugins is reported with the file, line and a resolution hint; two declarations by the same plugin are not reported as a conflict. Dynamic names are not resolved. The runtime authority is `scripts/matrix/conflicts.mjs`, which installs the plugins together and reads what the host registered — the static scan is a pre-flight hint, and a miss is not proof that two plugins compose. ### Performance analysis ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs performance ./my-plugin ``` Static counts, not measurements: shipped and JavaScript bytes, largest files, lines/functions/nesting depth (long functions are >100 lines), DOM access patterns, literal network call sites, and heavy dependency patterns. Comments are excluded because the analysis reads the masked source. The 0–100 score is a heuristic index assembled from fixed penalty thresholds; it is useful for comparing two packages or tracking a package over time, not as a runtime claim. A package with no JavaScript to analyse scores 0 with rating `insufficient-data` — the absence of evidence is not a clean bill. ### Security deep analysis ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs security ./my-plugin ``` Ten pattern rules (S1–S10) look for session data sent to external domains, credentials written to browser storage, `eval`/`Function`, non-static `innerHTML` in the client entry, literal external domains, shell commands built by interpolation, absolute-path file access, crypto use, `process.env` access, and insecure HTTP. Every rule reports at warn or info level: these patterns are not mechanically decidable, so none is an error. Rules read the masked source, so a URL or `eval` inside a comment is not a finding. S5 is an inventory of literal external domains — the report does not compare them against a declared capability, because the DSH manifest has no such field. `riskLevel` summarises the warning count (minimal · low · medium · high, no "critical") and is not a verdict; read the findings, not the label. ### Upgrade plan ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan.mjs --from 0.2.0-rc.2 --to 0.2.1-alpha.2 --installed ~/.dsh/profiles/default node bin/dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan.mjs --from 0.2.0-rc.2 --to 0.2.1-alpha.2 --installed --matrix matrix/cells --json node bin/dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan.mjs --check-compatibility ./my-plugin --target 0.2.1-alpha.2 ``` It reads the profile's installed bundles, joins them against the local matrix in `matrix/cells` (override with `--matrix `), and reports what changes on the target version. It makes no network request and does not query npm for newer versions: a recommended version is one the matrix observed active on the target DSH version. `--json` emits pure JSON in both modes. Exit codes for the analysis mode: `0` no action needed · `1` at least one plugin needs an update or has no compatible version · `2` the run failed, including when no matrix data is available. `--check-compatibility`: `0` compatible · `1` incompatible · `2` unknown or no data. The matrix is not shipped in the npm package and `matrix/cells/` is gitignored, so this command only works where a matrix snapshot exists. Its coverage is the 50 plugins in that snapshot, not the whole ecosystem. ### Programmatic API The analysis functions live behind the `./experimental` subpath (`@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/experimental`); the package entry point keeps only the ten stable core exports. In a checkout: ```javascript import { loadPackage } from './src/index.js'; import { detectConflicts, analyzePerformance, analyzeSecurityDeep } from './src/experimental/index.js'; const packages = ['./plugin-a', './plugin-b'].map((dir) => { const pkg = loadPackage(dir); return { name: pkg.manifest.name, manifest: pkg.manifest, jsFiles: pkg.jsFiles }; }); const conflicts = detectConflicts(packages); // { slots, toolNames, routes, configKeys, eventListeners, summary, experimental, limits } const perf = analyzePerformance(loadPackage('./plugin-a')); // { score, rating, recommendations, experimental, limits, … } const security = analyzeSecurityDeep(loadPackage('./plugin-a')); // { findings, summary, riskLevel, experimental, limits, … } ``` The 0.4.0 package publishes the `./experimental` subpath. See [docs/19](docs/19-analysis-tools.md) for field-level documentation and [docs/21](docs/21-release-0.4.0.md) for the 0.4.0 release notes. ## The compatibility matrix The probe also runs as a grid: one cell per plugin × DSH version × composition. ```bash node scripts/matrix/run.mjs --targets matrix/targets-top50.json --concurrency 4 node scripts/matrix/site.mjs ``` The current tracked snapshot was collected on **2026-10-16** (`generatedAt 2026-10-16T02:45:50Z`): **50 plugins × 2 DSH versions × 2 compositions = 200 cells**. The counts are in [`panel/data/aggregate.json`](panel/data/aggregate.json): | Status | 0.2.0-rc.2 | 0.2.1-alpha.2 | | --- | --- | --- | | active | 80 | 72 | | awaiting-service | 16 | 20 | | rejected-by-host | 2 | 8 | | install-failed | 2 | 0 | Each version column sums to 100 cells (50 plugins × headless/web). The snapshot covers only the two pinned DSH versions; newer releases are not tested. Three data-quality caveats apply to the matrix and to anything derived from it: - **Recorded version ≠ loaded version.** A cell records `plugin.version` from the registry at collection time, but the probe installs by bare package name. In **23 of the 200 cells** the recorded version differs from the version the cell notes was actually loaded (e.g. `dsh-context` records 0.72.0 while 0.71.0 was installed). The `reproduce` command in a cell does not pin a version, so rerunning it today can test a different release. - **The per-plugin data is not in the repository.** `matrix/cells/` and `matrix/index/` are gitignored. A clean clone contains the target list and the aggregate counts, not the cells; rebuilding them needs network access, npm and the probe. - **Older totals are not cited.** Earlier drafts reported a larger plugin run and a plugin-level count of verdicts that got worse. That run cannot be reconstructed from this repository, so it is not cited here; [docs/09](docs/09-ecosystem-measurements.md) records why. ### Upgrade preview The matrix answers "which version breaks this plugin"; the preview answers the question a user actually has: **should this profile upgrade?** It reads the profile's installed bundles, joins them against the matrix, and reports what changes on the target version: ```bash node scripts/upgrade-preview.mjs ~/.dsh/profiles/default ``` ```text Upgrade preview: 0.2.0-rc.2 -> 0.2.1-alpha.2 Profile ~/.dsh/profiles/default · 8 installed (6 community, 2 first-party) 2 worse · 0 better · 3 unchanged · 1 not covered by the matrix ✗ @michengai/dsh-archive-manager 0.2.0-rc.2: active -> 0.2.1-alpha.2: rejected-by-host ``` The output above is an illustrative sample. A plugin the matrix does not cover is reported as unknown, not as a verdict. First-party bundles are counted but not previewed — the matrix says nothing about them. ## Composition conflicts A plugin that mounts alone can still collide with another. `conflicts.mjs` scans two dimensions: the tool names recorded in the matrix cells (what the host registered), and the slot names each plugin's client bundle declares (what the code claims). A name claimed by two plugins in either dimension is a candidate, verified by installing the pair into **one** profile. Measured on 2026-10-13 over the sampled ecosystem (16 plugins): | Dimension | Collisions found | | --- | --- | | tool names (118 distinct) | **0** | | slot names (37 distinct) | **10** — `settings.section` alone is claimed by three plugins | The tool-name result is a clean bill; the slot result is not. Two fixtures claim the same tool name on purpose to show what a collision looks like: | Stage | Result | | --- | --- | | each alone | both `active`, +1 tool each | | **installed together** | **the later one never activates** | ```text tool-beta: Error: tool "collide_probe" is already registered (for a per-agent variant, register through that agent's `agent.ctx` instead) ``` It is not "the last one wins" — the later plugin is discarded whole. And because a failed mount is only a warning with exit code 0, a user can run two clashing plugins with one of them silently doing nothing. This measurement is historical: it depends on matrix cells that are gitignored, and the installed-pair verification is a manual step, not part of the CLI. See [docs/18](docs/18-composition-conflicts.md). ## The panel [`panel/`](panel/) is a real DSH plugin: a settings section — titled **Plugin Health Center** — listing what this profile has installed, how each plugin fares across DSH versions, and, below the table, aggregate ecosystem counts per version (never a package name). The screenshot at the top of this file was captured by [`scripts/screenshot-panel.mjs`](scripts/screenshot-panel.mjs) in a throwaway web profile. The panel reads two data files: the full matrix snapshot when one exists locally (`data/matrix-index.json`, overridable with `DSH_PLUGIN_LINT_INDEX`), and the aggregate that ships in the npm package (`data/aggregate.json`, counts only). **An npm-installed panel therefore shows the ecosystem counts and marks installed plugins as uncovered; per-plugin rows need a local matrix snapshot.** The npm release is panel 0.2.0 (published 2026-11-13), which includes the server-side action guards described in [docs/16](docs/16-m5-panel.md). Older 0.1.x releases predate those guards and hardcode `--profile desktop`; do not install one into a profile that runs untrusted plugins. With no per-plugin data, the page still shows the matrix overview: 50 plugins across 2 DSH versions, with 80 of 100 cells active on 0.2.0-rc.2 and 72 of 100 on 0.2.1-alpha.2. ```bash node scripts/matrix/bundle-panel-data.mjs # snapshot the local matrix into the package dsh plugin --profile add # from a checkout ``` It mounts on both pinned DSH versions in both compositions, and it passes this project's own linter with zero findings — only `react` comes from the browser module table, no Harness Client package is imported, and colours use `--dsw-alias-*` tokens with fallbacks. Visual verification caught two bugs a code review had not: the page said "Running DSH unknown" because `import.meta.resolve` cannot see the harness from inside a profile, and it called first-party bundles "not installed" although the dsh installation provides them. Both are fixed, and [docs/16](docs/16-m5-panel.md) records what was checked. ## Federation Plugin authors can run the same probe from their own CI — [docs/15](docs/15-federation.md). The composite action in `.github/actions/probe/` is **not usable yet** (its `github.action_path` points at the action directory, which does not contain the scripts it calls), so today the working path is a checkout plus: ```bash node scripts/probe-boot.mjs --tools --dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 --mode both ``` Self-reported cells are never presented as ours: they are sampled, re-run, and either promoted to `verified` or marked `disputed` with both verdicts kept. A disagreement is never hidden — that is the property the rest of the matrix depends on. | Trust level | Source | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `verified` ✅ | our runs, or a sampled re-run that matched | we stand behind "this is what we observed" | | `self-reported` 🟡 | author's CI, not yet re-run | represents only what the author reported | | `disputed` ⚠️ | re-run disagreed | both verdicts stay in the file; the diff

# dsh-plugin-lint [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint) [![CI](https://github.com/shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22-brightgreen)](package.json) [![Dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20dependencies-0-brightgreen)](package.json) **Conformance checks and a compatibility matrix for DeepSeek Harness plugins: what the code declares, what it publishes, and what the host does with it.** [Rules](#the-rules) · [Probe](#the-probe) · [Matrix](#the-compatibility-matrix) · [Panel](#the-panel) · [v0.3 analysis (experimental)](#v03-analysis-experimental) · [Federation](#federation) · [中文](#中文) ![The compatibility panel inside the DSH settings page](docs/assets/panel.png) *The panel, running in a throwaway web profile: what this profile has installed, and how each plugin fares across DSH versions.* --- ## Why this exists The ecosystem catalog used for the measurements below lists 4,508 entries (snapshot 2026-10-11). Upgrade breakage is a recurring problem, and the code that plugins publish is not checked against the documented practices. Measured on 2026-10-13 against the Top 100 published community plugins (static analysis of the published tarballs; no plugin code was executed): | Observation | Result | | --- | --- | | plugins that load at least one Harness Client package | **62 / 100 (62%)** | | plugins declaring `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` | **13 / 100 (13%)** | | plugins declaring no compatibility range | **87 / 100 (87%)** | | plugins declaring an `icon` | 31 / 100 (31%) | | plugins triggering at least one error-level rule | 1 / 100 (1%) | A coupling to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*` breaks when the host updates those packages without notice. A missing compatibility declaration means upgrade day is untested. A `files[]` gap passes local testing and only fails in the published tarball. The raw artifacts behind these numbers (`reports/`, `matrix/cells/`) are generated locally and gitignored; they are not part of a clean clone. See [docs/09](docs/09-ecosystem-measurements.md) for the aggregate record and the [data policy](#data-policy). ## What this is Four tools that answer four different questions about a DeepSeek Harness plugin. ```mermaid flowchart TB pkg["plugin package
on disk"] pkg --> lint["dsh-plugin-lint
static rules
is it written the way the reference says?"] pkg --> probe["probe-boot
one plugin, throwaway profile
does it mount, and what does the model get?"] probe --> matrix["matrix runner
plugin × DSH version × composition
which version breaks it?"] probe --> conflicts["conflicts
several plugins at once
do they collide?"] matrix --> panel["settings panel
your installed plugins
what about my setup?"] matrix --> index["aggregate index
ecosystem numbers"] classDef tool fill:#eef6ff,stroke:#4a7dbd,color:#123 class lint,probe,matrix,conflicts,panel tool ``` The linter and the static analysis commands need no build step, no config file and no network access. The probe and the matrix runner install packages from npm, so they need network access; the upgrade planner reads a local matrix and makes no network request. Every lint finding carries a file, a line, an evidence excerpt, and the upstream document the rule encodes. ## What this is not - **Not a security endorsement.** A clean run means no rule fired, nothing more. - **Not a replacement for the tools beside it.** Each answers a different question: | Tool | The question it answers | This project | | --- | --- | --- | | [dsh-plugin-doctor](https://github.com/zoahdev/dsh-plugin-doctor) | does the package structure and build hold up? | does not touch builds | | [dsh-testkit](https://github.com/iiwish/dsh-testkit) | does it install, run and uninstall on a real host? | only checks artifacts on disk | | [dsh-trust-check](https://github.com/liuwenji007/dsh-trust-check) | what can this plugin touch? | makes no security judgement | | [dsh-my-guardian](https://github.com/baosfeng/my-dsh-plugins) | what happens after it breaks? | does not recover anything | | **dsh-plugin-lint** | **is it written the way the reference says, will it survive publishing, and will it survive an upgrade?** | — | ```console $ node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . demo-plugin@1.0.0 13 checks E2 error client bundle factory id matches nothing the loader can ask for lib/client.js:2 factory id "other-name" is neither the package name "demo-plugin" nor a row name in the bundle patch. evidence: __ModuleLoader__.load({ id: "other-name" }) why: the browser module table keys the factory by the id it asks for and the loader throws when a bundle registers another one, leaving the client half unreachable. doc: dsh plugin-development / references/ui-plugin.md W1 warn couples the plugin to a Harness Client package lib/client.js:12 loads 1 Harness Client package from the browser module table: @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives. why: the reference advises copying the primitive instead — these packages change without notice and a throwing component blanks the slot. Official first-party bundles do the same, so treat this as a coupling risk to watch at upgrade time, not a defect. 1 error · 1 warn · 0 info ``` The header count is read from the rule set (`RULES.length`); it is 12 in this checkout. ## The rules Levels are assigned by **how reliably a rule can decide**, not by how bad the pattern sounds. A rule that cannot decide reliably does not get to be an error. Rule IDs are stable identifiers, not severity labels: `W3` reports at info level and `I3` at warn level. The tables below are grouped by level. **error** — mechanically decidable, never observed in the official packages | Rule | What it catches | | --- | --- | | E1 | `session.append("type", …)` with a type outside the Harness event catalog (380 types harvested from the official packages; 379 observed) | | E2 | client bundle factory id ≠ anything the loader can ask for (the registration silently never resolves) | | E3 | `main` / `exports["./client"]` / `dsh.bundle.patch` / `icon` points at a missing file | | E4 | `dsh.client` declared with no resolvable `./client` export | | E5 | `files[]` omits an artifact the manifest depends on — the "works locally, broken after publish" bug | | E6 | a `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` peer range does not accept the target runtime (`--dsh-version`); the host's real admission gate | | E7 | a published subpath export or bin target points at a missing file; icon format/size and stale `files` entries are warns | **warn** — documented risk patterns, evidence required | Rule | What it catches | | --- | --- | | W1 | loads a `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*` package as a module (first-party packages exempt: they ship with the module table) | | W2 | subscribes to `session/event` and rescans the log inside the listener instead of folding through `ctx.sessionProjections` | | I3 | locale metadata exists but is not exported or published | **info** — review hints and metadata completeness | Rule | What it catches | | --- | --- | | I1 | no `dsh.compatibility.dshReleases` (or it omits the running DSH version, with `--dsh-version`) | | I2 | no `icon`, or no `meta` title/description in `locale/.json` | | W3 | a timer that looks unowned (brace depth is approximate on bundled output, which is why this is a hint and not a warning) | Rules the first draft had, and why they are gone: "a waterfall listener must call `next()`" (real plugins reject deliberately, and re-enter `ctx.llm.stream()` on purpose), "never listen to `system-prompt/assemble`" (the official packages do, four times), "never subscribe to `session/event`" (the reference forbids *rescanning*, not subscribing). See [docs/06](docs/06-detailed-design.md). W1 encodes this passage from the reference, verbatim: > Do not `require('@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives')` or load any other Harness Client package as a module … copy markup, CSS, and behavior from the primitive into the plugin. > — `dsh plugin-development / references/practices.md` Measured on 2026-10-13: 62 of the Top 100 published plugins load at least one of these packages. The ui-primitives package is referenced by 48 distinct plugins; 71 of the 86 W1 findings mention it (one plugin can produce more than one finding). ### Measured with this tool | Run | Result | | --- | --- | | 80 official `@deepseek-ai/*` packages (zero-false-positive baseline) | **0 error · 0 warn** · 241 info | | Top 100 published community plugins | **1 error · 86 warn** · 240 info | | — of which couple to a Harness Client package | **62%** | | — of which declare no DSH compatibility range | **87%** | The official-package run predates the Top 100 run (both 2026-10-13); the two info totals are no longer equal (241 = 80 I1 + 160 I2 + 1 W3 on the official set; 240 = 87 I1 + 136 I2 + 17 W3 on the Top 100). The error rules fired on 1 of the 100 published plugins (E1: an append type outside the catalog). The daily value is the coupling inventory (W1) and declaration completeness (I1/I2), which nearly every plugin is missing something on. See [docs/07](docs/07-m1-results.md) and [docs/09](docs/09-ecosystem-measurements.md). ## The probe Static analysis reads code. The probe reads **behaviour**: it boots a real DSH in a throwaway home with one plugin installed and records what the host did with it. ```mermaid flowchart LR a["temporary
DSH_HOME"] --> b["materialize the
shipped profile"] b --> c["dsh plugin add <target>"] c --> d["boot with a stub
Anthropic-Messages provider"] d --> e["parse stderr:
mount warnings,
registered tools,
system prompt"] e --> f{"verdict"} f -->|"mounted"| g["active
+ what the model receives"] f -->|"waiting for a service
this composition lacks"| h["awaiting-service
not a failure"] f -->|"the host refused it"| i["rejected-by-host"] ``` Two details make it work, and both were learned the hard way: - **The success sentinel is a missing credential.** The throwaway home has no API key, so a plugin that mounted successfully ends in `MISSING_CREDENTIAL`. That is the signal. - **The exit code is never the signal.** A mount failure is a warning and the process still exits 0. ```bash node scripts/probe-boot.mjs dsh-mnemon --tools --dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 # active (3732 ms) # tools 24 -> 41 +17: mnemon_remember, mnemon_recall, mnemon_forget, ... # system prompt 2640 -> 7153 chars ``` That is example output from the 2026-10-13 run. The probe runs the target in a hardened Docker container (read-only root, no capabilities, no-new-privileges, non-root, network only during install) and refuses to run when Docker is unavailable. `--unsafe-host` is the explicit escape hatch: it runs the desktop DSH and the plugin in the current user's environment without isolation, and its results stay self-reported. The Docker backend needs an explicit `--dsh `; the desktop DSH can only be probed with `--unsafe-host`. Run the probe only on plugins you are willing to execute. See [docs/11](docs/11-m4-capability-probe.md). ## Usage The npm release is **0.4.0** (published 2026-11-13). The linter, the probe, and the analysis binaries ship in the package; commands that read the matrix snapshot or build reports still need a checkout. ```bash npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . # lint the package in the current directory npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint ./plugins/a ./plugins/b npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --json # machine-readable report npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --sarif # SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --dsh-version 0.2.0-rc.2 npx @shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint . --exit-code # exit 1 when an error-level finding is present ``` Exit codes: `0` ok · `1` errors found with `--exit-code` · `2` the run failed. The 0.4.0 author workflow adds the CI-facing surface: ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --phase author # pre-build TypeScript tree: unbuilt outputs are hints, not errors node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --fail-on warn # gate on errors+warnings; --max-warnings N also works node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --format github # GitHub Actions annotations node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --format junit -o report.xml node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --format json-envelope # { schemaVersion, reports, baseline } node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --baseline .dsh-plugin-lint-baseline.json node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --write-baseline # record the current findings node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --init # write a workflow, baseline, and agent skill node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --dsh-version 0.2.2-rc.1 # E6 checks the host's peer admission node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --changed HEAD # only packages touched since HEAD (or --staged) node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs . --pack # lint the tarball npm pack would publish node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs dist/plugin-1.2.3.tgz # or lint an existing tarball node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --from-npm @scope/name@1.2.3 # lint a published artifact node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --profile ~/.dsh/profiles/default # host-truth scan of an installed profile node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs --rules --explain E6 ``` `--changed` and `--staged` map a git diff back to the nearest `package.json`, so a monorepo lints only the packages a PR touches. `--pack`, `.tgz` and `--from-npm` force the publish phase and lint the real artifact: missing subpath exports, bins or icons are reported against what npm will actually ship, and tarballs containing path traversal or symlinks are rejected before extraction. `--profile` reads the runtime version and installed bundles from a DSH profile, reports which plugins the host will load or reject, and prints the exact `dsh plugin allow-version … --accept-risk` command for each rejection; with `--exit-code` it fails on any `will-reject`. The composite action is the same surface in CI: ```yaml jobs: lint: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: contents: read pull-requests: write # needed only when comment: true steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint@main # or the release tag once v0.4.0 is tagged with: path: . fail-on: error baseline: .dsh-plugin-lint-baseline.json comment: true # one sticky PR comment, created once and updated in place ``` Set `sarif: dsh-plugin-lint.sarif` to write SARIF, then upload it in a separate step (the job also needs `security-events: write`): ```yaml - uses: shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint@main with: path: . sarif: dsh-plugin-lint.sarif - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3 # use the current major from GitHub's docs with: sarif_file: dsh-plugin-lint.sarif ``` The package ships `schema/dsh-manifest.schema.json` (subpath `@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/schema/dsh-manifest.schema.json`). Point `$schema` at it so the editor validates the `dsh` block before CI runs: ```json { "$schema": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/main/schema/dsh-manifest.schema.json", "name": "@you/my-plugin", "version": "1.0.0", "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" } } } ``` The baseline fingerprint is `sha256(rule + file + normalized evidence)` and deliberately excludes the line number, so reformatting or rebuilding does not revive a suppressed finding. Every report still prints how many findings the baseline suppressed. To run the checkout instead of the npm release, use `node bin/dsh-plugin-lint.mjs `. Commands in this README that start with `node scripts/` also run from a **checkout** — the matrix runner, the probe, the upgrade preview, and the report builders read files the npm package does not ship. ## v0.3 analysis (experimental) The published release is 0.4.0. The four capabilities below ship behind the `./experimental` subpath and the `dsh-plugin-analyze` bin, and remain **experimental**: they are static heuristics over files on disk. None of them executes a plugin, measures runtime cost, or issues a security verdict. A clean run means no pattern matched. | Command | The question it answers | | --- | --- | | `dsh-plugin-analyze conflicts ` | do two or more plugins claim the same slot, tool name, route or config key? | | `dsh-plugin-analyze performance ` | how much does the package ship, and which static patterns look expensive? | | `dsh-plugin-analyze security ` | which patterns would a reviewer want to look at first? | | `dsh-plugin-analyze full ` | lint + performance + security for one package | | `dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan ...` | given a profile and a target DSH version, which plugins need action? | All four `analyze` subcommands accept `--json` (stdout is pure JSON; diagnostics go to stderr) and `--exit-code`. `--help` exits 0; an unknown option exits 2; a missing package directory exits 2. With `--exit-code`: `conflicts` exits 1 when any conflict is found, `security` exits 1 when a warning-level finding is present (info-level inventory entries do not gate), `full` exits 1 when lint reports an error or security reports a warning, and `performance` always exits 0 (a score is not a gate). Without the flag every successful run exits 0. ### Composition conflicts ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs conflicts ./plugin-a ./plugin-b ./plugin-c node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs conflicts ./plugin-a ./plugin-b --json ``` The static scan compares literals at registration sites: UI slot names (`ctx.slots.inject` / `ctx.slots.register`), tool names (`ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))` and declarative arrays), route paths (`connection.fetch.register`, older `ctx.router.*`), config keys, and waterfall listeners. A name claimed by two plugins is reported with the file, line and a resolution hint; two declarations by the same plugin are not reported as a conflict. Dynamic names are not resolved. The runtime authority is `scripts/matrix/conflicts.mjs`, which installs the plugins together and reads what the host registered — the static scan is a pre-flight hint, and a miss is not proof that two plugins compose. ### Performance analysis ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs performance ./my-plugin ``` Static counts, not measurements: shipped and JavaScript bytes, largest files, lines/functions/nesting depth (long functions are >100 lines), DOM access patterns, literal network call sites, and heavy dependency patterns. Comments are excluded because the analysis reads the masked source. The 0–100 score is a heuristic index assembled from fixed penalty thresholds; it is useful for comparing two packages or tracking a package over time, not as a runtime claim. A package with no JavaScript to analyse scores 0 with rating `insufficient-data` — the absence of evidence is not a clean bill. ### Security deep analysis ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-analyze.mjs security ./my-plugin ``` Ten pattern rules (S1–S10) look for session data sent to external domains, credentials written to browser storage, `eval`/`Function`, non-static `innerHTML` in the client entry, literal external domains, shell commands built by interpolation, absolute-path file access, crypto use, `process.env` access, and insecure HTTP. Every rule reports at warn or info level: these patterns are not mechanically decidable, so none is an error. Rules read the masked source, so a URL or `eval` inside a comment is not a finding. S5 is an inventory of literal external domains — the report does not compare them against a declared capability, because the DSH manifest has no such field. `riskLevel` summarises the warning count (minimal · low · medium · high, no "critical") and is not a verdict; read the findings, not the label. ### Upgrade plan ```bash node bin/dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan.mjs --from 0.2.0-rc.2 --to 0.2.1-alpha.2 --installed ~/.dsh/profiles/default node bin/dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan.mjs --from 0.2.0-rc.2 --to 0.2.1-alpha.2 --installed --matrix matrix/cells --json node bin/dsh-plugin-upgrade-plan.mjs --check-compatibility ./my-plugin --target 0.2.1-alpha.2 ``` It reads the profile's installed bundles, joins them against the local matrix in `matrix/cells` (override with `--matrix `), and reports what changes on the target version. It makes no network request and does not query npm for newer versions: a recommended version is one the matrix observed active on the target DSH version. `--json` emits pure JSON in both modes. Exit codes for the analysis mode: `0` no action needed · `1` at least one plugin needs an update or has no compatible version · `2` the run failed, including when no matrix data is available. `--check-compatibility`: `0` compatible · `1` incompatible · `2` unknown or no data. The matrix is not shipped in the npm package and `matrix/cells/` is gitignored, so this command only works where a matrix snapshot exists. Its coverage is the 50 plugins in that snapshot, not the whole ecosystem. ### Programmatic API The analysis functions live behind the `./experimental` subpath (`@shidesheng0218/dsh-plugin-lint/experimental`); the package entry point keeps only the ten stable core exports. In a checkout: ```javascript import { loadPackage } from './src/index.js'; import { detectConflicts, analyzePerformance, analyzeSecurityDeep } from './src/experimental/index.js'; const packages = ['./plugin-a', './plugin-b'].map((dir) => { const pkg = loadPackage(dir); return { name: pkg.manifest.name, manifest: pkg.manifest, jsFiles: pkg.jsFiles }; }); const conflicts = detectConflicts(packages); // { slots, toolNames, routes, configKeys, eventListeners, summary, experimental, limits } const perf = analyzePerformance(loadPackage('./plugin-a')); // { score, rating, recommendations, experimental, limits, … } const security = analyzeSecurityDeep(loadPackage('./plugin-a')); // { findings, summary, riskLevel, experimental, limits, … } ``` The 0.4.0 package publishes the `./experimental` subpath. See [docs/19](docs/19-analysis-tools.md) for field-level documentation and [docs/21](docs/21-release-0.4.0.md) for the 0.4.0 release notes. ## The compatibility matrix The probe also runs as a grid: one cell per plugin × DSH version × composition. ```bash node scripts/matrix/run.mjs --targets matrix/targets-top50.json --concurrency 4 node scripts/matrix/site.mjs ``` The current tracked snapshot was collected on **2026-10-16** (`generatedAt 2026-10-16T02:45:50Z`): **50 plugins × 2 DSH versions × 2 compositions = 200 cells**. The counts are in [`panel/data/aggregate.json`](panel/data/aggregate.json): | Status | 0.2.0-rc.2 | 0.2.1-alpha.2 | | --- | --- | --- | | active | 80 | 72 | | awaiting-service | 16 | 20 | | rejected-by-host | 2 | 8 | | install-failed | 2 | 0 | Each version column sums to 100 cells (50 plugins × headless/web). The snapshot covers only the two pinned DSH versions; newer releases are not tested. Three data-quality caveats apply to the matrix and to anything derived from it: - **Recorded version ≠ loaded version.** A cell records `plugin.version` from the registry at collection time, but the probe installs by bare package name. In **23 of the 200 cells** the recorded version differs from the version the cell notes was actually loaded (e.g. `dsh-context` records 0.72.0 while 0.71.0 was installed). The `reproduce` command in a cell does not pin a version, so rerunning it today can test a different release. - **The per-plugin data is not in the repository.** `matrix/cells/` and `matrix/index/` are gitignored. A clean clone contains the target list and the aggregate counts, not the cells; rebuilding them needs network access, npm and the probe. - **Older totals are not cited.** Earlier drafts reported a larger plugin run and a plugin-level count of verdicts that got worse. That run cannot be reconstructed from this repository, so it is not cited here; [docs/09](docs/09-ecosystem-measurements.md) records why. ### Upgrade preview The matrix answers "which version breaks this plugin"; the preview answers the question a user actually has: **should this profile upgrade?** It reads the profile's installed bundles, joins them against the matrix, and reports what changes on the target version: ```bash node scripts/upgrade-preview.mjs ~/.dsh/profiles/default ``` ```text Upgrade preview: 0.2.0-rc.2 -> 0.2.1-alpha.2 Profile ~/.dsh/profiles/default · 8 installed (6 community, 2 first-party) 2 worse · 0 better · 3 unchanged · 1 not covered by the matrix ✗ @michengai/dsh-archive-manager 0.2.0-rc.2: active -> 0.2.1-alpha.2: rejected-by-host ``` The output above is an illustrative sample. A plugin the matrix does not cover is reported as unknown, not as a verdict. First-party bundles are counted but not previewed — the matrix says nothing about them. ## Composition conflicts A plugin that mounts alone can still collide with another. `conflicts.mjs` scans two dimensions: the tool names recorded in the matrix cells (what the host registered), and the slot names each plugin's client bundle declares (what the code claims). A name claimed by two plugins in either dimension is a candidate, verified by installing the pair into **one** profile. Measured on 2026-10-13 over the sampled ecosystem (16 plugins): | Dimension | Collisions found | | --- | --- | | tool names (118 distinct) | **0** | | slot names (37 distinct) | **10** — `settings.section` alone is claimed by three plugins | The tool-name result is a clean bill; the slot result is not. Two fixtures claim the same tool name on purpose to show what a collision looks like: | Stage | Result | | --- | --- | | each alone | both `active`, +1 tool each | | **installed together** | **the later one never activates** | ```text tool-beta: Error: tool "collide_probe" is already registered (for a per-agent variant, register through that agent's `agent.ctx` instead) ``` It is not "the last one wins" — the later plugin is discarded whole. And because a failed mount is only a warning with exit code 0, a user can run two clashing plugins with one of them silently doing nothing. This measurement is historical: it depends on matrix cells that are gitignored, and the installed-pair verification is a manual step, not part of the CLI. See [docs/18](docs/18-composition-conflicts.md). ## The panel [`panel/`](panel/) is a real DSH plugin: a settings section — titled **Plugin Health Center** — listing what this profile has installed, how each plugin fares across DSH versions, and, below the table, aggregate ecosystem counts per version (never a package name). The screenshot at the top of this file was captured by [`scripts/screenshot-panel.mjs`](scripts/screenshot-panel.mjs) in a throwaway web profile. The panel reads two data files: the full matrix snapshot when one exists locally (`data/matrix-index.json`, overridable with `DSH_PLUGIN_LINT_INDEX`), and the aggregate that ships in the npm package (`data/aggregate.json`, counts only). **An npm-installed panel therefore shows the ecosystem counts and marks installed plugins as uncovered; per-plugin rows need a local matrix snapshot.** The npm release is panel 0.2.0 (published 2026-11-13), which includes the server-side action guards described in [docs/16](docs/16-m5-panel.md). Older 0.1.x releases predate those guards and hardcode `--profile desktop`; do not install one into a profile that runs untrusted plugins. With no per-plugin data, the page still shows the matrix overview: 50 plugins across 2 DSH versions, with 80 of 100 cells active on 0.2.0-rc.2 and 72 of 100 on 0.2.1-alpha.2. ```bash node scripts/matrix/bundle-panel-data.mjs # snapshot the local matrix into the package dsh plugin --profile add # from a checkout ``` It mounts on both pinned DSH versions in both compositions, and it passes this project's own linter with zero findings — only `react` comes from the browser module table, no Harness Client package is imported, and colours use `--dsw-alias-*` tokens with fallbacks. Visual verification caught two bugs a code review had not: the page said "Running DSH unknown" because `import.meta.resolve` cannot see the harness from inside a profile, and it called first-party bundles "not installed" although the dsh installation provides them. Both are fixed, and [docs/16](docs/16-m5-panel.md) records what was checked. ## Federation Plugin authors can run the same probe from their own CI — [docs/15](docs/15-federation.md). The composite action in `.github/actions/probe/` is **not usable yet** (its `github.action_path` points at the action directory, which does not contain the scripts it calls), so today the working path is a checkout plus: ```bash node scripts/probe-boot.mjs --tools --dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 --mode both ``` Self-reported cells are never presented as ours: they are sampled, re-run, and either promoted to `verified` or marked `disputed` with both verdicts kept. A disagreement is never hidden — that is the property the rest of the matrix depends on. | Trust level | Source | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `verified` ✅ | our runs, or a sampled re-run that matched | we stand behind "this is what we observed" | | `self-reported` 🟡 | author's CI, not yet re-run | represents only what the author reported | | `disputed` ⚠️ | re-run disagreed | both verdicts stay in the file; the diff
